For example:</p> <pre><code>- source: project quarto-pub: - id: "5f3abafe-68f9-4c1d-835b-9d668b892001" url: "[njones.quarto.pub](https://njones.quarto.pub/blog)"</code></pre> <p>You can also manually create a <code>_publish.yml</code> file that looks like the example above, but with the appropriate <code>id</code> and <code>url</code> values for your site.</p> <p>Do not proceed to the next step(s) until you have a <code>_publish.yml</code> that indicates your publishing destination.</p> <h6 id="freezing-computations-4">Freezing Computations</h6> <p>To make sure that R, Python, and Julia code is only executed locally, configure your project to use Quarto’s freeze feature by adding this to your <code>_quarto.yml</code>:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml execute: freeze: auto</code></pre> <p>Now, fully re-render your site:</p> <pre><code>Terminal quarto render</code></pre> <p>If you have executable code in your project you’ll notice that a <code>_freeze</code> directory has been created at the top level of your project. This directory stores the results of computations and should be checked in to version control. Whenever you change a <code>.qmd</code> file with executable code, it will automatically be re-run during your next render and the updated computations will be stored in <code>_freeze</code>.</p> <p>Note that an alternative approach is to execute the code as part of the GitHub Action. For now we’ll keep things simpler by executing code locally and storing the computations by using freeze. Then, further below, we’ll cover Executing Code within a GitHub Action.</p> <h6 id="publish-action-3">Publish Action</h6> <p>Add a <code>publish.yml</code> GitHub Action to your project by creating this YAML file and saving it to <code>.github/workflows/publish.yml</code>:</p> <pre><code>.github/workflows/publish.yml on: workflow_dispatch: push: branches: main name: Quarto Publish jobs: build-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Check out repository uses: actions/checkout@v7 - name: Set up Quarto uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2 - name: Render and Publish uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2 with: target: quarto-pub QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN }}</code></pre> <h6 id="quarto-pub-credentials">Quarto Pub Credentials</h6> <p>The final step is to configure your GitHub Action with the credentials required for publishing. To do this you need to create a Quarto Pub personal access token and then configure your GitHub action to be able to read it:</p> <ul> <li>If you don’t already have an access token, go to the Quarto Pub <a href="https://quartopub.com/profile">account profile page</a>, and click on New Token to create a token. Give this token a memorable name, and copy the token to the clipboard.</li> <li>Add the Quarto Pub access token to your repository’s action Secrets (accessible within repository Settings). You will see a New repository secret button at the top right:</li> <li>Click the button and add the personal access token from step 1 as a secret named <code>QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN</code>:</li> </ul> <h6 id="ignoring-output-3">Ignoring Output</h6> <p>It’s important to note that you don’t need to check your <code>_site</code> or <code>_book</code> directory into version control (if you have done this in the past you know it makes for very messy diffs!). Before proceeding you should add the output directory of your project to <code>.gitignore</code>. For example:</p> <pre><code>.gitignore /.quarto/ /_site/</code></pre> <p>If you’ve already checked these files into source control you may need to remove them explicitly:</p> <pre><code>Terminal git rm -r _site</code></pre> <h6 id="commit-to-publish-1">Commit to Publish</h6> <p>Once you’ve specified your publishing action and Quarto Pub credentials, and pushed your updated repository (including the <code>_freeze</code> directory) to GitHub, your action will run with this and subsequent commits, automatically rendering and publishing to Quarto Pub.</p> <h6 id="executing-code-3">Executing Code</h6> <p>If you prefer, you can also configure a GitHub Action to execute R, Python, or Julia code as part of rendering. While this might reflexively seem like the best approach, consider the following requirements imposed when you execute code within a CI service like GitHub Actions:</p> <ul> <li>You need to reconstitute all of the dependencies (R, Python, or Julia plus the correct versions of required packages) in the CI environment.</li> <li>If your code requires any special permissions (e.g. database or network access) those permissions also need to be present on the CI server.</li> <li>Your project may contain documents that can no longer be easily executed (e.g. blog posts from several years ago that use older versions of packages). These documents may need to have <code>freeze</code> individually enabled for them to prevent execution on CI.</li> </ul> <h6 id="prerequisites-4">Prerequisites</h6> <p>The best way to ensure that your code can be executed within a GitHub Action is to use a virtual environment like <a href="https://packaging.python.org/guides/installing-using-pip-and-virtual-environments/#creating-a-virtual-environment">venv</a> or <a href="https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html">renv</a> with your project (below we’ll provide example actions for each). If you aren’t familiar with using these tools check out the article on using Virtual Environments with Quarto to learn more.</p> <p>Once you’ve decided to execute code within your GitHub Action you can remove the <code>freeze: auto</code> described above from your <code>_quarto.yml</code> configuration. Note that if you want to use <code>freeze</code> selectively for some documents or directories that is still possible (for a directory, create a <code>_metadata.yml</code> file in the directory and specify your freeze configuration there—this is what Quarto does by default for the <code>posts</code> folder of blog projects).</p> <h6 id="example-jupyter-with-venv-3">Example: Jupyter with venv</h6> <p>Here is a complete example of a GitHub Action that installs Python, Jupyter, and package dependencies from <code>requirements.txt</code>, then executes code and renders output to Quarto Pub:</p> <pre><code>.github/workflows/publish.yml on: workflow_dispatch: push: branches: main name: Quarto Publish jobs: build-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Check out repository uses: actions/checkout@v7 - name: Set up Quarto uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2 - name: Install Python and Dependencies uses: actions/setup-python@v7 with: python-version: '3.14' cache: 'pip' - run: pip install jupyter - run: pip install -r requirements.txt - name: Render and Publish uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2 with: target: quarto-pub QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN }}</code></pre> <h6 id="example-knitr-with-renv-3">Example: Knitr with renv</h6> <p>Here is a complete example of a GitHub Action that installs R and package dependencies from <code>renv.lock</code>, then executes code and renders output to Quarto Pub:</p> <pre><code>.github/workflows/publish.yml on: workflow_dispatch: push: branches: main name: Quarto Publish jobs: build-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Check out repository uses: actions/checkout@v7 - name: Set up Quarto uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2 - name: Install R uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2 with: r-version: '4.6.1' - name: Install R Dependencies uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2 with: cache-version: 1 - name: Render and Publish uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2 with: target: quarto-pub QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN }}</code></pre> <h6 id="additional-options-3">Additional Options</h6> <p>It’s possible to have a Quarto project in a larger GitHub repository, where the Quarto project does not reside at the top-level directory. In this case, add a <code>path</code> input to the invocation of the <code>publish</code> action. For example:</p> <pre><code>- name: Render and Publish uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2 with: target: quarto-pub path: subdirectory-to-use QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN }}</code></pre> <p>By default, <code>quarto publish</code> will re-render your project before publishing it. However, if you store the rendered output in version control, you don’t need the GitHub action to re-render the project. In that case, add the option <code>render: false</code> to the <code>publish</code> action:</p> <pre><code>- name: Render and Publish uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2 with: target: quarto-pub render: false QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_PUB_AUTH_TOKEN }}</code></pre> <h2 id="reference">Reference</h2> <h3 id="asciidoc-options">AsciiDoc Options</h3> <h4 id="asciidoc-options-1">AsciiDoc Options</h4> <p>AsciiDoc is a text document format for writing documentation, articles, and books, ebooks, slideshows, web pages, man pages and blogs. You can learn more about AsciiDoc at <a href="https://asciidoc.org/">asciidoc.org</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: asciidoc format: asciidoctor</code></pre> <p>NoteAsciidoc vs Asciidoctor Format</p> <p>Pandoc includes support for both the <code>asciidoc</code> and <code>asciidoctor</code> formats. The <code>asciidoc</code> format produces older style syntax that is no longer typically used, while the <code>asciidoctor</code> format produces the more current markdown syntax that is part of the formal AsciiDoc specification.</p> <p>In Quarto, both <code>asciidoc</code> and <code>asciidoctor</code> are aliases for the <code>asciidoctor</code> format.</p> <h5 id="title-author">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Summary of document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-2">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-6">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-1">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-5">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-9">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-5">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-9">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-1">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-5">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="metadata-1">Metadata</h5> <p><code>keywords</code></p> <p>List of keywords to be included in the document metadata.</p> <h5 id="rendering-11">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run).</li> </ul> <h3 id="beamer-options-1">Beamer Options</h3> <h4 id="beamer-options-2">Beamer Options</h4> <p>Beamer is a LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides. To learn more about Beamer see <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer">ctan.org</a>.</p> <p>See the Beamer format user guide for more details on creating Beamer output with Quarto.</p> <pre><code>format: beamer</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-1">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>subtitle</code></p> <p>Identifies the subtitle of the document.</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>institute</code></p> <p>Author affiliations for the presentation.</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Summary of document</p> <p><code>thanks</code></p> <p>The contents of an acknowledgments footnote after the document title.</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-3">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Theme name, theme scss file, or a mix of both.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine</code></p> <p>Use the specified engine when producing PDF output. If the engine is not in your PATH, the full path of the engine may be specified here. If this option is not specified, Quarto uses the following defaults depending on the output format in use:</p> <ul> <li><code>latex</code>: <code>lualatex</code> (other options: <code>pdflatex</code>, <code>xelatex</code>, <code>tectonic</code>, <code>latexmk</code>)</li> <li><code>context</code>: <code>context</code></li> <li><code>html</code>: <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> (other options: <code>prince</code>, <code>weasyprint</code>, <code>pagedjs-cli</code>; see <a href="https://print-css.rocks">print-css.rocks</a> for a good introduction to PDF generation from HTML/CSS.)</li> <li><code>ms</code>: <code>pdfroff</code></li> <li><code>typst</code>: <code>typst</code> <code>pdf-engine-opt</code></li> </ul> <p>Use the given string as a command-line argument to the pdf-engine. For example, to use a persistent directory foo for latexmk’s auxiliary files, use <code>pdf-engine-opt: -outdir=foo</code>. Note that no check for duplicate options is done.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine-opts</code></p> <p>Use the given strings passed as a array as command-line arguments to the pdf-engine. This is an alternative to <code>pdf-engine-opt</code> for passing multiple options.</p> <p><code>beameroption</code></p> <p>Add an extra Beamer option using <code>\setbeameroption{}</code>.</p> <p><code>aspectratio</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio for this presentation.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>The logo image.</p> <p><code>titlegraphic</code></p> <p>The image for the title slide.</p> <p><code>navigation</code></p> <p>Controls navigation symbols for the presentation (<code>empty</code>, <code>frame</code>, <code>vertical</code>, or <code>horizontal</code>)</p> <p><code>section-titles</code></p> <p>Whether to enable title pages for new sections.</p> <p><code>colortheme</code></p> <p>The Beamer color theme for this presentation, passed to <code>\usecolortheme</code>.</p> <p><code>colorthemeoptions</code></p> <p>The Beamer color theme options for this presentation, passed to <code>\usecolortheme</code>.</p> <p><code>fonttheme</code></p> <p>The Beamer font theme for this presentation, passed to <code>\usefonttheme</code>.</p> <p><code>fontthemeoptions</code></p> <p>The Beamer font theme options for this presentation, passed to <code>\usefonttheme</code>.</p> <p><code>innertheme</code></p> <p>The Beamer inner theme for this presentation, passed to <code>\useinnertheme</code>.</p> <p><code>innerthemeoptions</code></p> <p>The Beamer inner theme options for this presentation, passed to <code>\useinnertheme</code>.</p> <p><code>outertheme</code></p> <p>The Beamer outer theme for this presentation, passed to <code>\useoutertheme</code>.</p> <p><code>outerthemeoptions</code></p> <p>The Beamer outer theme options for this presentation, passed to <code>\useoutertheme</code>.</p> <p><code>themeoptions</code></p> <p>Options passed to LaTeX Beamer themes inside <code>\usetheme</code>.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-7">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-title</code></p> <p>The title used for the table of contents.</p> <p><code>lof</code></p> <p>Print a list of figures in the document.</p> <p><code>lot</code></p> <p>Print a list of tables in the document.</p> <h5 id="numbering-2">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>number-depth</code></p> <p>By default, all headings in your document create a numbered section. You customize numbering depth using the <code>number-depth</code> option.</p> <p>For example, to only number sections immediately below the chapter level, use this:</p> <pre><code>number-depth: 1</code></pre> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <p><code>top-level-division</code></p> <p>Treat top-level headings as the given division type (<code>default</code>, <code>section</code>, <code>chapter</code>, or <code>part</code>). The hierarchy order is part, chapter, then section; all headings are shifted such that the top-level heading becomes the specified type.</p> <p>The default behavior is to determine the best division type via heuristics: unless other conditions apply, <code>section</code> is chosen. When the <code>documentclass</code> variable is set to <code>report</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>memoir</code> (unless the <code>article</code> option is specified), <code>chapter</code> is implied as the setting for this option. If <code>beamer</code> is the output format, specifying either <code>chapter</code> or <code>part</code> will cause top-level headings to become <code>\part{..}</code>, while second-level headings remain as their default type.</p> <h5 id="slides">Slides</h5> <p><code>incremental</code></p> <p>Make list items in slide shows display incrementally (one by one). The default is for lists to be displayed all at once.</p> <p><code>slide-level</code></p> <p>Specifies that headings with the specified level create slides. Headings above this level in the hierarchy are used to divide the slide show into sections; headings below this level create subheads within a slide. Valid values are 0-6. If a slide level of 0 is specified, slides will not be split automatically on headings, and horizontal rules must be used to indicate slide boundaries. If a slide level is not specified explicitly, the slide level will be set automatically based on the contents of the document</p> <h5 id="fonts-4">Fonts</h5> <p><code>mainfont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>font-family</code> on the HTML element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the main font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the main font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>monofont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS font-family property on code elements.</p> <p>For PowerPoint output, sets the font used for code.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the monospace font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>: take the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the monspace font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>fontsize</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the base CSS <code>font-size</code> property.</p> <p>For LaTeX and ConTeXt output, sets the font size for the document body text.</p> <p><code>fontenc</code></p> <p>Allows font encoding to be specified through <a href="https://www.ctan.org/pkg/fontenc"><code>fontenc</code></a> package.</p> <p>See <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/encguide">LaTeX Font Encodings Guide</a> for addition information on font encoding.</p> <p><code>fontfamily</code></p> <p>Font package to use when compiling a PDf with the <code>pdflatex</code> <code>pdf-engine</code>.</p> <p>See <a href="https://tug.org/FontCatalogue/">The LaTeX Font Catalogue</a> for a summary of font options available.</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) files, the font family for example, <code>T</code> or <code>P</code>.</p> <p><code>fontfamilyoptions</code></p> <p>Options for the package used as <code>fontfamily</code>.</p> <p>For example, to use the Libertine font with proportional lowercase (old-style) figures through the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/libertinus"><code>libertinus</code></a> package:</p> <pre><code>fontfamily: libertinus fontfamilyoptions: - osf - p</code></pre> <p><code>sansfont</code></p> <p>The sans serif font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p><code>mathfont</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the math font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the font used for mathematical content.</p> <p><code>CJKmainfont</code></p> <p>The CJK main font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xecjk"><code>xecjk</code></a> package.</p> <p><code>mainfontoptions</code></p> <p>The main font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p>For example, to use the <a href="http://www.gust.org.pl/projects/e-foundry/tex-gyre">TeX Gyre</a> version of Palatino with lowercase figures:</p> <pre><code>mainfont: TeX Gyre Pagella mainfontoptions: - Numbers=Lowercase - Numbers=Proportional</code></pre> <p><code>sansfontoptions</code></p> <p>The sans serif font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>monofontoptions</code></p> <p>The monospace font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>mathfontoptions</code></p> <p>The math font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>CJKoptions</code></p> <p>The CJK font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>microtypeoptions</code></p> <p>Options to pass to the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/microtype">microtype</a> package.</p> <p><code>linestretch</code></p> <p>For HTML output sets the CSS <code>line-height</code> property on the html element, which is preferred to be unitless.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, adjusts line spacing using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace">setspace</a> package, e.g. 1.25, 1.5.</p> <p>For Typst output, adjusts the spacing between lines of text.</p> <h5 id="colors-3">Colors</h5> <p><code>linkcolor</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>color</code> property on all links.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, The color used for internal links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the color for both external links and links within the document.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of internal hyperlinks using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>filecolor</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the color used for external links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of external file links using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>citecolor</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the color used for citation links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of citation links using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>urlcolor</code></p> <p>The color used for linked URLs using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p><code>toccolor</code></p> <p>The color used for links in the Table of Contents using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p><code>colorlinks</code></p> <p>Add color to link text, automatically enabled if any of <code>linkcolor</code>, <code>filecolor</code>, <code>citecolor</code>, <code>urlcolor</code>, or <code>toccolor</code> are set.</p> <h5 id="layout-9">Layout</h5> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>documentclass</code></p> <p>The document class.</p> <p><code>classoption</code></p> <p>For LaTeX/PDF output, the options set for the document class.</p> <p>For HTML output using KaTeX, you can render display math equations flush left using <code>classoption: fleqn</code></p> <p><code>pagestyle</code></p> <p>Control the <code>\pagestyle{}</code> for the document.</p> <p><code>papersize</code></p> <p>The paper size for the document.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-left</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the left margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the left margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the left page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-right</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-right</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the right margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the right margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the right page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-top</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-top</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the top margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the top margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-bottom</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the bottom margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <p><code>geometry</code></p> <p>Options for the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry">geometry</a> package. For example:</p> <pre><code>geometry: - top=30mm - left=20mm - heightrounded</code></pre> <p><code>hyperrefoptions</code></p> <p>Options for the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref">hyperref</a> package. For example:</p> <pre><code>hyperrefoptions: - linktoc=all - pdfwindowui - pdfpagemode=FullScreen</code></pre> <p>To customize link colors, please see the <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/pdf.html#colors">Quarto PDF reference</a>.</p> <p><code>indent</code></p> <p>Whether to use document class settings for indentation. If the document class settings are not used, the default LaTeX template removes indentation and adds space between paragraphs</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) documents, the paragraph indent, for example, <code>2m</code>.</p> <p><code>block-headings</code></p> <p>Make <code>\paragraph</code> and <code>\subparagraph</code> (fourth- and fifth-level headings, or fifth- and sixth-level with book classes) free-standing rather than run-in; requires further formatting to distinguish from <code>\subsubsection</code> (third- or fourth-level headings). Instead of using this option, <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script">KOMA-Script</a> can adjust headings more extensively:</p> <pre><code>header-includes: | \RedeclareSectionCommand[ beforeskip=-10pt plus -2pt minus -1pt, afterskip=1sp plus -1sp minus 1sp, font=\normalfont\itshape]{paragraph} \RedeclareSectionCommand[ beforeskip=-10pt plus -2pt minus -1pt, afterskip=1sp plus -1sp minus 1sp, font=\normalfont\scshape, indent=0pt]{subparagraph}</code></pre> <h5 id="code-1">Code</h5> <p><code>code-line-numbers</code></p> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-annotations</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>code-block-border-left</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a left border on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the border is enabled as well as the color of the border.</p> <p><code>code-block-bg</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a background color on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the background color is enabled as well as the color of the background.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <p><code>listings</code></p> <p>Use the <code>listings</code> package for LaTeX code blocks. The package does not support multi-byte encoding for source code. To handle UTF-8 you would need to use a custom template. This issue is fully documented here: <a href="https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/LaTeX/Source_Code_Listings#Encoding_issue">Encoding issue with the listings package</a></p> <p><code>indented-code-classes</code></p> <p>Specify classes to use for all indented code blocks</p> <h5 id="execution-1">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-6">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-env</code></p> <p>LaTeX environment for figure output</p> <p><code>fig-pos</code></p> <p>LaTeX figure position arrangement to be used in <code>\begin{figure}[]</code>.</p> <p>Computational figure output that is accompanied by the code that produced it is given a default value of <code>fig-pos="H"</code> (so that the code and figure are not inordinately separated).</p> <p>If <code>fig-pos</code> is <code>false</code>, then we don’t use any figure position specifier, which is sometimes necessary with custom figure environments (such as <code>sidewaysfigure</code>).</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-10">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>tbl-cap-location</code></li> </ul> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-6">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>cite-method</code></p> <p>Method used to format citations (<code>citeproc</code>, <code>natbib</code>, or <code>biblatex</code>).</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>biblatexoptions</code></p> <p>A list of options for BibLaTeX.</p> <p><code>natbiboptions</code></p> <p>One or more options to provide for <code>natbib</code> when generating a bibliography.</p> <p><code>biblio-style</code></p> <p>The bibliography style to use (e.g. <code>\bibliographystyle{dinat}</code>) when using <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code>.</p> <p><code>biblio-title</code></p> <p>The bibliography title to use when using <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code>.</p> <p><code>biblio-config</code></p> <p>Controls whether to output bibliography configuration for <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code> when cite method is not <code>citeproc</code>.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <p><code>link-citations</code></p> <p>If true, citations will be hyperlinked to the corresponding bibliography entries (for author-date and numerical styles only). Defaults to false.</p> <p><code>link-bibliography</code></p> <p>If true, DOIs, PMCIDs, PMID, and URLs in bibliographies will be rendered as hyperlinks. (If an entry contains a DOI, PMCID, PMID, or URL, but none of these fields are rendered by the style, then the title, or in the absence of a title the whole entry, will be hyperlinked.) Defaults to true.</p> <p><code>notes-after-punctuation</code></p> <p>If true (the default for note styles), Quarto (via Pandoc) will put footnote references or superscripted numerical citations after following punctuation. For example, if the source contains <code>blah blah [@jones99]</code>., the result will look like <code>blah blah.[^1]</code>, with the note moved after the period and the space collapsed.</p> <p>If false, the space will still be collapsed, but the footnote will not be moved after the punctuation. The option may also be used in numerical styles that use superscripts for citation numbers (but for these styles the default is not to move the citation).</p> <h5 id="footnotes-10">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>links-as-notes</code></p> <p>Causes links to be printed as footnotes.</p> <h5 id="cross-references-10">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-2">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-1">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>shorthands</code></p> <p>Enable babel language-specific shorthands in LaTeX output. When <code>true</code>, babel’s language shortcuts are enabled (e.g., French <code><<</code>/<code>>></code> for guillemets, German <code>"</code> shortcuts, proper spacing around French punctuation).</p> <p>Default is <code>false</code> because language shorthands can interfere with code blocks and other content. Only enable if you need specific typographic features for your language.</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-6">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="metadata-2">Metadata</h5> <p><code>keywords</code></p> <p>List of keywords to be included in the document metadata.</p> <p><code>subject</code></p> <p>The document subject</p> <p><code>title-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the title metadata for the document</p> <p><code>author-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the author metadata for the document</p> <p><code>date-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the date metadata for the document</p> <h5 id="rendering-12">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>keep-tex</code></p> <p>Keep the intermediate tex file used during render.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <p><code>use-rsvg-convert</code></p> <p>If <code>true</code>, attempt to use <code>rsvg-convert</code> to convert SVG images to PDF.</p> <h5 id="latexmk-1">Latexmk</h5> <p><code>latex-auto-mk</code></p> <p>Use Quarto’s built-in PDF rendering wrapper (includes support for automatically installing missing LaTeX packages)</p> <p><code>latex-auto-install</code></p> <p>Enable/disable automatic LaTeX package installation</p> <p><code>latex-min-runs</code></p> <p>Minimum number of compilation passes.</p> <p><code>latex-max-runs</code></p> <p>Maximum number of compilation passes.</p> <p><code>latex-clean</code></p> <p>Clean intermediates after compilation.</p> <p><code>latex-makeindex</code></p> <p>Program to use for <code>makeindex</code>.</p> <p><code>latex-makeindex-opts</code></p> <p>Array of command line options for <code>makeindex</code>.</p> <p><code>latex-tlmgr-opts</code></p> <p>Array of command line options for <code>tlmgr</code>.</p> <p><code>latex-output-dir</code></p> <p>Output directory for intermediates and PDF.</p> <p><code>latex-tinytex</code></p> <p>Set to <code>false</code> to prevent an installation of TinyTex from being used to compile PDF documents.</p> <p><code>latex-input-paths</code></p> <p>Array of paths LaTeX should search for inputs.</p> <h5 id="pdfa">PDF/A</h5> <p><code>pdf-standard</code></p> <p>Specifies PDF conformance standards and/or version for the output.</p> <p>Accepts a single value or array of values:</p> <p>PDF versions (both Typst and LaTeX): <code>1.4</code>, <code>1.5</code>, <code>1.6</code>, <code>1.7</code>, <code>2.0</code></p> <p>PDF/A standards (both engines): <code>a-1b</code>, <code>a-2a</code>, <code>a-2b</code>, <code>a-2u</code>, <code>a-3a</code>, <code>a-3b</code>, <code>a-3u</code>, <code>a-4</code>, <code>a-4f</code></p> <p>PDF/A standards (Typst only): <code>a-1a</code>, <code>a-4e</code></p> <p>PDF/UA standards: <code>ua-1</code> (Typst), <code>ua-2</code> (LaTeX)</p> <p>PDF/X standards (LaTeX only): <code>x-4</code>, <code>x-4p</code>, <code>x-5g</code>, <code>x-5n</code>, <code>x-5pg</code>, <code>x-6</code>, <code>x-6n</code>, <code>x-6p</code></p> <p>Example: <code>pdf-standard: [a-2b, ua-2]</code> for accessible archival PDF.</p> <h5 id="text-output-1">Text Output</h5> <p><code>ascii</code></p> <p>Use only ASCII characters in output. Currently supported for XML and HTML formats (which use entities instead of UTF-8 when this option is selected), CommonMark, gfm, and Markdown (which use entities), roff ms (which use hexadecimal escapes), and to a limited degree LaTeX (which uses standard commands for accented characters when possible). roff man output uses ASCII by default.</p> <h3 id="book-options">Book Options</h3> <h4 id="book-options-1">Book Options</h4> <p>All available options for <code>book</code> projects are documented below. See Creating a Book for an in-depth guide to creating books with Quarto.</p> <h5 id="project-1">Project</h5> <p>Options that define the type, render targets, and output of a project. Project options are specified under the <code>project</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: book output-dir: _book</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Project type (<code>default</code>, <code>website</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>manuscript</code>)</p> <p><code>render</code></p> <p>Files to render (defaults to all files)</p> <p><code>execute-dir</code></p> <p>Control the working directory for computations.</p> <ul> <li><code>file</code>: Use the directory of the file that is currently executing.</li> <li><code>project</code>: Use the root directory of the project. <code>output-dir</code></li> </ul> <p>Output directory</p> <p><code>lib-dir</code></p> <p>HTML library (JS/CSS/etc.) directory</p> <p><code>resources</code></p> <p>Additional file resources to be copied to output directory</p> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Path to brand.yml or object with light and dark paths to brand.yml</p> <p><code>preview</code></p> <p>Options for <code>quarto preview</code> (see Preview)</p> <p><code>pre-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a pre-render step</p> <p><code>post-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a post-render step</p> <h6 id="preview-7">Preview</h6> <p>Specify options that control the behavior of <code>quarto preview</code> within the <code>preview</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: book output-dir: _book preview: port: 4200 browser: false</code></pre> <p>Available <code>preview</code> options include:</p> <p><code>port</code></p> <p>Port to listen on (defaults to random value between 3000 and 8000)</p> <p><code>host</code></p> <p>Hostname to bind to (defaults to 127.0.0.1)</p> <p><code>serve</code></p> <p>Options for external preview server (see Serve)</p> <p><code>browser</code></p> <p>Open a web browser to view the preview (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>watch-inputs</code></p> <p>Re-render input files when they change (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>navigate</code></p> <p>Navigate the browser automatically when outputs are updated (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>timeout</code></p> <p>Time (in seconds) after which to exit if there are no active clients</p> <h6 id="serve-2">Serve</h6> <p>If you are creating a project extension for another publishing system that includes its own preview server (for example, Hugo or Docusaurus) then use the <code>preview: serve</code> options to customize the behavior of the preview server.</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: book preview: serve: cmd: "hugo serve --port {port} --bind {host} --navigateToChanged" env: HUGO_RELATIVEURLS: "true" ready: "Web Server is available at"</code></pre> <p><code>cmd</code></p> <p>Serve project preview using the specified command. Interpolate the <code>--port</code> into the command using <code>{port}</code>.</p> <p><code>args</code></p> <p>Additional command line arguments for preview command.</p> <p><code>env</code></p> <p>Environment variables to set for preview command.</p> <p><code>ready</code></p> <p>Regular expression for detecting when the server is ready.</p> <p>See the <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/hugo/_extension.yml">Hugo</a> and <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/docusaurus/_extension.yml">Docusaurus</a> extension source code for example usages of <code>preview: serve</code>.</p> <h5 id="book-3">Book</h5> <p>Options that affect book output. Book options are specified under the <code>book</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: title: "My Book" image: opengraph.png page-navigation: true</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Book title</p> <p><code>subtitle</code></p> <p>Book subtitle</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the book</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Book publication date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Format string for dates in the book</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Book abstract</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>Description metadata for HTML version of book</p> <p><code>references</code></p> <p>Book references file</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Base name for single-file output (e.g. PDF, ePub, docx)</p> <p><code>cover-image</code></p> <p>Cover image (used in HTML and ePub formats)</p> <p><code>cover-image-alt</code></p> <p>Alternative text for cover image (used in HTML format)</p> <p><code>sharing</code></p> <p>Sharing buttons to include on navbar or sidebar (one or more of <code>twitter</code>, <code>facebook</code>, <code>linkedin</code>)</p> <p><code>downloads</code></p> <p>Download buttons for other formats to include on navbar or sidebar (one or more of <code>pdf</code>, <code>epub</code>, and <code>docx</code>)</p> <p><code>tools</code></p> <p>Custom tools for navbar or sidebar</p> <p><code>doi</code></p> <p>The Digital Object Identifier for this book.</p> <p><code>abstract-url</code></p> <p>A url to the abstract for this item.</p> <p><code>accessed</code></p> <p>Date the item has been accessed.</p> <p><code>annote</code></p> <p>Short markup, decoration, or annotation to the item (e.g., to indicate items included in a review);</p> <p>For descriptive text (e.g., in an annotated bibliography), use <code>note</code> instead</p> <p><code>archive</code></p> <p>Archive storing the item</p> <p><code>archive-collection</code></p> <p>Collection the item is part of within an archive.</p> <p><code>archive-location</code></p> <p>Storage location within an archive (e.g. a box and folder number).</p> <p><code>archive-place</code></p> <p>Geographic location of the archive.</p> <p><code>authority</code></p> <p>Issuing or judicial authority (e.g. “USPTO” for a patent, “Fairfax Circuit Court” for a legal case).</p> <p><code>available-date</code></p> <p>Date the item was initially available (e.g. the online publication date of a journal article before its formal publication date; the date a treaty was made available for signing).</p> <p><code>call-number</code></p> <p>Call number (to locate the item in a
