<p><code>chapter-number</code></p> <p>Chapter number (e.g. chapter number in a book; track number on an album).</p> <p><code>citation-key</code></p> <p>Identifier of the item in the input data file (analogous to BiTeX entrykey);</p> <p>Use this variable to facilitate conversion between word-processor and plain-text writing systems; For an identifer intended as formatted output label for a citation (e.g. “Ferr78”), use <code>citation-label</code> instead</p> <p><code>citation-label</code></p> <p>Label identifying the item in in-text citations of label styles (e.g. “Ferr78”);</p> <p>May be assigned by the CSL processor based on item metadata; For the identifier of the item in the input data file, use <code>citation-key</code> instead</p> <p><code>collection-editor</code></p> <p>Editor of the collection holding the item (e.g. the series editor for a book).</p> <p><code>collection-number</code></p> <p>Number identifying the collection holding the item (e.g. the series number for a book)</p> <p><code>collection-title</code></p> <p>Title of the collection holding the item (e.g. the series title for a book; the lecture series title for a presentation).</p> <p><code>compiler</code></p> <p>Person compiling or selecting material for an item from the works of various persons or bodies (e.g. for an anthology).</p> <p><code>composer</code></p> <p>Composer (e.g. of a musical score).</p> <p><code>container-author</code></p> <p>Author of the container holding the item (e.g. the book author for a book chapter).</p> <p><code>container-title</code></p> <p>Title of the container holding the item (e.g. the book title for a book chapter, the journal title for a journal article; the album title for a recording; the session title for multi-part presentation at a conference)</p> <p><code>contributor</code></p> <p>A minor contributor to the item; typically cited using “with” before the name when listed in a bibliography.</p> <p><code>curator</code></p> <p>Curator of an exhibit or collection (e.g. in a museum).</p> <p><code>dimensions</code></p> <p>Physical (e.g. size) or temporal (e.g. running time) dimensions of the item.</p> <p><code>director</code></p> <p>Director (e.g. of a film).</p> <p><code>division</code></p> <p>Minor subdivision of a court with a <code>jurisdiction</code> for a legal item</p> <p><code>edition</code></p> <p>(Container) edition holding the item (e.g. “3” when citing a chapter in the third edition of a book).</p> <p><code>editor</code></p> <p>The editor of the item.</p> <p><code>editorial-director</code></p> <p>Managing editor (“Directeur de la Publication” in French).</p> <p><code>editor-translator</code></p> <p>Combined editor and translator of a work.</p> <p>The citation processory must be automatically generate if editor and translator variables are identical; May also be provided directly in item data.</p> <p><code>event-date</code></p> <p>Date the event related to an item took place.</p> <p><code>event-title</code></p> <p>Name of the event related to the item (e.g. the conference name when citing a conference paper; the meeting where presentation was made).</p> <p><code>event-place</code></p> <p>Geographic location of the event related to the item (e.g. “Amsterdam, The Netherlands”).</p> <p><code>executive-producer</code></p> <p>Executive producer of the item (e.g. of a television series).</p> <p><code>fulltext-url</code></p> <p>A url to the full text for this item.</p> <p><code>genre</code></p> <p>Type, class, or subtype of the item (e.g. “Doctoral dissertation” for a PhD thesis; “NIH Publication” for an NIH technical report);</p> <p>Do not use for topical descriptions or categories (e.g. “adventure” for an adventure movie)</p> <p><code>guest</code></p> <p>Guest (e.g. on a TV show or podcast).</p> <p><code>host</code></p> <p>Host of the item (e.g. of a TV show or podcast).</p> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>A value which uniquely identifies this item.</p> <p><code>illustrator</code></p> <p>Illustrator (e.g. of a children’s book or graphic novel).</p> <p><code>interviewer</code></p> <p>Interviewer (e.g. of an interview).</p> <p><code>isbn</code></p> <p>International Standard Book Number (e.g. “978-3-8474-1017-1”).</p> <p><code>issn</code></p> <p>International Standard Serial Number.</p> <p><code>issue</code></p> <p>Issue number of the item or container holding the item (e.g. “5” when citing a journal article from journal volume 2, issue 5);</p> <p>Use <code>volume-title</code> for the title of the issue, if any.</p> <p><code>issued</code></p> <p>Date the item was issued/published.</p> <p><code>jurisdiction</code></p> <p>Geographic scope of relevance (e.g. “US” for a US patent; the court hearing a legal case).</p> <p><code>keyword</code></p> <p>Keyword(s) or tag(s) attached to the item.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>The language of the item (used only for citation of the item).</p> <p>Should be entered as an ISO 639-1 two-letter language code (e.g. “en”, “zh”), optionally with a two-letter locale code (e.g. “de-DE”, “de-AT”).</p> <p>This does not change the language of the item, instead it documents what language the item uses (which may be used in citing the item).</p> <p><code>license</code></p> <p>The license information applicable to an item (e.g. the license an article or software is released under; the copyright information for an item; the classification status of a document)</p> <p><code>locator</code></p> <p>A cite-specific pinpointer within the item (e.g. a page number within <p>Description of the item’s format or medium (e.g. “CD”, “DVD”, “Album”, etc.)</p> <p><code>narrator</code></p> <p>Narrator (e.g. of an audio book).</p> <p><code>note</code></p> <p>Descriptive text or notes about an item (e.g. in an annotated bibliography).</p> <p><code>number</code></p> <p>Number identifying the item (e.g. a report number).</p> <p><code>number-of-pages</code></p> <p>Total number of pages of the cited item.</p> <p><code>number-of-volumes</code></p> <p>Total number of volumes, used when citing multi-volume books and such.</p> <p><code>organizer</code></p> <p>Organizer of such as a book adapted into a screenplay)</p> <p><code>original-date</code></p> <p>Issue date of the original version.</p> <p><code>original-publisher</code></p> <p>Original publisher, for items that of an item (e.g. an actor appearing in a film; a muscian performing a piece of music).</p> <p><code>pmcid</code></p> <p>PubMed Central reference number.</p> <p><code>pmid</code></p> <p>PubMed broadcast).</p> <p><code>public-url</code></p> <p>A public url for this item.</p> <p><code>publisher</code></p> <p>The publisher of the item.</p> <p><code>publisher-place</code></p> <p>The geographic location of the publisher.</p> <p><code>recipient</code></p> <p>Recipient (e.g. of a letter).</p> <p><code>reviewed-author</code></p> <p>Author of the item reviewed by the current item.</p> item.</p> <p><code>scale</code></p> <p>Scale of e.g. a map or model.</p> <p><code>script-writer</code></p> <p>Writer of a script or screenplay (e.g. of a film).</p> <p><code>section</code></p> <p>Section of the item or container holding the item (e.g. “§2.0.1” for a law; “politics” for a newspaper article).</p> <p><code>series-creator</code></p> <p>Creator of a series (e.g. of a television to site (defaults to <code>/</code>). <p><code>repo-branch</code></p> <p>Branch of website source code (defaults to <code>main</code>)</p> <p><code>issue-url</code></p> <p>URL to use for the ‘report an issue’ repository action.</p> <p><code>reader-mode</code></p> <p>Displays a ‘reader-mode’ tool which allows users to hide the sidebar and table of contents when viewing a page.</p> <p><code>llms-txt</code></p> <p>Generate llms.txt and .llms.md files for LLM-friendly content consumption.</p> <p><code>google-analytics</code></p> <p>Enable Google Analytics for this website</p> <p><code>plausible-analytics</code></p> <p>Enable Plausible Analytics for this website by pasting the script snippet from your Plausible dashboard, or by providing a path to a file containing the snippet.</p> <p>Plausible is a privacy-friendly, GDPR-compliant web analytics service that does not use cookies and does not require cookie consent.</p> <p>Option 1: Inline snippet</p> <pre><code>website: plausible-analytics: | <script async src="[plausible.io](https://plausible.io/js/script.js)"></script></code></pre> <p>Option 2: File path</p> <pre><code>website: plausible-analytics: path: _plausible_snippet.html</code></pre> <p>To get your script snippet:</p> <ul> <li>Log into your Plausible account at <a href="https://plausible.io">plausible.io</a></li> <li>Go to your site settings</li> <li>Copy the JavaScript snippet provided</li> <li>Either paste it directly in your configuration or save it to a file For more information, see <a href="https://plausible.io/docs/plausible-script">plausible.io</a></li> </ul> <p><code>cookie-consent</code></p> <p>Quarto includes the ability to request cookie consent before enabling scripts that set cookies, using <a href="https://www.cookieconsent.com/">Cookie Consent</a>.</p> <p>The user’s cookie preferences will automatically control Google Analytics (if enabled) and can be used to control custom scripts you add as well. For more information see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html#custom-scripts-and-cookie-consent">Custom Scripts and Cookie Consent</a>.</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Site search (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code> to enable/disable, or provide custom Search Options</p> <p><code>navbar</code></p> <p>Navbar options (see Navbar)</p> <p><code>sidebar</code></p> <p>Sidebar options (see Sidebar)</p> <p><code>body-header</code></p> <p>Markdown to insert at the beginning of each page’s body (below the title and author block).</p> <p><code>body-footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to insert below each page’s body.</p> <p><code>margin-header</code></p> <p>Markdown to place above margin content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>margin-footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to place below margin content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>page-navigation</code></p> <p>Provide next and previous article links in footer</p> <p><code>back-to-top-navigation</code></p> <p>Provide a ‘back to top’ navigation button</p> <p><code>bread-crumbs</code></p> <p>Whether to show navigation breadcrumbs for pages more than 1 level deep</p> <p><code>page-footer</code></p> <p>Page footer. Text content or page footer definition.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>Default site thumbnail image for <code>twitter</code> /<code>open-graph</code></p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>Default site thumbnail image alt text for <code>twitter</code> /<code>open-graph</code></p> <p><code>comments</code></p> <p><code>open-graph</code></p> <p>Generate Open Graph metadata (see Open Graph options)</p> <p><code>twitter-card</code></p> <p>Generate Twitter Card metadata (see Twitter Card options)</p> <p><code>other-links</code></p> <p>A list of other links to appear below the TOC.</p> <p><code>code-links</code></p> <p>A list of code links to appear with this document.</p> <h5 id="navbar">Navbar</h5> <p>Options that define the top navigation bar for a book For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: navbar: search: true</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The navbar title. Uses the project title if none is specified. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Specification of image that will be displayed to the left of the title.</p> <p><code>logo-alt</code></p> <p>Alternate text for the logo image.</p> <p><code>logo-href</code></p> <p>Target href from navbar logo / title. By default, the logo and title link to the root page of the site (/index.html).</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>The navbar’s background color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>The navbar’s foreground color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Include a search box in the navbar.</p> <p><code>pinned</code></p> <p>Always show the navbar (keeping it pinned).</p> <p><code>collapse</code></p> <p>Collapse the navbar into a menu when the display becomes narrow.</p> <p><code>collapse-below</code></p> <p>The responsive breakpoint below which the navbar will collapse into a menu (<code>sm</code>, <code>md</code>, <code>lg</code> (default), <code>xl</code>, <code>xxl</code>).</p> <p><code>left</code></p> <p>List of items for the left side of the navbar (see Nav Items)</p> <p><code>right</code></p> <p>List of items for the right side of the navbar (see Nav Items)</p> <p><code>toggle-position</code></p> <p>The position of the collapsed navbar toggle when in responsive mode</p> <p><code>tools-collapse</code></p> <p>Collapse tools into the navbar menu when the display becomes narrow.</p> <h5 id="nav-items">Nav Items</h5> <p>Nav items appear in the <code>left</code> or <code>right</code> key of <code>navbar</code> definitions, or <code>contents</code> key of <code>sidebar</code> definitions. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: navbar: right: - icon: github href: [github.com](https://github.com/) aria-label: GitHub</code></pre> <p><code>aria-label</code></p> <p>Accessible label for the item.</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Link to file contained with the project or external URL</p> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Name of bootstrap icon (e.g. <code>github</code>, <code>bluesky</code>, <code>share</code>) See <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com/">icons.getbootstrap.com</a> for a list of available icons</p> <p><code>menu</code></p> <p>Submenu of navigation items</p> <p><code>text</code></p> <p>Text to display for item (defaults to the document title if not provided). Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>rel</code></p> <p>Value for rel attribute. Multiple space-separated values are permitted. See <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel">developer.mozilla.org</a> for a details.</p> <p><code>target</code></p> <p>Value for target attribute. See <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#attr-target">developer.mozilla.org</a> for details.</p> <p>Note that the <code>icon</code> option is available for items in the Navbar, however items in the Sidebar do not support the <code>icon</code> option.</p> <h5 id="sidebar">Sidebar</h5> <p>Options that define the side navigation area for a book. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: sidebar: search: true</code></pre> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>The identifier for this sidebar.</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The sidebar title. Uses the project title if none is specified. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Specification of image that will be displayed in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>logo-alt</code></p> <p>Alternate text for the logo image.</p> <p><code>logo-href</code></p> <p>Target href from navbar logo / title. By default, the logo and title link to the root page of the site (/index.html).</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Include a search control in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>tools</code></p> <p>List of sidebar tools (see Sidebar Tools)</p> <p><code>contents</code></p> <p>List of navigation items to appear in the sidebar. Can also include <code>section</code> entries which in turn contain sub-lists of navigation items.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The style of sidebar (<code>docked</code> or <code>floating</code>).</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>The sidebar’s background color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>The sidebar’s foreground color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>border</code></p> <p>Whether to show a border on the sidebar (defaults to true for ‘docked’ sidebars)</p> <p><code>alignment</code></p> <p>Alignment of the items within the sidebar (<code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>collapse-level</code></p> <p>The depth at which the sidebar contents should be collapsed by default.</p> <p><code>pinned</code></p> <p>When collapsed, pin the collapsed sidebar to the top of the page.</p> <p><code>header</code></p> <p>Markdown to place above sidebar content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to place below sidebar content (text or file path)</p> <h6 id="sidebar-tools-1">Sidebar Tools</h6> <p>Action buttons that appear on the sidebar. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: sidebar: tools: - icon: github href: [github.com](https://github.com/)</code></pre> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Name of bootstrap icon (e.g. <code>github</code>, <code>twitter</code>, <code>share</code>) See <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com/">icons.getbootstrap.com</a> for a list of available icons</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Link to file contained with the project or external URL</p> <p><code>menu</code></p> <p>Submenu of navigation items</p> <h5 id="footer">Footer</h5> <p>Book page footer definition. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: page-footer: center: - text: "About" href: about.qmd - text: "License" href: license.qmd - text: "Trademark" href: trademark.qmd</code></pre> <p><code>left</code></p> <p>Footer left content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>right</code></p> <p>Footer right content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>center</code></p> <p>Footer center content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>border</code></p> <p>Footer border (<code>true</code>, <code>false</code>, or a border color)</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>Footer background color</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>Footer foreground color</p> <h5 id="search">Search</h5> <p>Search options are specified under the <code>search</code> key of <code>book</code>. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: search: location: navbar type: overlay</code></pre> <p><code>location</code></p> <p>Location for search widget (<code>navbar</code> or <code>sidebar</code>)</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Type of search UI (<code>overlay</code> or <code>textbox</code>)</p> <p><code>limit</code></p> <p>Number of matches to display (defaults to 20)</p> <p><code>collapse-after</code></p> <p>Matches after which to collapse additional results</p> <p><code>copy-button</code></p> <p>Provide button for copying search link</p> <p><code>merge-navbar-crumbs</code></p> <p>When false, do not merge navbar crumbs into the crumbs in <code>search.json</code>.</p> <p><code>keyboard-shortcut</code></p> <p>One or more keys that will act as a shortcut to launch search (single characters)</p> <p><code>show-item-context</code></p> <p>Whether to include search result parents when displaying items in search results (when possible).</p> <p><code>algolia</code></p> <p>Use an Algolia index for site search (see Algolia Options)</p> <h6 id="algolia-options">Algolia Options</h6> <p>You can use an Algolia index as the back end of book search. Specify Algolia options using the <code>algolia</code> sub-key of <code>search</code>, for example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: search: algolia: index-name: <my-index-name> application-id: <my-application-id> search-only-api-key: <my-search-only-api-key></code></pre> <p><code>index-name</code></p> <p>The name of the index to use when performing a search</p> <p><code>application-id</code></p> <p>The unique ID used by Algolia to identify your application</p> <p><code>search-only-api-key</code></p> <p>The Search-Only API key to use to connect to Algolia</p> <p><code>analytics-events</code></p> <p>Enable tracking of Algolia analytics events</p> <p><code>show-logo</code></p> <p>Enable the display of the Algolia logo in the search results footer.</p> <p><code>index-fields</code></p> <p>Fields to target for searches (see below for details)</p> <p><code>params</code></p> <p>Additional parameters to pass when executing a search</p> <p>The <code>index-fields</code> option provides sub-fields within the Algolia index to target for searches:</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Field that contains the URL of index entries</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Field that contains the title of index entries</p> <p><code>text</code></p> <p>Field that contains the text of index entries</p> <p><code>section</code></p> <p>Field that contains the section of index entries</p> <h5 id="social">Social</h5> <p>Social metadata is provided as a subkey of <code>book</code> options. You can specify <code>true</code> to generate social metadata using a set of default option, or specify one or more Twitter or Open Graph specific options as enumerated below. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: open-graph: true twitter-card: site: "@sitehandle"</code></pre> <h6 id="twitter-card">Twitter Card</h6> <p>Set Twitter options under the <code>twitter-card</code> key:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: twitter-card: site: "@sitehandle"</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The title of the page. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the title metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the title for this provider.</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>A short description of the content. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the description metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the description for this provider.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to a preview image for the content. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for the preview image. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image-alt</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>Image width (pixels)</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>Image height (pixels)</p> <p><code>card-style</code></p> <p>Card style (<code>summary</code> or <code>summary_large_image</code>).</p> <p>If this is not provided, the best style will automatically selected based upon other metadata. You can learn more about Twitter Card styles <a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/abouts-cards">here</a>.</p> <p><code>creator</code></p> <p><code>@username</code> of the content creator (must be a quoted string)</p> <p><code>site</code></p> <p><code>@username</code> of the website (must be a quoted string)</p> <h6 id="open-graph">Open Graph</h6> <p>Set Open Graph options under the <code>open-graph</code> key:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml book: open-graph: title: "Title for Open Graph"</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The title of the page. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the title metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the title for this provider.</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>A short description of the content. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the description metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the description for this provider.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to a preview image for the content. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for the preview image. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image-alt</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>Image width (pixels)</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>Image height (pixels)</p> <p><code>locale</code></p> <p>Locale of open graph metadata</p> <p><code>site-name</code></p> <p>Name that should be displayed for the overall site. If not explicitly provided in the <code>open-graph</code> metadata, Quarto will use the website or book <code>title</code> by default.</p> <h5 id="comments">Comments</h5> <p>You can add commenting to your book using either <a href="https://web.hypothes.is/">Hypothesis</a>, <a href="https://utteranc.es/">Utterances</a>, or <a href="https://giscus.app/">Giscus</a>.</p> <h6 id="hypothesis">Hypothesis</h6> <p>Enable and configure Hypothesis commenting via <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: hypothesis: theme: clean openSidebar: false</code></pre> <p><code>client-url</code></p> <p>Override the default hypothesis client url with a custom client url.</p> <p><code>openSidebar</code></p> <p>Controls whether the sidebar opens automatically on startup.</p> <p><code>showHighlights</code></p> <p>Controls whether the in-document highlights are shown by default (<code>always</code>, <code>whenSidebarOpen</code> or <code>never</code>)</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Controls the overall look of the sidebar (<code>classic</code> or <code>clean</code>)</p> <p><code>enableExperimentalNewNoteButton</code></p> <p>Controls whether the experimental New Note button should be shown in the notes tab in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>usernameUrl</code></p> <p>Specify a URL to direct a user to, in a new tab. when they click on the annotation author link in the header of an annotation.</p> <p><code>services</code></p> <p>Array of service definitions</p> <p><code>branding</code></p> <p>Custom branding/colors to apply to UI</p> <p><code>externalContainerSelector</code></p> <p>A CSS selector specifying the containing element into which the sidebar iframe will be placed.</p> <p><code>focus</code></p> <p>User focused filter set for the available annotations on a page</p> <p><code>requestConfigFromFrame</code></p> <p>Specify a host iframe to request configuration from</p> <p><code>assetRoot</code></p> <p>The root URL from which assets are loaded.</p> <p><code>sidebarAppUrl</code></p> <p>The URL for the sidebar application which displays annotations.</p> <p>For additional documentation on the Hypothesis options enumerated above, see the <a href="https://h.readthedocs.io/projects/client/en/latest/publishers/config.html">Hypothesis Publisher Config</a> documentation.</p> <h6 id="utterances">Utterances</h6> <p>Enable and configure Utterances commenting via the <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: utterances: repo: quarto-dev/quarto-web</code></pre> <p><code>repo</code></p> <p>The Github repo that will be used to store comments.</p> <p><code>label</code></p> <p>The label that will be assigned to issues created by Utterances.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>The Github theme that should be used for Utterances (<code>github-light</code>, <code>github-dark</code>, <code>github-dark-orange</code>, <code>icy-dark</code>, <code>dark-blue</code>, <code>photon-dark</code>, <code>body-light</code>, or <code>gruvbox-dark</code>)</p> <p><code>issue-term</code></p> <p>How posts should be mapped to Github issues (<code>pathname</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>title</code> or <code>og:title</code>)</p> <h6 id="giscus">Giscus</h6> <p>Enable and configure usage of the <a href="https://giscus.app">Giscus app</a> via the <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: giscus: repo: quarto-dev/quarto-web</code></pre> <p><code>repo</code></p> <p>The Github repo that will be used to store comments.</p> <p>In order to work correctly, the repo must be public, with the giscus app installed, and the discussions feature must be enabled.</p> <p><code>repo-id</code></p> <p>The Github repository identifier.</p> <p>You can quickly find this by using the configuration tool at <a href="https://giscus.app">giscus.app</a>. If this is not provided, Quarto will attempt to discover it at render time.</p> <p><code>category</code></p> <p>The discussion category where new discussions will be created. It is recommended to use a category with the Announcements type so that new discussions can only be created by maintainers and giscus.</p> <p><code>category-id</code></p> <p>The Github category identifier.</p> <p>You can quickly find this by using the configuration tool at <a href="https://giscus.app">giscus.app</a>. If this is not provided, Quarto will attempt to discover it at render time.</p> <p><code>mapping</code></p> <p>The mapping between the page and the embedded discussion.</p> <ul> <li><code>pathname</code>: The discussion title contains the page path</li> <li><code>url</code>: The discussion title contains the page url</li> <li><code>title</code>: The discussion title contains the page title</li> <li><code>og:title</code>: The discussion title contains the <code>og:title</code> metadata value</li> <li>any other string or number: Any other strings will be passed through verbatim and a discussion title containing that value will be used. Numbers will be treated as a discussion number and automatic discussion creation is not supported. <code>reactions-enabled</code></li> </ul> <p>Display reactions for the discussion’s main post before the comments.</p> <p><code>loading</code></p> <p>Specify <code>loading: lazy</code> to defer loading comments until the user scrolls near the comments container.</p> <p><code>input-position</code></p> <p>Place the comment input box above or below the comments.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>The giscus theme to use when displaying comments. Light and dark themes are supported. If a single theme is provided by name, it will be used as light and dark theme. To use different themes, use <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> key:</p> <pre><code>website: comments: giscus: theme: light: light # giscus theme used for light website theme dark: dark_dimmed # giscus theme used for dark website theme</code></pre> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>The language that should be used when displaying the commenting interface.</p> <h5 id="listings-2">Listings</h5> <p>Listings enable you to automatically generate the contents of a page (or region of a page) from a list of Quarto documents or other custom data. You can enable listings on a page using the <code>listing</code> option in the document front matter. For example, setting <code>listing: default</code> will generate a listing of all documents in the directory (with the exception of the current document):</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Listing Example" listing: default ---</code></pre> <p>To customize the listing, specify additional options under the <code>listing</code> key:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Listing Example" listing: contents: posts type: grid grid-columns: 2 ---</code></pre> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>The id of this listing. When the listing is rendered, it will place the contents into a <code>div</code> with this id. If no such <code>div</code> is defined on the page, a <code>div</code> with this id will be created and appended to the end of the page.</p> <p>If no <code>id</code> is provided for a listing, Quarto will synthesize one when rendering the page.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>The type of listing to create. Choose one of:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: A blog style list of items</li> <li><code>table</code>: A table of items</li> <li><code>grid</code>: A grid of item cards</li> <li><code>custom</code>: A custom template, provided by the <code>template</code> field <code>contents</code></li> </ul> <p>The files or path globs of Quarto documents or YAML files that should be included in the listing.</p> <p><code>sort</code></p> <p>Sort items in the listing by these fields. The sort key is made up of a field name followed by a direction <code>asc</code> or <code>desc</code>.</p> <p>For example: <code>date asc</code></p> <p>Use <code>sort:false</code> to use the unsorted original order of items.</p> <p><code>max-items</code></p> <p>The maximum number of items to include in this listing.</p> <p><code>page-size</code></p> <p>The number of items to display on a page.</p> <p><code>sort-ui</code></p> <p>Shows or hides the sorting control for the listing. To control the fields that will be displayed in the sorting control, provide a list of field names.</p> <p><code>filter-ui</code></p> <p>Shows or hides the filtering control for the listing. To control the fields that will be used to filter the listing, provide a list of field names. By default all fields of the listing will be used when filtering.</p> <p><code>categories</code></p> <p>Display item categories from this listing in the margin of the page.</p> <ul> <li><code>numbered</code>: Category list with number of items</li> <li><code>unnumbered</code>: Category list</li> <li><code>cloud</code>: Word cloud style categories <code>feed</code></li> </ul> <p>Create an RSS feed for this page using the items in this listing (see Feed).</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>The date format to use when displaying dates (e.g. d-M-yyy). Learn more about supported date formatting values <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/dates.html">here</a>.</p> <p><code>max-description-length</code></p> <p>The maximum length (in characters) of the description displayed in the listing. Defaults to 175.</p> <p><code>image-placeholder</code></p> <p>The default image to use if an item in the listing doesn’t have an image.</p> <p><code>image-lazy-loading</code></p> <p>If false, images in the listing will be loaded immediately. If true, images will be loaded as they come into view.</p> <p><code>image-align</code></p> <p>In <code>default</code> type listings, whether to place the image on the right or left side of the post content (<code>left</code> or <code>right</code>).</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>The height of the image being displayed (a CSS height string).</p> <p>The width is automatically determined and the image will fill the rectangle without scaling (cropped to fill).</p> <p><code>grid-columns</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, the number of columns in the grid display. Defaults to 3.</p> <p><code>grid-item-border</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, whether to display a border around the item card. Defaults to <code>true</code>.</p> <p><code>grid-item-align</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, the alignment of the content within the card (<code>left</code> (default), <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>).</p> <p><code>table-striped</code></p> <p>In table type listings, display the table rows with alternating background colors. Defaults to <code>false</code>.</p> <p><code>table-hover</code></p> <p>In table type listings, highlight rows of the table when the user hovers the mouse over them. Defaults to false.</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>The path to a custom listing template.</p> <p><code>template-params</code></p> <p>Parameters that are passed to the custom template.</p> <p><code>fields</code></p> <p>The list of fields to include in this listing.</p> <p><code>field-display-names</code></p> <p>A mapping that provides display names for specific fields. For example, to display the title column as ‘Report’ in a table listing you would write:</p> <pre><code>listing: field-display-names: title: "Report"</code></pre> <p><code>field-types</code></p> <p>Provides the date type for the field of a listing item. Unknown fields are treated as strings unless a type is provided. Valid types are <code>date</code>, <code>number</code>.</p> <p><code>field-links</code></p> <p>The list of fields to display as hyperlinks to the source document when the listing type is a table. By default, only the <code>title</code> or <code>filename</code> is displayed as a link.</p> <p><code>field-required</code></p> <p>Fields that items in this listing must have populated. If a listing is rendered and one more items in this listing is missing a required field, an error will occur and the render will.</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Items with matching field values will be included in the listing.</p> <p><code>exclude</code></p> <p>Items with matching field values will be excluded from the listing.</p> <h6 id="feed">Feed</h6> <p>Enable an RSS feed for your listing by including the <code>feed</code> option:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Listing Example" listing: contents: posts feed: items: 10 ---</code></pre> <p><code>items</code></p> <p>The number of items to include in your feed. Defaults to 20.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Whether to include full or partial content in the feed.</p> <ul> <li><code>full</code> (default): Include the complete content of the document in the feed.</li> <li><code>partial</code>: Include only the first paragraph of the document in the feed.</li> <li><code>metadata</code>: Use only the title, description, and other document metadata in the feed. <code>title</code></li> </ul> <p>The title for this feed. Defaults to the site title provided the Quarto project.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to an image for this feed. If not specified, the image for the page the listing appears on will be used, otherwise an image will be used if specified for the site in the Quarto project.</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>The description of this feed. If not specified, the description for the page the listing appears on will be used, otherwise the description of the site will be used if specified in the Quarto project.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>The language of the feed. Omitted if not specified. See <a href="https://www.rssboard.org/rss-language-codes">rssboard.org</a> for a list of valid language codes.</p> <p><code>categories</code></p> <p>A list of categories for which to create separate RSS feeds containing only posts with that category</p> <p><code>xml-stylesheet</code></p> <p>The path to an XML stylesheet (XSL file) used to style the RSS feed.</p> <h5 id="about">About</h5> <p>Layout a simple about page for an individual or organization. Specify about page options under the <code>about</code> key in the document front matter:</p> <pre><code>--- title: About about: template: jolla image: profile.jpg links: - icon: bluesky text: Bluesky href: [bsky.app](https://bsky.app) ---</code></pre> <p>For more, see the About Pages documentation.</p> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>The target id of this about page. When the about page is rendered, it will place read the contents of a <code>div</code> with this id into the about template that you have selected (and replace the contents with the rendered about content).</p> <p>If no such <code>div</code> is defined on the page, a <code>div</code> with this id will be created and appended to the end of the page.</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>The template to use to layout this about page. Choose from:</p> <ul> <li><code>jolla</code></li> <li><code>trestles</code></li> <li><code>solana</code></li> <li><code>marquee</code></li> <li><code>broadside</code> <code>image</code></li> </ul> <p>The path to the main image on the about page. If not specified, the <code>image</code> provided for the document itself will be used.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for the main image on the about page.</p> <p><code>image-title</code></p> <p>The title for the main image on the about page.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>A valid CSS width for the about page image.</p> <p><code>image-shape</code></p> <p>The shape of the image on the about page.</p> <ul> <li><code>rectangle</code></li> <li><code>round</code></li> <li><code>rounded</code> <code>links</code></li> </ul> <p>Links (as navigation items) to display on the about page.</p> <h3 id="brand">Brand</h3> <h4 id="brand-1">Brand</h4> <p>The <code>brand</code> option is used to define cross-format branding. You can read more about using Brand in the Guide.</p> <p>Set brand options in the <code>_brand.yml</code> file:</p> <pre><code>_brand.yml color: palette: blue: "#1c84e5" foreground: blue</code></pre> <p>You can also specify brand options in a document header under <code>brand</code>:</p> <pre><code>document.qmd --- brand: color: palette: blue: "#1c84e5" foreground: blue ---</code></pre> <h5 id="brand-2">Brand</h5> <p><code>meta</code></p> <p>Metadata for a brand, including the brand name and important links. See Meta for more information.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Provide definitions and defaults for brand’s logo in various formats and sizes. See Logo for more information.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The brand’s custom color palette and theme. See Color for more information.</p> <p><code>typography</code></p> <p>Typography definitions for the brand. See Typography for more information.</p> <p><code>defaults</code></p> <p>Default settings</p> <h5 id="meta-3">Meta</h5> <p><code>name</code></p> <p>The brand name.</p> <p><code>link</code></p> <p>Important links for the brand, including social media links. If a single string, it is the brand’s home page or website. Additional fields are allowed for internal use.</p> <h5 id="logo-1">Logo</h5> <p><code>images</code></p> <p>A dictionary of named logo resources.</p> <p><code>small</code></p> <p>A link or path to the brand’s small-sized logo or icon, or a link or path to both the light and dark versions.</p> <p><code>medium</code></p> <p>A link or path to the brand’s medium-sized logo, or a link or path to both the light and dark versions.</p> <p><code>large</code></p> <p>A link or path to the brand’s large- or full-sized logo, or a link or path to both the light and dark versions.</p> <h5 id="color-2">Color</h5> <p><code>palette</code></p> <p>The brand’s custom color palette. Any number of colors can be defined, each color having a custom name.</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>The foreground color, used for text.</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>The background color, used for the page background.</p> <p><code>primary</code></p> <p>The primary accent color, i.e. the main theme color. Typically used for hyperlinks, active states, primary action buttons, etc.</p> <p><code>secondary</code></p> <p>The secondary accent color. Typically used for lighter text or disabled states.</p> <p><code>tertiary</code></p> <p>The tertiary accent color. Typically an even lighter color, used for hover states, accents, and wells.</p> <p><code>success</code></p> <p>The color used for positive or successful actions and information.</p> <p><code>info</code></p> <p>The color used for neutral or informational actions and information.</p> <p><code>warning</code></p> <p>The color used for warning or cautionary actions and information.</p> <p><code>danger</code></p> <p>The color used for errors, dangerous actions, or negative information.</p> <p><code>light</code></p> <p>A bright color, used as a high-contrast foreground color on dark elements or low-contrast background color on light elements.</p> <p><code>dark</code></p> <p>A dark color, used as a high-contrast foreground color on light elements or high-contrast background color on light elements.</p> <p><code>link</code></p> <p>The color used for hyperlinks. If not defined, the <code>primary</code> color is used.</p> <h5 id="typography-2">Typography</h5> <p><code>fonts</code></p> <p>Font files and definitions for the brand. See Font resource definitions for more information.</p> <p><code>base</code></p> <p>The base font settings for the brand. These are used as the default for all text. See base for more information.</p> <p><code>headings</code></p> <p>Settings for headings, or a string specifying the font family only. See headings-unified for more information.</p> <p><code>monospace</code></p> <p>Settings for monospace text, or a string specifying the font family only. See monospace-unified for more information.</p> <p><code>monospace-inline</code></p> <p>Settings for inline code, or a string specifying the font family only. See monospace-inline-unified for more information.</p> <p><code>monospace-block</code></p> <p>Settings for code blocks, or a string specifying the font family only. See monospace-block-unified for more information.</p> <p><code>link</code></p> <p>Settings for links. See link-unified for more information.</p> <h6 id="font-resource-definitions">Font resource definitions</h6> <h6 id="google">google</h6> <p><code>source</code></p> <p><code>"google"</code></p> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family name, which must match the name of the font on the foundry website.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weights to include.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The font styles to include.</p> <p><code>display</code></p> <p>The font display method, determines how a font face is font face is shown depending on its download status and readiness for use.</p> <h6 id="bunny">bunny</h6> <p><code>source</code></p> <p><code>"bunny"</code></p> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family name, which must match the name of the font on the foundry website.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weights to include.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The font styles to include.</p> <p><code>display</code></p> <p>The font display method, determines how a font face is font face is shown depending on its download status and readiness for use.</p> <h6 id="file">file</h6> <p><code>source</code></p> <p><code>"file"</code></p> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family name.</p> <p><code>files</code></p> <p>The font files to include. These can be local or online. Local file paths should be relative to the <code>brand.yml</code> file. Online paths should be complete URLs.</p> <h6 id="system">system</h6> <p><code>source</code></p> <p><code>"system"</code></p> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family name, which must match the name of the font on the foundry website.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weights to include.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The font styles to include.</p> <p><code>display</code></p> family.</p> <p><code>size</code></p> <p>The font size.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>line-height</code></p> <p>The distance between lines of text.</p> <h6 id="headings-unified">headings-unified</h6> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The font style.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The text color.</p> <p><code>line-height</code></p> <p>The distance between lines of text.</p> <h6 id="monospace-unified">monospace-unified</h6> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family.</p> <p><code>size</code></p> <p>The font size.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The text color.</p> <p><code>background-color</code></p> <p>The text background color.</p> <h6 id="monospace-inline-unified">monospace-inline-unified</h6> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family.</p> <p><code>size</code></p> <p>The font size.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The text color.</p> <p><code>background-color</code></p> <p>The text background color.</p> <h6 id="monospace-block-unified">monospace-block-unified</h6> <p><code>family</code></p> <p>The font family.</p> <p><code>size</code></p> <p>The font size.</p> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The text color.</p> <p><code>background-color</code></p> <p>The text background color.</p> <p><code>line-height</code></p> <p>The distance between lines of text.</p> <h6 id="link-unified">link-unified</h6> <p><code>weight</code></p> <p>The font weight.</p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>The text color.</p> <p><code>background-color</code></p> <p>The text background color.</p> <p><code>decoration</code></p> <p>The text decoration, i.e. underline</p> <h3 id="citation-metadata">Citation Metadata</h3> <h4 id="citation-metadata-1">Citation Metadata</h4> <p>You can provide citation data for Quarto documents in the document front matter. The citation options are based upon the <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">Citation Style Language (CSL) specification for items</a>, but as YAML (rather than XML).</p> <pre><code>--- citation: type: article-journal container-title: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems volume: 21 issue: 2 issued: 2022-03 issn: 1539-9087 doi: 10.1145/3514174 ---</code></pre> <h5 id="citation-3">Citation</h5> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Abstract of the item (e.g. the abstract of a journal article)</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>The author(s) of the item.</p> <p><code>doi</code></p> <p>Digital Object Identifier (e.g. “10.1128/AEM.02591-07”)</p> <p><code>references</code></p> <p>Resources related to the procedural history of a legal case or legislation;</p> <p>Can also be used to refer to the procedural history of other items (e.g. “Conference canceled” for a presentation accepted as a conference that was subsequently canceled; details of a retraction or correction notice)</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The primary title of the item.</p> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>Citation identifier for the item (e.g. “item1”). Will be autogenerated if not provided.</p> <h3 id="code-cells-1">Code Cells</h3> <h4 id="code-cells-2">Code Cells</h4> <p>The options available in an executable code cell depend on the engine used to process them. The engine is chosen automatically, as outlined in the Guide.</p> <h5 id="code-cells-3">Code Cells</h5> <ul> <li>Jupyter</li> <li>Knitr</li> <li>Observable JS No matching items</li> </ul> <h3 id="code-cells-jupyter">Code Cells: Jupyter</h3> <h4 id="code-cells-jupyter-1">Code Cells: Jupyter</h4> <p><a href="https://jupyter.org">Jupyter</a> is an open document format that supports computations in many languages including Python, R, and Julia. Learn more about using Jupyter with Quarto in the articles on Using Python and Using Julia.</p> <h5 id="overview-119">Overview</h5> <p>Cell options affect the execution and output of executable code blocks. They are specified within comments at the top of a block. For example:</p> <pre><code>```{python} #| label: fig-polar #| echo: false #| fig-cap: "A line plot on a polar axis" ```</code></pre> <h5 id="attributes-1">Attributes</h5> <p><code>label</code></p> <p>Unique label for code cell. Used when other code needs to refer to the cell (e.g. for cross references <code>fig-samples</code> or <code>tbl-summary</code>)</p> <p><code>classes</code></p> <p>Classes to apply to cell container</p> <p><code>renderings</code></p> <p>Array of rendering names, e.g. <code>[light, dark]</code></p> <p><code>tags</code></p> <p>Array of tags for notebook cell</p> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>Notebook cell identifier. Note that if there is no cell <code>id</code> then <code>label</code> will be used as the cell <code>id</code> if it is present. See <a href="https://jupyter.org/enhancement-proposals/62-cell-id/cell-id.html">jupyter.org</a> for additional details on cell ids.</p> <h5 id="code-output">Code Output</h5> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>code-fold</code></li> </ul> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>lst-label</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Unique label for code listing (used in cross references)</p> <p><code>lst-cap</code></p> <p>Caption for code listing</p> <h5 id="cell-output-3">Cell Output</h5> <p><code>output</code></p> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>panel</code></p> <p>Panel type for cell output (<code>tabset</code>, <code>input</code>, <code>sidebar</code>, <code>fill</code>, <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>output-location</code></p> <p>Location of output relative to the code that generated it. The possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Normal flow of the slide after the code</li> <li><code>fragment</code>: In a fragment (not visible until you advance)</li> <li><code>slide</code>: On a new slide after the curent one</li> <li><code>column</code>: In an adjacent column</li> <li><code>column-fragment</code>: In an adjacent column (not visible until you advance) Note that this option is supported only for the <code>revealjs</code> format.</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-7">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-cap</code></p> <p>Figure caption</p> <p><code>fig-subcap</code></p> <p>Figure subcaptions</p> <p><code>fig-link</code></p> <p>Hyperlink target for the figure</p> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-alt</code></p> <p>Alternative text to be used in the <code>alt</code> attribute of HTML images.</p> <p><code>fig-env</code></p> <p>LaTeX environment for figure output</p> <p><code>fig-pos</code></p> <p>LaTeX figure position arrangement to be used in <code>\begin{figure}[]</code>.</p> <p>Computational figure output that is accompanied by the code that produced it is given a default value of <code>fig-pos="H"</code> (so that the code and figure are not inordinately separated).</p> <p>If <code>fig-pos</code> is <code>false</code>, then we don’t use any figure position specifier, which is sometimes necessary with custom figure environments (such as <code>sidewaysfigure</code>).</p> <p><code>fig-scap</code></p> <p>A short caption (only used in LaTeX output). A short caption is inserted in <code>\caption[]</code>, and usually displayed in the “List of Figures” of a PDF document.</p> <h5 id="tables-11">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-cap</code></p> <p>Table caption</p> <p><code>tbl-subcap</code></p> <p>Table subcaptions</p> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>html-table-processing</code></li> </ul> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process raw HTML table in cell output and leave it as-is</p> <h5 id="panel-layout-2">Panel Layout</h5> <p><code>layout</code></p> <p>2d-array of widths where the first dimension specifies columns and the second rows.</p> <p>For example, to layout the first two output blocks side-by-side on the top with the third block spanning the full width below, use <code>[[3,3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p>Use negative values to create margin. For example, to create space between the output blocks in the top row of the previous example, use <code>[[3,-1, 3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p><code>layout-ncol</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into columns</p> <p><code>layout-nrow</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into rows</p> <p><code>layout-align</code></p> <p>Horizontal alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>layout-valign</code></p> <p>Vertical alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>top</code>, <code>center</code>, or <code>bottom</code>)</p> <h5 id="page-columns">Page Columns</h5> <p><code>column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for output</p> <p><code>fig-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for figure output</p> <p><code>tbl-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for table output</p> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <h3 id="code-cells-knitr">Code Cells: Knitr</h3> <h4 id="code-cells-knitr-1">Code Cells: Knitr</h4> <p><a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/">Knitr</a> is an R package for dynamic document generation. Used when other code needs to refer to the cell (e.g. for cross references <code>fig-samples</code> or <code>tbl-summary</code>)</p> <p><code>classes</code></p> <p>Classes to apply to cell container</p> <p><code>renderings</code></p> <p>Array of rendering names, e.g. <code>[light, dark]</code></p> <h5 id="code-output-1">Code Output</h5> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>code-fold</code></li> </ul> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>lst-label</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Unique label for code listing (used in cross references)</p> <p><code>lst-cap</code></p> <p>Caption for code listing</p> <p><code>tidy</code></p> <p>Whether to reformat R code.</p> <p><code>tidy-opts</code></p> <p>List of options to pass to <code>tidy</code> handler</p> <p><code>collapse</code></p> <p>Collapse all the source and output blocks from one code chunk into a single block</p> <p><code>prompt</code></p> <p>Whether to add the prompt characters in R code. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>panel</code></p> <p>Panel type for cell output (<code>tabset</code>, <code>input</code>, <code>sidebar</code>, <code>fill</code>, <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>output-location</code></p> <p>Location of output relative to the code that generated it. The possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Normal flow of the slide after the code</li> <li><code>fragment</code>: In a fragment (not visible until you advance)</li> <li><code>slide</code>: On a new slide after the curent one</li> <li><code>column</code>: In an adjacent column</li> <li><code>column-fragment</code>: In an adjacent column (not visible until you advance) Note that this option is supported only for the <code>revealjs</code> format.</li> </ul> <p><code>message</code></p> <p>Include messages in rendered output. Possible values are <code>true</code>, <code>false</code>, or <code>NA</code>. If <code>true</code>, messages are included in the output. If <code>false</code>, messages are not included. If <code>NA</code>, messages are not included in output but shown in the knitr log to console.</p> <p><code>results</code></p> <p>How to display text results. Note that this option only applies to normal text output (not warnings, messages, or errors). The possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><p><code>markup</code>: Mark up text output with the appropriate environments depending on the output format. For example, if the text output is a character string <code>"[1] 1 2 3"</code>, the actual output that knitr produces will be:</p> <pre><code>[1] 1 2 3</code></pre></li> <li><p>In this case, <code>results: markup</code> means to put the text output in fenced code blocks (`````).</p></li> <li><p><code>asis</code>: Write text output as-is, i.e., write the raw text results directly into the output document without any markups.</p> <p><code>{r} #| results: asis cat("I'm raw **Markdown** content.\n")</code></p></li> <li><p><code>hold</code>: Hold all pieces of text output in a chunk and flush them to the end of the chunk.</p></li> <li><p><code>hide</code> (or <code>false</code>): Hide text output. <code>comment</code></p></li> </ul> <p>Prefix to be added before each line of text output. By default, the text output is commented out by <code>##</code>, so if readers want to copy and run the source code from the output document, they can select and copy everything from the chunk, since the text output is masked in comments (and will be ignored when running the copied text). Set <code>comment: ''</code> to remove the default <code>##</code>.</p> <p><code>class-output</code></p> <p>Class name(s) for text/console output</p> <p><code>attr-output</code></p> <p>Attribute(s) for text/console output</p> <p><code>class-warning</code></p> <p>Class name(s) for warning output</p> <p><code>attr-warning</code></p> <p>Attribute(s) for warning output</p> <p><code>class-message</code></p> <p>Class name(s) for message output</p> <p><code>attr-message</code></p> <p>Attribute(s) for message output</p> <p><code>class-error</code></p> <p>Class name(s) for error output</p> <p><code>attr-error</code></p> <p>Attribute(s) for error output</p> <h5 id="figures-8">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures</p> <p><code>fig-cap</code></p> <p>Figure caption</p> <p><code>fig-subcap</code></p> <p>Figure subcaptions</p> <p><code>fig-link</code></p> <p>Hyperlink target for the figure</p> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-alt</code></p> <p>Alternative text to be used in the <code>alt</code> attribute of HTML images.</p> <p><code>fig-env</code></p> <p>LaTeX environment for figure output</p> <p><code>fig-pos</code></p> <p>LaTeX figure position arrangement to be used in <code>\begin{figure}[]</code>.</p> <p>Computational figure output that is accompanied by the code that produced it is given a default value of <code>fig-pos="H"</code> (so that the code and figure are not inordinately separated).</p> <p>If <code>fig-pos</code> is <code>false</code>, then we don’t use any figure position specifier, which is sometimes necessary with custom figure environments (such as <code>sidewaysfigure</code>).</p> <p><code>fig-scap</code></p> <p>A short caption (only used in LaTeX output). A short caption is inserted in <code>\caption[]</code>, and usually displayed in the “List of Figures” of a PDF document.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default output format for figures (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p><code>out-width</code></p> <p>Width of the plot in the output document, which can be different from its physical <code>fig-width</code>, i.e., plots can be scaled in the output document. When used without a unit, the unit is assumed to be pixels. However, any of the following unit identifiers can be used: px, cm, mm, in, inch and %, for example, <code>3in</code>, <code>8cm</code>, <code>300px</code> or <code>50%</code>.</p> <p><code>out-height</code></p> <p>Height of the plot in the output document, which can be different from its physical <code>fig-height</code>, i.e., plots can be scaled in the output document. Depending on the output format, this option can take special values. For example, for LaTeX output, it can be <code>3in</code>, or <code>8cm</code>; for HTML, it can be <code>300px</code>.</p> <p><code>fig-keep</code></p> <p>How plots in chunks should be kept. Possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><code>high</code>: Only keep high-level plots (merge low-level changes into high-level plots).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Discard all plots.</li> <li><code>all</code>: Keep all plots (low-level plot changes may produce new plots).</li> <li><code>first</code>: Only keep the first plot.</li> <li><code>last</code>: Only keep the last plot.</li> <li>A numeric vector: In this case, the values are indices of (low-level) plots to keep. <code>fig-show</code></li> </ul> <p>How to show/arrange the plots. Possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><code>asis</code>: Show plots exactly in places where they were generated (as if the code were run in an R terminal).</li> <li><code>hold</code>: Hold all plots and output them at the end of a code chunk.</li> <li><code>animate</code>: Concatenate all plots into an animation if there are multiple plots in a chunk.</li> <li><code>hide</code>: Generate plot files but hide them in the output document. <code>out-extra</code></li> </ul> <p>Additional raw LaTeX or HTML options to be applied to figures</p> <p><code>external</code></p> <p>Externalize tikz graphics (pre-compile to PDF)</p> <p><code>sanitize</code></p> <p>sanitize tikz graphics (escape special LaTeX characters).</p> <p><code>interval</code></p> <p>Time interval (number of seconds) between animation frames.</p> <p><code>aniopts</code></p> <p>Extra options for animations; see the documentation of the LaTeX <a href="http://ctan.org/pkg/animate">animate package.</a></p> <p><code>animation-hook</code></p> <p>Hook function to create animations in HTML output.</p> <p>The default hook (<code>ffmpeg</code>) uses FFmpeg to convert images to a WebM video.</p> <p>Another hook function is <code>gifski</code> based on the <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/package=gifski">gifski</a> package to create GIF animations.</p> <h5 id="tables-12">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-cap</code></p> <p>Table caption</p> <p><code>tbl-subcap</code></p> <p>Table subcaptions</p> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>html-table-processing</code></li> </ul> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process raw HTML table in cell output and leave it as-is</p> <h5 id="panel-layout-3">Panel Layout</h5> <p><code>layout</code></p> <p>2d-array of widths where the first dimension specifies columns and the second rows.</p> <p>For example, to layout the first two output blocks side-by-side on the top with the third block spanning the full width below, use <code>[[3,3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p>Use negative values to create margin. For example, to create space between the output blocks in the top row of the previous example, use <code>[[3,-1, 3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p><code>layout-ncol</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into columns</p> <p><code>layout-nrow</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into rows</p> <p><code>layout-align</code></p> <p>Horizontal alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>layout-valign</code></p> <p>Vertical alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>top</code>, <code>center</code>, or <code>bottom</code>)</p> <h5 id="page-columns-1">Page Columns</h5> <p><code>column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for output</p> <p><code>fig-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for figure output</p> <p><code>tbl-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for table output</p> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <h5 id="cache-1">Cache</h5> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Whether to cache a code chunk. When evaluating code chunks for the second time, the cached chunks are skipped (unless they have been modified), but the objects created in these chunks are loaded from previously saved databases (<code>.rdb</code> and <code>.rdx</code> files), and these files are saved when a chunk is evaluated for the first time, or when cached files are not found (e.g., you may have removed them by hand). Note that the filename consists of the chunk label with an MD5 digest of the R code and chunk options of the code chunk, which means any changes in the chunk will produce a different MD5 digest, and hence invalidate the cache.</p> <p><code>cache-vars</code></p> <p>Variable names to be saved in the cache database. By default, all variables created in the current chunks are identified and saved, but you may want to manually specify the variables to be saved, because the automatic detection of variables may not be robust, or you may want to save only a subset of variables.</p> <p><code>cache-globals</code></p> <p>Variables names that are not created from the current chunk.</p> <p>This option is mainly for <code>autodep: true</code> to work more precisely—a chunk <code>B</code> depends on chunk <code>A</code> when any of <code>B</code>’s global variables are <code>A</code>’s local variables. In case the automatic detection of global variables in a chunk fails, you may manually specify the names of global variables via this option. In addition, <code>cache-globals: false</code> means detecting all variables in a code chunk, no matter if they are global or local variables.</p> <p><code>cache-lazy</code></p> <p>Whether to <code>lazyLoad()</code> or directly <code>load()</code> objects. For very large objects, lazyloading may not work, so <code>cache-lazy: false</code> may be desirable (see <a href="https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/572">#572</a>).</p> <p><code>cache-rebuild</code></p> <p>Force rebuild of cache for chunk</p> <p><code>cache-comments</code></p> <p>Prevent comment changes from invalidating the cache for a chunk</p> <p><code>dependson</code></p> <p>Explicitly specify cache dependencies for this chunk (one or more chunk labels)</p> <p><code>autodep</code></p> <p>Detect cache dependencies automatically via usage of global variables</p> <h5 id="include">Include</h5> <p><code>child</code></p> <p>One or more paths of child documents to be knitted and input into the main document.</p> <p><code>file</code></p> <p>File containing code to execute for this chunk</p> <p><code>code</code></p> <p>String containing code to execute for this chunk</p> <p><code>purl</code></p> <p>Include chunk when extracting code with <code>knitr::purl()</code></p> <h3 id="code-cells-observable-js">Code Cells: Observable JS</h3> <h4 id="code-cells-observable-js-1">Code Cells: Observable JS</h4> <p><a href="https://observablehq.com/@observablehq/observables-not-javascript">Observable JS</a> is a set of enhancements to vanilla JavaScript created by <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Bostock">Mike Bostock</a> (also the author of <a href="https://d3js.org/">D3</a>). Observable JS is distinguished by its <a href="https://github.com/observablehq/runtime">reactive runtime</a>, which is especially well suited for interactive data exploration and analysis.</p> <p>Learn more about using Observable JS with Quarto in the articles on Interactive Documents with Observable JS.</p> <h5 id="overview-121">Overview</h5> <p>Cell options affect the execution and output of executable code blocks. They are specified within comments at the top of a block. For example:</p> <pre><code>```{ojs} //| label: fig-polar //| echo: false //| fig-cap: "A line plot on a polar axis" ```</code></pre> <h5 id="attributes-3">Attributes</h5> <p><code>label</code></p> <p>Unique label for code cell.
