Used when other code needs to refer to the cell (e.g. for cross references <code>fig-samples</code> or <code>tbl-summary</code>)</p> <p><code>classes</code></p> <p>Classes to apply to cell container</p> <p><code>renderings</code></p> <p>Array of rendering names, e.g. <code>[light, dark]</code></p> <h5 id="code-output-2">Code Output</h5> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>code-fold</code></li> </ul> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>lst-label</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Unique label for code listing (used in cross references)</p> <p><code>lst-cap</code></p> <p>Caption for code listing</p> <h5 id="cell-output-5">Cell Output</h5> <p><code>output</code></p> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>panel</code></p> <p>Panel type for cell output (<code>tabset</code>, <code>input</code>, <code>sidebar</code>, <code>fill</code>, <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>output-location</code></p> <p>Location of output relative to the code that generated it. The possible values are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Normal flow of the slide after the code</li> <li><code>fragment</code>: In a fragment (not visible until you advance)</li> <li><code>slide</code>: On a new slide after the curent one</li> <li><code>column</code>: In an adjacent column</li> <li><code>column-fragment</code>: In an adjacent column (not visible until you advance) Note that this option is supported only for the <code>revealjs</code> format.</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-9">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-cap</code></p> <p>Figure caption</p> <p><code>fig-subcap</code></p> <p>Figure subcaptions</p> <p><code>fig-link</code></p> <p>Hyperlink target for the figure</p> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-alt</code></p> <p>Alternative text to be used in the <code>alt</code> attribute of HTML images.</p> <p><code>fig-env</code></p> <p>LaTeX environment for figure output</p> <p><code>fig-pos</code></p> <p>LaTeX figure position arrangement to be used in <code>\begin{figure}[]</code>.</p> <p>Computational figure output that is accompanied by the code that produced it is given a default value of <code>fig-pos="H"</code> (so that the code and figure are not inordinately separated).</p> <p>If <code>fig-pos</code> is <code>false</code>, then we don’t use any figure position specifier, which is sometimes necessary with custom figure environments (such as <code>sidewaysfigure</code>).</p> <p><code>fig-scap</code></p> <p>A short caption (only used in LaTeX output). A short caption is inserted in <code>\caption[]</code>, and usually displayed in the “List of Figures” of a PDF document.</p> <h5 id="tables-13">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-cap</code></p> <p>Table caption</p> <p><code>tbl-subcap</code></p> <p>Table subcaptions</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process raw HTML table in cell output and leave it as-is</p> <h5 id="panel-layout-4">Panel Layout</h5> <p><code>layout</code></p> <p>2d-array of widths where the first dimension specifies columns and the second rows.</p> <p>For example, to layout the first two output blocks side-by-side on the top with the third block spanning the full width below, use <code>[[3,3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p>Use negative values to create margin. For example, to create space between the output blocks in the top row of the previous example, use <code>[[3,-1, 3], [1]]</code>.</p> <p><code>layout-ncol</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into columns</p> <p><code>layout-nrow</code></p> <p>Layout output blocks into rows</p> <p><code>layout-align</code></p> <p>Horizontal alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>layout-valign</code></p> <p>Vertical alignment for layout content (<code>default</code>, <code>top</code>, <code>center</code>, or <code>bottom</code>)</p> <h5 id="page-columns-2">Page Columns</h5> <p><code>column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for output</p> <p><code>fig-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for figure output</p> <p><code>tbl-column</code></p> <p><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html">Page column</a> for table output</p> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <h3 id="commonmark-options">CommonMark Options</h3> <h4 id="commonmark-options-1">CommonMark Options</h4> <p>CommonMark is a strongly defined, highly compatible specification of Markdown. You can learn more about CommonMark at <a href="https://commonmark.org/">commonmark.org</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: commonmark</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-2">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-4">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>identifier-prefix</code></p> <p>Specify a prefix to be added to all identifiers and internal links in HTML and DocBook output, and to footnote numbers in Markdown and Haddock output. This is useful for preventing duplicate identifiers when generating fragments to be included in other pages.</p> <p><code>variant</code></p> <p>Enable and disable extensions for markdown output (e.g. “+emoji”)</p> <p><code>markdown-headings</code></p> <p>Specify whether to use <code>atx</code> (<code>#</code>-prefixed) or <code>setext</code> (underlined) headings for level 1 and 2 headings (<code>atx</code> or <code>setext</code>).</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-8">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-3">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code-2">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution-2">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-10">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-14">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-7">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="footnotes-11">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>reference-location</code></p> <p>Specify location for footnotes. Also controls the location of references, if <code>reference-links</code> is set.</p> <ul> <li><code>block</code>: Place at end of current top-level block</li> <li><code>section</code>: Place at end of current section</li> <li><code>margin</code>: Place at the margin</li> <li><code>document</code>: Place at end of document</li> </ul> <h5 id="cross-references-11">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-4">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-2">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-7">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="rendering-13">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output-2">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run). <code>strip-comments</code></li> </ul> <p>Strip out HTML comments in the Markdown source, rather than passing them on to Markdown, Textile or HTML output as raw HTML. This does not apply to HTML comments inside raw HTML blocks when the <code>markdown_in_html_blocks</code> extension is not set.</p> <p><code>ascii</code></p> <p>Use only ASCII characters in output. Currently supported for XML and HTML formats (which use entities instead of UTF-8 when this option is selected), CommonMark, gfm, and Markdown (which use entities), roff ms (which use hexadecimal escapes), and to a limited degree LaTeX (which uses standard commands for accented characters when possible). roff man output uses ASCII by default.</p> <h3 id="context-options">Context Options</h3> <h4 id="context-options-1">Context Options</h4> <p>Context is a system for typesetting documents based on TEX and METAPOST. You can learn more about Context at <a href="http://www.pragma-ade.nl/">pragma-ade.nl</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: context</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-3">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>subtitle</code></p> <p>Identifies the subtitle of the document.</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Summary of document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-5">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine</code></p> <p>Use the specified engine when producing PDF output. If the engine is not in your PATH, the full path of the engine may be specified here. If this option is not specified, Quarto uses the following defaults depending on the output format in use:</p> <ul> <li><code>latex</code>: <code>lualatex</code> (other options: <code>pdflatex</code>, <code>xelatex</code>, <code>tectonic</code>, <code>latexmk</code>)</li> <li><code>context</code>: <code>context</code></li> <li><code>html</code>: <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> (other options: <code>prince</code>, <code>weasyprint</code>, <code>pagedjs-cli</code>; see <a href="https://print-css.rocks">print-css.rocks</a> for a good introduction to PDF generation from HTML/CSS.)</li> <li><code>ms</code>: <code>pdfroff</code></li> <li><code>typst</code>: <code>typst</code> <code>pdf-engine-opt</code></li> </ul> <p>Use the given string as a command-line argument to the pdf-engine. For example, to use a persistent directory foo for latexmk’s auxiliary files, use <code>pdf-engine-opt: -outdir=foo</code>. Note that no check for duplicate options is done.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine-opts</code></p> <p>Use the given strings passed as a array as command-line arguments to the pdf-engine. This is an alternative to <code>pdf-engine-opt</code> for passing multiple options.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-9">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-4">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <p><code>pagenumbering</code></p> <p>Sets the page numbering style and location for the document using the <code>\setuppagenumbering</code> command.</p> <p>See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Command/setuppagenumbering">ConTeXt Page Numbering</a> for additional information.</p> <p><code>top-level-division</code></p> <p>Treat top-level headings as the given division type (<code>default</code>, <code>section</code>, <code>chapter</code>, or <code>part</code>). The hierarchy order is part, chapter, then section; all headings are shifted such that the top-level heading becomes the specified type.</p> <p>The default behavior is to determine the best division type via heuristics: unless other conditions apply, <code>section</code> is chosen. When the <code>documentclass</code> variable is set to <code>report</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>memoir</code> (unless the <code>article</code> option is specified), <code>chapter</code> is implied as the setting for this option. If <code>beamer</code> is the output format, specifying either <code>chapter</code> or <code>part</code> will cause top-level headings to become <code>\part{..}</code>, while second-level headings remain as their default type.</p> <h5 id="fonts-5">Fonts</h5> <p><code>mainfont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>font-family</code> on the HTML element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the main font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the main font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>monofont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS font-family property on code elements.</p> <p>For PowerPoint output, sets the font used for code.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the monospace font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>: take the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the monspace font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>fontsize</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the base CSS <code>font-size</code> property.</p> <p>For LaTeX and ConTeXt output, sets the font size for the document body text.</p> <p><code>linestretch</code></p> <p>For HTML output sets the CSS <code>line-height</code> property on the html element, which is preferred to be unitless.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, adjusts line spacing using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace">setspace</a> package, e.g. 1.25, 1.5.</p> <p>For Typst output, adjusts the spacing between lines of text.</p> <p><code>interlinespace</code></p> <p>Adjusts line spacing using the <code>\setupinterlinespace</code> command.</p> <p><code>linkstyle</code></p> <p>The typeface style for links in the document.</p> <p><code>whitespace</code></p> <p>Set the spacing between paragraphs, for example <code>none</code>, <code>small</code> using the <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Command/setupwhitespace"><code>setupwhitespace</code></a> command.</p> <h5 id="colors-4">Colors</h5> <p><code>linkcolor</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>color</code> property on all links.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, The color used for internal links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the color for both external links and links within the document.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of internal hyperlinks using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>contrastcolor</code></p> <p>Color for links to other content within the document.</p> <p>See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Color">ConTeXt Color</a> for additional information.</p> <h5 id="layout-10">Layout</h5> <p><code>layout</code></p> <p>The options for margins and text layout for this document.</p> <p>See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Layout">ConTeXt Layout</a> for additional information.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-left</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the left margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the left margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the left page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-right</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-right</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the right margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the right margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the right page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-top</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-top</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the top margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the top margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-bottom</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the bottom margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <h5 id="formatting-1">Formatting</h5> <p><code>indenting</code></p> <p>Set the indentation of paragraphs with one or more options.</p> <p>See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Indentation">ConTeXt Indentation</a> for additional information.</p> <h5 id="code-3">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution-3">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-11">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-15">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-8">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-12">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-5">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-3">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-8">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>headertext</code></p> <p>Text to be in a running header.</p> <p>Provide a single option or up to four options for different placements (odd page inner, odd page outer, even page innner, even page outer).</p> <p><code>footertext</code></p> <p>Text to be in a running footer.</p> <p>Provide a single option or up to four options for different placements (odd page inner, odd page outer, even page innner, even page outer).</p> <p>See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Headers_and_Footers">ConTeXt Headers and Footers</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>includesource</code></p> <p>Whether to include all source documents as file attachments in the PDF file.</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="metadata-3">Metadata</h5> <p><code>keywords</code></p> <p>List of keywords to be included in the document metadata.</p> <h5 id="rendering-14">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="pdfa-1">PDF/A</h5> <p><code>pdfa</code></p> <p>Adds the necessary setup to the document preamble to generate PDF/A of the type specified.</p> <p>If the value is set to <code>true</code>, <code>1b:2005</code> will be used as default.</p> <p>To successfully generate PDF/A the required ICC color profiles have to be available and the content and all included files (such as images) have to be standard conforming. The ICC profiles and output intent may be specified using the variables <code>pdfaiccprofile</code> and <code>pdfaintent</code>. See also <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/PDF/A">ConTeXt PDFA</a> for more details.</p> <p><code>pdfaiccprofile</code></p> <p>When used in conjunction with <code>pdfa</code>, specifies the ICC profile to use in the PDF, e.g. <code>default.cmyk</code>.</p> <p>If left unspecified, <code>sRGB.icc</code> is used as default. May be repeated to include multiple profiles. Note that the profiles have to be available on the system. They can be obtained from <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/PDFX#ICC_profiles">ConTeXt ICC Profiles</a>.</p> <p><code>pdfaintent</code></p> <p>When used in conjunction with <code>pdfa</code>, specifies the output intent for the colors, for example <code>ISO coated v2 300\letterpercent\space (ECI)</code></p> <p>If left unspecified, <code>sRGB IEC61966-2.1</code> is used as default.</p> <h5 id="text-output-3">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run).</li> </ul> <h3 id="cross-reference-options-cross-reference-options-the-crossref">Cross Reference Options (# Cross Reference Options The <code>crossref</code>)</h3> <h4 id="cross-reference-options-2">Cross Reference Options</h4> <p>The <code>crossref</code> option is used to customize the appearance and behavior of cross-references. You can read more about using Cross-References in the Guide.</p> <pre><code>--- crossref: labels: roman title-delim: "-" ---</code></pre> <h5 id="crossref">Crossref</h5> <p><code>custom</code></p> <p>A custom cross reference type. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html#custom">Custom</a> for more details.</p> <p><code>chapters</code></p> <p>Use top level sections (H1) in this document as chapters.</p> <p><code>title-delim</code></p> <p>The delimiter used between the prefix and the caption.</p> <p><code>fig-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for figure captions.</p> <p><code>tbl-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for table captions.</p> <p><code>eq-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for equation captions.</p> <p><code>lst-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for listing captions.</p> <p><code>thm-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for theorem captions.</p> <p><code>lem-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for lemma captions.</p> <p><code>cor-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for corollary captions.</p> <p><code>prp-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for proposition captions.</p> <p><code>cnj-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for conjecture captions.</p> <p><code>def-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for definition captions.</p> <p><code>exm-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for example captions.</p> <p><code>exr-title</code></p> <p>The title prefix used for exercise captions.</p> <p><code>fig-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a figure.</p> <p><code>tbl-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a table.</p> <p><code>eq-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to an equation.</p> <p><code>sec-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a section.</p> <p><code>lst-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a listing.</p> <p><code>thm-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a theorem.</p> <p><code>lem-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a lemma.</p> <p><code>cor-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a corollary.</p> <p><code>prp-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a proposition.</p> <p><code>cnj-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a conjecture.</p> <p><code>def-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to a definition.</p> <p><code>exm-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to an example.</p> <p><code>exr-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used for an inline reference to an exercise.</p> <p><code>fig-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for figures.</p> <p><code>tbl-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for tables.</p> <p><code>eq-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for equations.</p> <p><code>sec-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for sections.</p> <p><code>lst-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for listings.</p> <p><code>thm-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for theorems.</p> <p><code>lem-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for lemmas.</p> <p><code>cor-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for corollaries.</p> <p><code>prp-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for propositions.</p> <p><code>cnj-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for conjectures.</p> <p><code>def-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for definitions.</p> <p><code>exm-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for examples.</p> <p><code>exr-labels</code></p> <p>The numbering scheme used for exercises.</p> <p><code>lof-title</code></p> <p>The title used for the list of figures.</p> <p><code>lot-title</code></p> <p>The title used for the list of tables.</p> <p><code>lol-title</code></p> <p>The title used for the list of listings.</p> <p><code>labels</code></p> <p>The number scheme used for references.</p> <p><code>subref-labels</code></p> <p>The number scheme used for sub references.</p> <p><code>ref-hyperlink</code></p> <p>Whether cross references should be hyper-linked.</p> <p><code>appendix-title</code></p> <p>The title used for appendix.</p> <p><code>appendix-delim</code></p> <p>The delimiter beween appendix number and title.</p> <h5 id="custom-1">Custom</h5> <p>Use the <code>custom</code> option to <code>crossref</code> to define new types of cross reference. For example:</p> <pre><code>--- crossref: custom: - key: vid kind: float reference-prefix: Video ---</code></pre> <p><code>kind</code></p> <p>The kind of cross reference (currently only “float” is supported).</p> <p><code>reference-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used in rendered references when referencing this type.</p> <p><code>caption-prefix</code></p> <p>The prefix used in rendered captions when referencing this type. If omitted, the field <code>reference-prefix</code> is used.</p> <p><code>space-before-numbering</code></p> <p>If false, use no space between crossref prefixes and numbering.</p> <p><code>key</code></p> <p>The key used to prefix reference labels of this type, such as “fig”, “tbl”, “lst”, etc.</p> <p><code>latex-env</code></p> <p>In LaTeX output, the name of the custom environment to be used.</p> <p><code>latex-list-of-file-extension</code></p> <p>In LaTeX output, the extension of the auxiliary file used by LaTeX to collect names to be used in the custom “list of” command. If omitted, a string with prefix <code>lo</code> and suffix with the value of <code>ref-type</code> is used.</p> <p><code>latex-list-of-description</code></p> <p>The description of the crossreferenceable object to be used in the title of the “list of” command. If omitted, the field <code>reference-prefix</code> is used.</p> <p><code>caption-location</code></p> <p>The location of the caption relative to the crossreferenceable content.</p> <h3 id="dashboard-options">Dashboard Options</h3> <h4 id="dashboard-options-1">Dashboard Options</h4> <h5 id="format">Format</h5> <p>The following document and format options are either dashboard-specific or have special behavior within dashboards:</p> <p>Option</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Title (displayed in top left of navigation bar)</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author (displayed alongside title in smaller font)</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Logo (displayed left of the title in the navigation bar)</p> <p><code>orientation</code></p> <p><code>rows</code> or <code>columns</code> (default: <code>rows</code>)</p> <p><code>scrolling</code></p> <p>Use scrolling rather than fill layout? (default: <code>false</code>)</p> <p><code>expandable</code></p> <p>Make card content expandable (default: <code>true</code>)</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Dashboard theme (built in or custom scss)</p> <p><code>nav-buttons</code></p> <p>Buttons to appear on the right side of the navigation bar. Use <code>linkedin</code>, <code>facebook</code>, <code>reddit</code>, <code>twitter</code>, <code>github</code>, or a custom Nav Item.</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Dashboard" author: "Acme, Inc." logo: images/acme.png format: dashboard: theme: default orientation: rows expandable: true scrolling: false nav-buttons: - reddit - icon: gitlab href: [gitlab.com](https://gitlab.com/) ---</code></pre> <h6 id="pages-1">Pages</h6> <p>Pages can specify a custom orientation that is distinct from the global orientation:</p> <p>Option</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>orientation</code></p> <p><code>rows</code> or <code>columns</code> (default to global orientation)</p> <p><code>scrolling</code></p> <p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code> (defaults to global scrolling)</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Dashboard" format: dashboard --- # Plots {orientation="columns" scrolling="true"}</code></pre> <h6 id="sidebars-1">Sidebars</h6> <p>Create Sidebars by applying the <code>.sidebar</code> attribute to a level 1 heading (for global sidebars) or level 2 heading (for page level sidebars).</p> <p>Class</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>.sidebar</code></p> <p>Contents should be arranged into a sidebar</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Dashboard" format: dashboard --- # Plots {.sidebar}</code></pre> <h6 id="rows-columns">Rows & Columns</h6> <p>Rows and columns support options for customizing their layout and sizing behavior. The following classes can be used to modify layout behavior:</p> <p>Class</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>.tabset</code></p> <p>Contents should be arranged into a Tabset</p> <p><code>.fill</code></p> <p>Contents should fill available layout space</p> <p><code>.flow</code></p> <p>Contents should flow to their natural size</p> <p>Note that in most dashboards, <code>.fill</code> and <code>.flow</code> are determined automatically based on the contents of cards and don’t need to be specified manually.</p> <p>The following attributes can be used for explicit sizing:</p> <p>Option</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>width</code></p> <p>Percentage or absolute pixel width (default distributes space evenly across elements in a row)</p> <p><code>height</code></p> <p>Percentage or absolute pixel height (default distributes space evenly across elements in a column)</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Dashboard" format: dashboard --- ## Row {height="65%"} ## Row {height="35%"}</code></pre> <p>Note that if some components specify an explicit <code>width</code> or <code>height</code> and others do not, then remaining space will be distributed evenly across those elements.</p> <h6 id="cards-1">Cards</h6> <p>Card options enable you to specify a title and various layout behaviors:</p> <p>Option</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Title displayed in card header</p> <p><code>padding</code></p> <p>Padding around card content (default: <code>8px</code>)</p> <p><code>expandable</code></p> <p>Make card content expandable (default: <code>true</code>)</p> <p><code>width</code></p> <p>Percentage or absolute pixel width (default distributes space evenly across elements in a row)</p> <p><code>height</code></p> <p>Percentage or absolute pixel height (default distributes space evenly across elements in a column)</p> <p><code>fill</code></p> <p>Whether the card should fill its container or ‘flow’, matching the height of its content. (Quarto determines the default value based upon the card contents)</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>```{python} #| title: "Life Expectancy" #| padding: 3px #| expandable: false #| width: 70% ```</code></pre> <p>These same options can be applied to <code>.card</code> divs. For example:</p> <pre><code>::: {.card title="Life Expectancy" padding="3px"} This is the content. :::</code></pre> <h6 id="value-boxes-2">Value Boxes</h6> <p>Value Boxes support the following options:</p> <p>Option</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Title displayed above value</p> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Icon identifier from <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com">bootstrap icons</a></p> <p><code>color</code></p> <p>Background color—this can be any CSS color or one of the theme specific color aliases (see below)</p> <p><code>value</code></p> <p>Main display value</p> <p>Available themed aliases for <code>color</code> include:</p> <p>Color Alias</p> <p>Default Theme Color(s)</p> <p><code>primary</code></p> <p>Blue</p> <p><code>secondary</code></p> <p>Gray</p> <p><code>success</code></p> <p>Green</p> <p><code>info</code></p> <p>Bright Blue</p> <p><code>warning</code></p> <p>Yellow/Orange</p> <p><code>danger</code></p> <p>Red</p> <p><code>light</code></p> <p>Light Gray</p> <p><code>dark</code></p> <p>Black</p> <p>Note that value box options can be specified either as cell options or by printing a <code>dict()</code> (for Python) or <code>list()</code> (for R) (this is helpful when options need to be dynamic). See the Value Boxes component documentation for details.</p> <h5 id="title-author-4">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>subtitle</code></p> <p>Identifies the subtitle of the document.</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="dashboard-2">Dashboard</h5> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Logo image(s) (placed on the left side of the navigation bar)</p> <p><code>orientation</code></p> <p>Default orientation for dashboard content (default <code>rows</code>)</p> <p><code>scrolling</code></p> <p>Use scrolling rather than fill layout (default: <code>false</code>)</p> <p><code>expandable</code></p> <p>Make card content expandable (default: <code>true</code>)</p> <p><code>nav-buttons</code></p> <p>Links to display on the dashboard navigation bar</p> <h5 id="format-options-6">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Theme name, theme scss file, or a mix of both.</p> <p><code>css</code></p> <p>One or more CSS style sheets.</p> <p><code>identifier-prefix</code></p> <p>Specify a prefix to be added to all identifiers and internal links in HTML and DocBook output, and to footnote numbers in Markdown and Haddock output. This is useful for preventing duplicate identifiers when generating fragments to be included in other pages.</p> <p><code>email-obfuscation</code></p> <p>Specify a method for obfuscating <code>mailto:</code> links in HTML documents.</p> <ul> <li><code>javascript</code>: Obfuscate links using JavaScript.</li> <li><code>references</code>: Obfuscate links by printing their letters as decimal or hexadecimal character references.</li> <li><code>none</code> (default): Do not obfuscate links. <code>html-q-tags</code></li> </ul> <p>Use <code><q></code> tags for quotes in HTML.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-10">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-5">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>number-depth</code></p> <p>By default, all headings in your document create a numbered section. You customize numbering depth using the <code>number-depth</code> option.</p> <p>For example, to only number sections immediately below the chapter level, use this:</p> <pre><code>number-depth: 1</code></pre> <p><code>number-offset</code></p> <p>Offset for section headings in output (offsets are 0 by default) The first number is added to the section number for top-level headings, the second for second-level headings, and so on. So, for example, if you want the first top-level heading in your document to be numbered “6”, specify <code>number-offset: 5</code>. If your document starts with a level-2 heading which you want to be numbered “1.5”, specify <code>number-offset: [1,4]</code>. Implies <code>number-sections</code></p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="layout-11">Layout</h5> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>classoption</code></p> <p>For LaTeX/PDF output, the options set for the document class.</p> <p>For HTML output using KaTeX, you can render display math equations flush left using <code>classoption: fleqn</code></p> <p><code>max-width</code></p> <p>Adds a css <code>max-width</code> to the body Element.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-left</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the left margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the left margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the left page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-right</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-right</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the right margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the right margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the right page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-top</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-top</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the top margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the top margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-bottom</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the bottom margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <h5 id="code-4">Code</h5> <p><code>code-fold</code></p> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-copy</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Enable a code copy icon for code blocks.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Always show the icon</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never show the icon</li> <li><code>hover</code> (default): Show the icon when the mouse hovers over the code block <code>code-link</code></li> </ul> <p>Enables hyper-linking of functions within code blocks to their online documentation.</p> <p>Code linking is currently implemented only for the knitr engine (via the <a href="https://downlit.r-lib.org/">downlit</a> package). A limitation of downlit currently prevents code linking if <code>code-line-numbers</code> is also <code>true</code>.</p> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <p><code>indented-code-classes</code></p> <p>Specify classes to use for all indented code blocks</p> <h5 id="execution-4">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache
