results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-12">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <p><code>fig-responsive</code></p> <p>Whether to make images in this document responsive.</p> <h5 id="tables-16">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>tbl-cap-location</code></li> </ul> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-9">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citations-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for citation that shows the reference information.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="footnotes-12">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>footnotes-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for footnotes that shows the footnote contents.</p> <p><code>reference-location</code></p> <p>Specify location for footnotes. Also controls the location of references, if <code>reference-links</code> is set.</p> <ul> <li><code>block</code>: Place at end of current top-level block</li> <li><code>section</code>: Place at end of current section</li> <li><code>margin</code>: Place at the margin</li> <li><code>document</code>: Place at end of document</li> </ul> <h5 id="cross-references-13">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <p><code>crossrefs-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for cross references that shows the item being referenced.</p> <h5 id="citation-6">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-4">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-7">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code-6">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution-6">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-14">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-18">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-11">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-15">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-8">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-6">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-11">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="rendering-17">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>css</code></p> <p>One or more CSS style sheets.</p> <p><code>html-math-method</code></p> <p>Method use to render math in HTML output (<code>plain</code>, <code>webtex</code>, <code>gladtex</code>, <code>mathml</code>, <code>mathjax</code>, <code>katex</code>).</p> <p>See the Pandoc documentation on <a href="https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#math-rendering-in-html">Math Rendering in HTML</a> for additional details.</p> <p><code>html-q-tags</code></p> <p>Use <code><q></code> tags for quotes in HTML.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-14">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>number-depth</code></p> <p>By default, all headings in your document create a numbered section. You customize numbering depth using the <code>number-depth</code> option.</p> <p>For example, to only number sections immediately below the chapter level, use this:</p> <pre><code>number-depth: 1</code></pre> <p><code>number-offset</code></p> <p>Offset for section headings in output (offsets are 0 by default) The first number is added to the section number for top-level headings, the second for second-level headings, and so on. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="epub-options-2">ePub Options</h5> <p><code>identifier</code></p> <p>The identifier for this publication.</p> <p><code>creator</code></p> <p>Creators of this publication.</p> <p><code>contributor</code></p> <p>Contributors to this publication.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Text describing the specialized type of this publication.</p> <p>An informative registry of specialized EPUB Publication types for use with this element is maintained in the <a href="https://www.w3.org/publishing/epub32/epub-packages.html#bib-typesregistry">TypesRegistry</a>, but Authors may use any text string as a value.</p> <p><code>format</code></p> <p>Text describing the format of this publication.</p> <p><code>relation</code></p> <p>Text describing the relation of this publication.</p> <p><code>coverage</code></p> <p>Text describing the coverage of this publication.</p> <p><code>rights</code></p> <p>Text describing the rights of this publication.</p> <p><code>belongs-to-collection</code></p> <p>Identifies the name of a collection to which the EPUB Publication belongs.</p> <p><code>group-position</code></p> <p>Indicates the numeric position in which this publication belongs relative to other works belonging to the same <code>belongs-to-collection</code> field.</p> <p><code>page-progression-direction</code></p> <p>Sets the global direction in which content flows (<code>ltr</code> or <code>rtl</code>)</p> <p><code>ibooks</code></p> <p>iBooks specific metadata options.</p> <p><code>epub-metadata</code></p> <p>Look in the specified XML file for metadata for the EPUB. Any of these may be overridden by elements in the metadata file.</p> <p>Note: if the source document is Markdown, a YAML metadata block in the document can be used instead.</p> <p><code>epub-subdirectory</code></p> <p>Specify the subdirectory in the OCF container that is to hold the EPUB-specific contents. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-copy</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Enable a code copy icon for code blocks.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Always show the icon</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never show the icon</li> <li><code>hover</code> (default): Show the icon when the mouse hovers over the code block <code>code-annotations</code></li> </ul> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>df-print</code></li> </ul> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-14">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-14">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-18">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output-11">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run).</li> </ul> <h3 id="groff-manuscript-options">Groff Manuscript Options</h3> <h4 id="groff-manuscript-options-1">Groff Manuscript Options</h4> <p>The Groff (GNU troff) manuscript format consists of plain text mixed with formatting commands that produces PostScript, PDF, or HTML. Learn more about Groff at <a href="https://www.gnu.org/software/groff/groff.html">gnu.org</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: ms</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-13">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Summary of document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-15">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine</code></p> <p>Use the specified engine when producing PDF output. If the engine is not in your PATH, the full path of the engine may be specified here. If this option is not specified, Quarto uses the following defaults depending on the output format in use:</p> <ul> <li><code>latex</code>: <code>lualatex</code> (other options: <code>pdflatex</code>, <code>xelatex</code>, <code>tectonic</code>, <code>latexmk</code>)</li> <li><code>context</code>: <code>context</code></li> <li><code>html</code>: <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> (other options: <code>prince</code>, <code>weasyprint</code>, <code>pagedjs-cli</code>; see <a href="https://print-css.rocks">print-css.rocks</a> for a good introduction to PDF generation from HTML/CSS.)</li> <li><code>ms</code>: <code>pdfroff</code></li> <li><code>typst</code>: <code>typst</code> <code>pdf-engine-opt</code></li> </ul> <p>Use the given string as a command-line argument to the pdf-engine. For example, to use a persistent directory foo for latexmk’s auxiliary files, use <code>pdf-engine-opt: -outdir=foo</code>. Note that no check for duplicate options is done.</p> <p><code>pdf-engine-opts</code></p> <p>Use the given strings passed as a array as command-line arguments to the pdf-engine. This is an alternative to <code>pdf-engine-opt</code> for passing multiple options.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-17">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-14">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="fonts-6">Fonts</h5> <p><code>fontfamily</code></p> <p>Font package to use when compiling a PDf with the <code>pdflatex</code> <code>pdf-engine</code>.</p> <p>See <a href="https://tug.org/FontCatalogue/">The LaTeX Font Catalogue</a> for a summary of font options available.</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) files, the font family for example, <code>T</code> or <code>P</code>.</p> <p><code>pointsize</code></p> <p>The point size, for example, <code>10p</code>.</p> <p><code>lineheight</code></p> <p>The line height, for example, <code>12p</code>.</p> <h5 id="layout-12">Layout</h5> <p><code>indent</code></p> <p>Whether to use document class settings for indentation. If the document class settings are not used, the default LaTeX template removes indentation and adds space between paragraphs</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) documents, the paragraph indent, for example, <code>2m</code>.</p> <h5 id="code-13">Code</h5> <p><code>code-line-numbers</code></p> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-annotations</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <p><code>indented-code-classes</code></p> <p>Specify classes to use for all indented code blocks</p> <h5 id="execution-13">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-21">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-25">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-18">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-22">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-15">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-13">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-18">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension.
