Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code-14">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution-14">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-22">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-26">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-19">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-23">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-16">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-14">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-19">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="rendering-25">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output-13">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run).</li> </ul> <h3 id="html-options">HTML Options</h3> <h4 id="html-options-1">HTML Options</h4> <p>HTML is a markup language used for structuring and presenting content on the web. To learn more about HTML see <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML5">en.wikipedia.org</a>.</p> <p>See the HTML format user guide for more details on creating HTML output with Quarto.</p> <pre><code>format: html</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-15">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>subtitle</code></p> <p>Identifies the subtitle of the document.</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>date-modified</code></p> <p>Document date modified</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>abstract</code></p> <p>Summary of document</p> <p><code>abstract-title</code></p> <p>Title used to label document abstract</p> <p><code>doi</code></p> <p>Displays the document Digital Object Identifier in the header.</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-17">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Theme name, theme scss file, or a mix of both.</p> <p><code>body-classes</code></p> <p>Classes to apply to the body of the document.</p> <p><code>minimal</code></p> <p>Disables the built in html features like theming, anchor sections, code block behavior, and more.</p> <p><code>css</code></p> <p>One or more CSS style sheets.</p> <p><code>anchor-sections</code></p> <p>Enables hover over a section title to see an anchor link.</p> <p><code>tabsets</code></p> <p>Enables tabsets to present content.</p> <p><code>smooth-scroll</code></p> <p>Enables smooth scrolling within the page.</p> <p><code>respect-user-color-scheme</code></p> <p>If set, Quarto reads the <code>prefers-color-scheme</code> media query to determine whether to show the user a dark or light page. Otherwise the author-preferred color scheme is shown.</p> <p><code>html-math-method</code></p> <p>Method use to render math in HTML output (<code>plain</code>, <code>webtex</code>, <code>gladtex</code>, <code>mathml</code>, <code>mathjax</code>, <code>katex</code>).</p> <p>See the Pandoc documentation on <a href="https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#math-rendering-in-html">Math Rendering in HTML</a> for additional details.</p> <p><code>section-divs</code></p> <p>Wrap sections in <code><section></code> tags and attach identifiers to the enclosing <code><section></code> rather than the heading itself.</p> <p><code>identifier-prefix</code></p> <p>Specify a prefix to be added to all identifiers and internal links in HTML and DocBook output, and to footnote numbers in Markdown and Haddock output. This is useful for preventing duplicate identifiers when generating fragments to be included in other pages.</p> <p><code>email-obfuscation</code></p> <p>Specify a method for obfuscating <code>mailto:</code> links in HTML documents.</p> <ul> <li><code>javascript</code>: Obfuscate links using JavaScript.</li> <li><code>references</code>: Obfuscate links by printing their letters as decimal or hexadecimal character references.</li> <li><code>none</code> (default): Do not obfuscate links. <code>html-q-tags</code></li> </ul> <p>Use <code><q></code> tags for quotes in HTML.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-19">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <p><code>toc-location</code></p> <p>Location for table of contents:</p> <ul> <li><code>body</code>: Show the Table of Contents in the center body of the document.</li> <li><code>left</code>: Show the Table of Contents in left margin of the document.</li> <li><code>right</code>(default): Show the Table of Contents in right margin of the document.</li> <li><code>left-body</code>: Show two Tables of Contents in both the center body and the left margin of the document.</li> <li><code>right-body</code>: Show two Tables of Contents in both the center body and the right margin of the document. <code>toc-title</code></li> </ul> <p>The title used for the table of contents.</p> <p><code>toc-expand</code></p> <p>Specifies the depth of items in the table of contents that should be displayed as expanded in HTML output. Use <code>true</code> to expand all or <code>false</code> to collapse all.</p> <h5 id="numbering-16">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>number-depth</code></p> <p>By default, all headings in your document create a numbered section. You customize numbering depth using the <code>number-depth</code> option.</p> <p>For example, to only number sections immediately below the chapter level, use this:</p> <pre><code>number-depth: 1</code></pre> <p><code>number-offset</code></p> <p>Offset for section headings in output (offsets are 0 by default) The first number is added to the section number for top-level headings, the second for second-level headings, and so on. So, for example, if you want the first top-level heading in your document to be numbered “6”, specify <code>number-offset: 5</code>. If your document starts with a level-2 heading which you want to be numbered “1.5”, specify <code>number-offset: [1,4]</code>. Implies <code>number-sections</code></p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="fonts-7">Fonts</h5> <p><code>mainfont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>font-family</code> on the HTML element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the main font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the main font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>monofont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS font-family property on code elements.</p> <p>For PowerPoint output, sets the font used for code.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the monospace font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>: take the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the monspace font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>fontsize</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the base CSS <code>font-size</code> property.</p> <p>For LaTeX and ConTeXt output, sets the font size for the document body text.</p> <p><code>linestretch</code></p> <p>For HTML output sets the CSS <code>line-height</code> property on the html element, which is preferred to be unitless.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, adjusts line spacing using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace">setspace</a> package, e.g. 1.25, 1.5.</p> <p>For Typst output, adjusts the spacing between lines of text.</p> <h5 id="colors-5">Colors</h5> <p><code>fontcolor</code></p> <p>Sets the CSS <code>color</code> property.</p> <p><code>linkcolor</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>color</code> property on all links.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, The color used for internal links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the color for both external links and links within the document.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of internal hyperlinks using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>monobackgroundcolor</code></p> <p>Sets the CSS <code>background-color</code> property on code elements and adds extra padding.</p> <p><code>backgroundcolor</code></p> <p>Sets the CSS <code>background-color</code> property on the html element.</p> <h5 id="layout-13">Layout</h5> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>classoption</code></p> <p>For LaTeX/PDF output, the options set for the document class.</p> <p>For HTML output using KaTeX, you can render display math equations flush left using <code>classoption: fleqn</code></p> <p><code>page-layout</code></p> <p>The page layout to use for this document (<code>article</code>, <code>full</code>, or <code>custom</code>)</p> <p><code>grid</code></p> <p>Properties of the grid system used to layout Quarto HTML and Typst pages.</p> <p><code>appendix-style</code></p> <p>The layout of the appendix for this document (<code>none</code>, <code>plain</code>, or <code>default</code>).</p> <p>To completely disable any styling of the appendix, choose the appendix style <code>none</code>. For minimal styling, choose <code>plain.</code></p> <p><code>appendix-cite-as</code></p> <p>Controls the formats which are provided in the citation section of the appendix.</p> <p>Use <code>false</code> to disable the display of the ‘cite as’ appendix. Pass one or more of <code>display</code> or <code>bibtex</code> to enable that format in ‘cite as’ appendix.</p> <p><code>title-block-style</code></p> <p>The layout of the title block for this document (<code>none</code>, <code>plain</code>, or <code>default</code>).</p> <p>To completely disable any styling of the title block, choose the style <code>none</code>. For minimal styling, choose <code>plain.</code></p> <p><code>title-block-banner</code></p> <p>Applies a banner style treatment for the title block. You may specify one of the following values:</p> <p><code>true</code></p> <p>Will enable the banner style display and automatically select a background color based upon the theme.</p> <p><code><css color value></code></p> <p>If you provide a CSS color value, the banner will be enabled and the background color set to the provided CSS color.</p> <p><code><path></code></p> <p>If you provide the path to a file, the banner will be enabled and the background image will be set to the file path.</p> <p>See <code>title-block-banner-color</code> if you’d like to control the color of the title block banner text.</p> <p><code>title-block-banner-color</code></p> <p>Sets the color of text elements in a banner style title block. Use one of the following values:</p> <p><code>body</code> | <code>body-bg</code></p> <p>Will set the text color to the body text color or body background color, respectively.</p> <p><code><css color value></code></p> <p>If you provide a CSS color value, the text color will be set to the provided CSS color.</p> <p><code>title-block-categories</code></p> <p>Enables or disables the display of categories in the title block.</p> <p><code>max-width</code></p> <p>Adds a css <code>max-width</code> to the body Element.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-left</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the left margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the left margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the left page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-right</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-right</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the right margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the right margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the right page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-top</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-top</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the top margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the top margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-bottom</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the bottom margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <h5 id="code-15">Code</h5> <p><code>code-fold</code></p> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-copy</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Enable a code copy icon for code blocks.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Always show the icon</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never show the icon</li> <li><code>hover</code> (default): Show the icon when the mouse hovers over the code block <code>code-link</code></li> </ul> <p>Enables hyper-linking of functions within code blocks to their online documentation.</p> <p>Code linking is currently implemented only for the knitr engine (via the <a href="https://downlit.r-lib.org/">downlit</a> package). A limitation of downlit currently prevents code linking if <code>code-line-numbers</code> is also <code>true</code>.</p> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>code-tools</code></p> <p>Include a code tools menu (for hiding and showing code). Use <code>true</code> or <code>false</code> to enable or disable the standard code tools menu. Specify sub-properties <code>source</code>, <code>toggle</code>, and <code>caption</code> to customize the behavior and appearance of code tools.</p> <p><code>code-block-border-left</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a left border on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the border is enabled as well as the color of the border.</p> <p><code>code-block-bg</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a background color on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the background color is enabled as well as the color of the background.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <p><code>indented-code-classes</code></p> <p>Specify classes to use for all indented code blocks</p> <h5 id="execution-15">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-23">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <p><code>fig-responsive</code></p> <p>Whether to make images in this document responsive.</p> <h5 id="lightbox-figures-3">Lightbox Figures</h5> <p><code>lightbox</code></p> <p>Enable or disable lightbox treatment for images in this document. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-lightbox-figures.html">Lightbox Figures</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="tables-27">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>tbl-cap-location</code></li> </ul> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="links-1">Links</h5> <p><code>link-external-icon</code></p> <p>Show a special icon next to links that leave the current site.</p> <p><code>link-external-newwindow</code></p> <p>Open external links in a new browser window or tab (rather than navigating the current tab).</p> <p><code>link-external-filter</code></p> <p>A regular expression that can be used to determine whether a link is an internal link. For example, the following will treat links that start with <code>http://www.quarto.org/custom</code> or <code>https://www.quarto.org/custom</code> as internal links (and others will be considered external):</p> <pre><code>^(?:http:|https:)\/\/www\.quarto\.org\/custom</code></pre> <p><code>format-links</code></p> <p>Controls whether links to other rendered formats are displayed in HTML output.</p> <p>Pass <code>false</code> to disable the display of format lengths or pass a list of format names for which you’d like links to be shown.</p> <p><code>notebook-links</code></p> <p>Controls the display of links to notebooks that provided embedded content or are created from documents.</p> <p>Specify <code>false</code> to disable linking to source Notebooks. Specify <code>inline</code> to show links to source notebooks beneath the content they provide. Specify <code>global</code> to show a set of global links to source notebooks.</p> <p><code>other-links</code></p> <p>A list of links that should be displayed below the table of contents in an <code>Other Links</code> section.</p> <p><code>code-links</code></p> <p>A list of links that should be displayed below the table of contents in an <code>Code Links</code> section.</p> <p><code>notebook-view</code></p> <p>Configures the HTML viewer for notebooks that provide embedded content.</p> <p><code>notebook-preview-options</code></p> <p>Options for controlling the display and behavior of Notebook previews.</p> <p><code>canonical-url</code></p> <p>Include a canonical link tag in website pages. You may pass either <code>true</code> to automatically generate a canonical link, or pass a canonical url that you’d like to have placed in the <code>href</code> attribute of the tag.</p> <p>Canonical links can only be generated for websites with a known <code>site-url</code>.</p> <h5 id="references-20">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citations-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for citation that shows the reference information.</p> <p><code>citation-location</code></p> <p>Where citation information should be displayed (<code>document</code> or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="footnotes-15">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>footnotes-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for footnotes that shows the footnote contents.</p> <p><code>reference-location</code></p> <p>Specify location for footnotes. Also controls the location of references, if <code>reference-links</code> is set.</p> <ul> <li><code>block</code>: Place at end of current top-level block</li> <li><code>section</code>: Place at end of current section</li> <li><code>margin</code>: Place at the margin</li> <li><code>document</code>: Place at end of document</li> </ul> <h5 id="cross-references-24">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <p><code>crossrefs-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for cross references that shows the item being referenced.</p> <h5 id="citation-17">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-15">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="accessibility-1">Accessibility</h5> <p><code>axe</code></p> <p>When defined, run axe-core accessibility tests on the document.</p> <h5 id="includes-20">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>resources</code></p> <p>Path (or glob) to files to publish with this document.</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="metadata-6">Metadata</h5> <p><code>keywords</code></p> <p>List of keywords to be included in the document metadata.</p> <p><code>copyright</code></p> <p>The copyright for this document, if any.</p> <p><code>license</code></p> <p>The license for this document, if any.</p> <p>Creative Commons licenses <code>CC BY</code>, <code>CC BY-SA</code>, <code>CC BY-ND</code>, <code>CC BY-NC</code>, <code>CC BY-NC-SA</code>, and <code>CC BY-NC-ND</code> will automatically generate a license link in the document appendix. Other license text will be placed in the appendix verbatim.</p> <p><code>pagetitle</code></p> <p>Sets the title metadata for the document</p> <p><code>title-prefix</code></p> <p>Specify STRING as a prefix at the beginning of the title that appears in the HTML header (but not in the title as it appears at the beginning of the body)</p> <p><code>description-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the description metadata for the document</p> <p><code>author-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the author metadata for the document</p> <p><code>date-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the date metadata for the document</p> <h5 id="rendering-26">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>embed-resources</code></p> <p>Produce a standalone HTML file with no external dependencies, using <code>data:</code> URIs to incorporate the contents of linked scripts, stylesheets, images, and videos. The resulting file should be “self-contained,” in the sense that it needs no external files and no net access to be displayed properly by a browser. This option works only with HTML output formats, including <code>html4</code>, <code>html5</code>, <code>html+lhs</code>, <code>html5+lhs</code>, <code>s5</code>, <code>slidy</code>, <code>slideous</code>, <code>dzslides</code>, and <code>revealjs</code>. Scripts, images, and stylesheets at absolute URLs will be downloaded; those at relative URLs will be sought relative to the working directory (if the first source file is local) or relative to the base URL (if the first source file is remote). Elements with the attribute <code>data-external="1"</code> will be left alone; the documents they link to will not be incorporated in the document. Limitation: resources that are loaded dynamically through JavaScript cannot be incorporated; as a result, some advanced features (e.g. zoom or speaker notes) may not work in an offline “self-contained” <code>reveal.js</code> slide show.</p> <p><code>self-contained-math</code></p> <p>Embed math libraries (e.g. MathJax) within <code>self-contained</code> output. Note that math libraries are not embedded by default because they are quite large and often time consuming to download.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="website-4">Website</h5> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Setting this to false prevents this document from being included in searches.</p> <p><code>repo-actions</code></p> <p>Setting this to false prevents the <code>repo-actions</code> from appearing on this page. Other possible values are <code>none</code> or one or more of <code>edit</code>, <code>source</code>, and <code>issue</code>, e.g. <code>[edit, source, issue]</code>.</p> <p><code>aliases</code></p> <p>URLs that alias this document, when included in a website.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to a preview image for this content. By default, Quarto will use the image value from the site: metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an image-width and image-height to improve the appearance of your Twitter Card.</p> <p>If image is not provided, Quarto will automatically attempt to locate a preview image.</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>The height of the preview image for this document.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>The width of the preview image for this document.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for preview image on this page.</p> <p><code>image-lazy-loading</code></p> <p>Enables lazy loading for the preview image. If true, the preview image element will have <code>loading="lazy"</code>, and will only load when it comes into view.</p> <p>If false, the preview image will load immediately.</p> <h5 id="text-output-14">Text Output</h5> <p><code>strip-comments</code></p> <p>Strip out HTML comments in the Markdown source, rather than passing them on to Markdown, Textile or HTML output as raw HTML. This does not apply to HTML comments inside raw HTML blocks when the <code>markdown_in_html_blocks</code> extension is not set.</p> <p><code>ascii</code></p> <p>Use only ASCII characters in output. Currently supported for XML and HTML formats (which use entities instead of UTF-8 when this option is selected), CommonMark, gfm, and Markdown (which use entities), roff ms (which use hexadecimal escapes), and to a limited degree LaTeX (which uses standard commands for accented characters when possible). roff man output uses ASCII by default.</p> <h3 id="hugo-options">Hugo Options</h3> <h4 id="hugo-options-1">Hugo Options</h4> <p>Hugo is an open-source static website generator. To learn more about Hugo see <a href="https://gohugo.io/">gohugo.io</a>.</p> <p>See the Hugo format user guide for more details on creating Hugo output with Quarto.</p> <pre><code>format: hugo</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-16">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-18">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. To disable any special previewing features, pass <code>raw</code> as the preview-mode.</p> <h5 id="table-of-contents-20">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code-16">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-24">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-25">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-29">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-22">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="cross-references-26">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-22">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="rendering-28">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output-16">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. See the Pandoc <a href="https://pandoc.org/jats.html">JATS documentation</a> for details on <code>copyright</code> fields.</p> <p><code>article</code></p> <p>Information concerning the article that identifies or describes it. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-28">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-25">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. The hierarchy order is part, chapter, then section; all headings are shifted such that the top-level heading becomes the specified type.</p> <p>The default behavior is to determine the best division type via heuristics: unless other conditions apply, <code>section</code> is chosen. When the <code>documentclass</code> variable is set to <code>report</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>memoir</code> (unless the <code>article</code> option is specified), <code>chapter</code> is implied as the setting for this option. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, the main font family. Use the name of any system font. See <a href="https://wiki.contextgarden.net/Fonts">ConTeXt Fonts</a> for more information.</p> <p><code>fontsize</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the base CSS <code>font-size</code> property.</p> <p>For LaTeX and ConTeXt output, sets the font size for the document body text.</p> <p><code>fontenc</code></p> <p>Allows font encoding to be specified through <a href="https://www.ctan.org/pkg/fontenc"><code>fontenc</code></a> package.</p> <p>See <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/encguide">LaTeX Font Encodings Guide</a> for addition information on font encoding.</p> <p><code>fontfamily</code></p> <p>Font package to use when compiling a PDf with the <code>pdflatex</code> <code>pdf-engine</code>.</p> <p>See <a href="https://tug.org/FontCatalogue/">The LaTeX Font Catalogue</a> for a summary of font options available.</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) files, the font family for example, <code>T</code> or <code>P</code>.</p> <p><code>fontfamilyoptions</code></p> <p>Options for the package used as <code>fontfamily</code>.</p> <p>For example, to use the Libertine font with proportional lowercase (old-style) figures through the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/libertinus"><code>libertinus</code></a> package:</p> <pre><code>fontfamily: libertinus fontfamilyoptions: - osf - p</code></pre> <p><code>sansfont</code></p> <p>The sans serif font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. Takes the name of any system font, using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a> package.</p> <p><code>mathfont</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the math font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p>For example, to use the <a href="http://www.gust.org.pl/projects/e-foundry/tex-gyre">TeX Gyre</a> version of Palatino with
