href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>mathfontoptions</code></p> <p>The math font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code> allowing any options available through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec"><code>fontspec</code></a>.</p> <p><code>CJKoptions</code></p> <p>The CJK font options for use with <code>xelatex</code> or href="https://ctan.org/pkg/microtype">microtype</a> package.</p> <p><code>linestretch</code></p> <p>For HTML output sets the CSS <code>line-height</code> property on the html element, which is spacing between lines of text.</p> <h5 id="colors-6">Colors</h5> <p><code>linkcolor</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>color</code> property on all links.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, The color used for internal links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the color for both external links and links within the document.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of internal hyperlinks using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>filecolor</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the color used for external links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of external file links using Typst color syntax.</p> <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of citation links using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>urlcolor</code></p> href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p><code>colorlinks</code></p> <p>Add <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table options set for the document class.</p> <p>For HTML output using KaTeX, you can render display math equations flush left using <code>classoption: fleqn</code></p> <p><code>pagestyle</code></p> <p>Control the <code>\pagestyle{}</code> for the document.</p> <p><code>papersize</code></p> <p>The paper size for the document.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <p><code>geometry</code></p> <p>Options for the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry">geometry</a> package. For example:</p> <pre><code>geometry: - top=30mm - left=20mm - heightrounded</code></pre> <p><code>hyperrefoptions</code></p> <p>Options for the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref">hyperref</a> package. For example:</p> <pre><code>hyperrefoptions: - linktoc=all - pdfwindowui - pdfpagemode=FullScreen</code></pre> <p>To customize link colors, please see the <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/pdf.html#colors">Quarto PDF reference</a>.</p> <p><code>indent</code></p> <p>Whether to use document class settings for indentation. If the document class settings are not used, the default LaTeX template removes indentation and adds space between paragraphs</p> <p>For groff (<code>ms</code>) documents, the paragraph indent, for example, <code>2m</code>.</p> <p><code>block-headings</code></p> <p>Make <code>\paragraph</code> and <code>\subparagraph</code> (fourth- and fifth-level headings, or fifth- and sixth-level with book classes) free-standing rather than run-in; requires further formatting to distinguish from <code>\subsubsection</code> (third- or fourth-level headings). Instead of using this option, <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script">KOMA-Script</a> can adjust headings more extensively:</p> <pre><code>header-includes: | \RedeclareSectionCommand[ beforeskip=-10pt plus -2pt minus -1pt, afterskip=1sp plus -1sp minus 1sp, font=\normalfont\itshape]{paragraph} \RedeclareSectionCommand[ beforeskip=-10pt plus -2pt minus -1pt, afterskip=1sp plus -1sp minus 1sp, font=\normalfont\scshape, indent=0pt]{subparagraph}</code></pre> <h5 id="code-26">Code</h5> <p><code>code-line-numbers</code></p> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-annotations</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>code-block-border-left</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a left border on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the border is enabled as well as the color of the border.</p> <p><code>code-block-bg</code></p> <p>Specifies to apply a background color on code blocks. Provide a hex color to specify that the background color is enabled as well as the color of the background.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <p><code>listings</code></p> <p>Use the <code>listings</code> package for LaTeX code blocks. The package does not support multi-byte encoding for source code. To handle UTF-8 you would need to use a custom template. This issue is fully documented here: <a href="https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/LaTeX/Source_Code_Listings#Encoding_issue">Encoding issue with the listings package</a></p> <p><code>indented-code-classes</code></p> <p>Specify classes to use for all indented code blocks</p> <h5 id="execution-26">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-34">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-env</code></p> <p>LaTeX environment for figure output</p> <p><code>fig-pos</code></p> <p>LaTeX figure position arrangement to be used in <code>\begin{figure}[]</code>.</p> <p>Computational figure output that is accompanied by the code that produced it is given a default value of <code>fig-pos="H"</code> (so that the code and figure are not inordinately separated).</p> <p>If <code>fig-pos</code> is <code>false</code>, then we don’t use any figure position specifier, which is sometimes necessary with custom figure environments (such as <code>sidewaysfigure</code>).</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-38">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>tbl-cap-location</code></li> </ul> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-31">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>cite-method</code></p> <p>Method used to format citations (<code>citeproc</code>, <code>natbib</code>, or <code>biblatex</code>).</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>biblatexoptions</code></p> <p>A list of options for BibLaTeX.</p> <p><code>natbiboptions</code></p> <p>One or more options to provide for <code>natbib</code> when generating a bibliography.</p> <p><code>biblio-style</code></p> <p>The bibliography style to use (e.g. <code>\bibliographystyle{dinat}</code>) when using <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code>.</p> <p><code>biblio-title</code></p> <p>The bibliography title to use when using <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code>.</p> <p><code>biblio-config</code></p> <p>Controls whether to output bibliography configuration for <code>natbib</code> or <code>biblatex</code> when cite method is not <code>citeproc</code>.</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <p><code>link-citations</code></p> <p>If true, citations will be hyperlinked to the corresponding bibliography entries (for author-date and numerical styles only). Defaults to false.</p> <p><code>link-bibliography</code></p> <p>If true, DOIs, PMCIDs, PMID, and URLs in bibliographies will be rendered as hyperlinks. (If an entry contains a DOI, PMCID, PMID, or URL, but none of these fields are rendered by the style, then the title, or in the absence of a title the whole entry, will be hyperlinked.) Defaults to true.</p> <p><code>notes-after-punctuation</code></p> <p>If true (the default for note styles), Quarto (via Pandoc) will put footnote references or superscripted numerical citations after following punctuation. For example, if the source contains <code>blah blah [@jones99]</code>., the result will look like <code>blah blah.[^1]</code>, with the note moved after the period and the space collapsed.</p> <p>If false, the space will still be collapsed, but the footnote will not be moved after the punctuation. The option may also be used in numerical styles that use superscripts for citation numbers (but for these styles the default is not to move the citation).</p> <h5 id="footnotes-18">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>links-as-notes</code></p> <p>Causes links to be printed as footnotes.</p> <p><code>reference-location</code></p> <p>Specify location for footnotes. Also controls the location of references, if <code>reference-links</code> is set.</p> <ul> <li><code>block</code>: Place at end of current top-level block</li> <li><code>section</code>: Place at end of current section</li> <li><code>margin</code>: Place at the margin</li> <li><code>document</code>: Place at end of document</li> </ul> <h5 id="cross-references-35">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>shorthands</code></p> <p>Enable babel language-specific shorthands in LaTeX output. Project options are specified under the <code>project</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: default output-dir: _output</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Project type (<code>default</code>, <code>website</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>manuscript</code>)</p> <p><code>render</code></p> <p>Files to render (defaults to all files)</p> <p><code>execute-dir</code></p> <p>Control the working directory for computations.</p> <ul> <li><code>file</code>: Use the directory of the file that is currently executing.</li> <li><code>project</code>: Use the root directory of the project. <code>output-dir</code></li> </ul> <p>Output directory</p> <p><code>lib-dir</code></p> <p>HTML library (JS/CSS/etc.) directory</p> <p><code>resources</code></p> <p>Additional file resources to be copied to output directory</p> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Path to brand.yml or object with light and dark paths to brand.yml</p> <p><code>preview</code></p> <p>Options for <code>quarto preview</code> (see Preview)</p> <p><code>pre-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a pre-render step</p> <p><code>post-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a post-render step</p> <h5 id="preview-8">Preview</h5> <p>Specify options that control the behavior of <code>quarto preview</code> within the <code>preview</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: default output-dir: _output preview: port: 4200 browser: false</code></pre> <p>Available <code>preview</code> options include:</p> <p><code>port</code></p> <p>Port to listen on (defaults to random value between 3000 and 8000)</p> <p><code>host</code></p> <p>Hostname to bind to (defaults to 127.0.0.1)</p> <p><code>serve</code></p> <p>Options for external preview server (see Serve)</p> <p><code>browser</code></p> <p>Open a web browser to view the preview (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>watch-inputs</code></p> <p>Re-render input files when they change (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>navigate</code></p> <p>Navigate the browser automatically when outputs are updated (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>timeout</code></p> <p>Time (in seconds) after which to exit if there are no active clients</p> <h5 id="serve-3">Serve</h5> <p>If you are creating a project extension for another publishing system that includes its own preview server (for example, Hugo or Docusaurus) then use the <code>preview: serve</code> options to customize the behavior of the preview server.</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: default preview: serve: cmd: "hugo serve --port {port} --bind {host} --navigateToChanged" env: HUGO_RELATIVEURLS: "true" ready: "Web Server is available at"</code></pre> <p><code>cmd</code></p> <p>Serve project preview using the specified command. Interpolate the <code>--port</code> into the command using <code>{port}</code>.</p> <p><code>args</code></p> <p>Additional command line arguments for preview command.</p> <p><code>env</code></p> <p>Environment variables to set for preview command.</p> <p><code>ready</code></p> <p>Regular expression for detecting when the server is ready.</p> <p>See the <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/hugo/_extension.yml">Hugo</a> and <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/docusaurus/_extension.yml">Docusaurus</a> extension source code for example usages of <code>preview: serve</code>.</p> <h3 id="projects-7">Projects</h3> <h4 id="projects-8">Projects</h4> <p>Reference for Quarto project types and their YAML options. Project types include websites, books, and manuscripts; the Options page covers settings shared across all project types.</p> <h5 id="projects-9">Projects</h5> <ul> <li>Options</li> <li>Websites</li> <li>Books</li> <li>Manuscripts No matching items</li> </ul> <h3 id="quarto-dates-and-date-formatting">Quarto Dates and Date Formatting</h3> <h4 id="quarto-dates-and-date-formatting-1">Quarto Dates and Date Formatting</h4> <h5 id="date-parsing">Date Parsing</h5> <p>When you write a date for Quarto document, Quarto will attempt to parse a date string by trying a number of standard forms before ultimately attempting to infer the date format. Quarto will try dates formatted as follows, in the following order:</p> <ul> <li><code>MM/dd/yyyy</code></li> <li><code>MM-dd-yyyy</code></li> <li><code>MM/dd/yy</code></li> <li><code>MM-dd-yy</code></li> <li><code>yyyy-MM-dd</code></li> <li><code>dd MM yyyy</code></li> <li><code>MM dd, yyyy</code></li> <li><code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ</code> In addition, you may also provide date keywords, which will provide a dynamic date.</li> </ul> <p>Keyword</p> <p>Date</p> <p><code>today</code></p> <p>The current local date, with the time portion set to 0.</p> <p><code>now</code></p> <p>The current local date and time.</p> <p><code>last-modified</code></p> <p>The last modified date and time of the input file containing the date.</p> <h5 id="date-formatting">Date Formatting</h5> <p>When specifying a date format in Quarto, there are two ways to represent the format that you’d like.</p> <h6 id="using-a-date-style">Using a Date Style</h6> <p>You can specify a simple date style which will be used to format the date.</p> <p>For example:</p> <pre><code>--- date: 03/07/2005 date-format: long ---</code></pre> <p>Valid styles and examples of the formatted output are as follows:</p> <p>Style</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Example</p> <p><code>full</code></p> <p>A full date that includes the weekday name</p> <p>Monday, March 7, 2005</p> <p><code>long</code></p> <p>A long date that includes a wide month name</p> <p>March 7, 2005</p> <p><code>medium</code></p> <p>A medium date</p> <p>Mar 7, 2005</p> <p><code>short</code></p> <p>A short date with a numeric month</p> <p>3/7/05</p> <p><code>iso</code></p> <p>A short date in ISO format</p> <p>2005-03-07</p> <h6 id="using-a-date-format">Using a Date Format</h6> <p>You can also specify a date format string that will be used to format the date. For example:</p> <pre><code>--- date: 03/07/2005 date-format: "MMM D, YYYY"</code></pre> <p>The permissible values in this string include:</p> <p>Format String</p> <p>Output</p> <p>Description</p> <p><code>YY</code></p> <p>18</p> <p>Two-digit year</p> <p><code>YYYY</code></p> <p>2018</p> <p>Four-digit year</p> <p><code>M</code></p> <p>1-12</p> <p>The month, beginning at 1</p> <p><code>MM</code></p> <p>01-12</p> <p>The month, 2-digits</p> <p><code>MMM</code></p> <p>Jan-Dec</p> <p>The abbreviated month name</p> <p><code>MMMM</code></p> <p>January-December</p> <p>The full month name</p> <p><code>D</code></p> <p>1-31</p> <p>The day of the month</p> <p><code>DD</code></p> <p>01-31</p> <p>The day of the month, 2-digits</p> <p><code>d</code></p> <p>0-6</p> <p>The day of the week, with Sunday as 0</p> <p><code>dd</code></p> <p>Su-Sa</p> <p>The min name of the day of the week</p> <p><code>ddd</code></p> <p>Sun-Sat</p> <p>The short name of the day of the week</p> <p><code>dddd</code></p> <p>Sunday-Saturday</p> <p>The name of the day of the week</p> <p><code>H</code></p> <p>0-23</p> <p>The hour</p> <p><code>HH</code></p> <p>00-23</p> <p>The hour, 2-digits</p> <p><code>h</code></p> <p>1-12</p> <p>The hour, 12-hour clock</p> <p><code>hh</code></p> <p>01-12</p> <p>The hour, 12-hour clock, 2-digits</p> <p><code>m</code></p> <p>0-59</p> <p>The minute</p> <p><code>mm</code></p> <p>00-59</p> <p>The minute, 2-digits</p> <p><code>s</code></p> <p>0-59</p> <p>The second</p> <p><code>ss</code></p> <p>00-59</p> <p>The second, 2-digits</p> <p><code>SSS</code></p> <p>000-999</p> <p>The millisecond, 3-digits</p> <p><code>Z</code></p> <p>+05:00</p> <p>The offset from UTC, ±HH:mm</p> <p><code>ZZ</code></p> <p>+0500</p> <p>The offset from UTC, ±HHmm</p> <p><code>A</code></p> <p>AM PM</p> <p><code>a</code></p> <p>am pm</p> <p><code>Q</code></p> <p>1-4</p> <p>Quarter</p> <p><code>Do</code></p> <p>1st 2nd … 31st</p> <p>Day of Month with ordinal</p> <p><code>k</code></p> <p>1-24</p> <p>The hour, beginning at 1</p> <p><code>kk</code></p> <p>01-24</p> <p>The hour, 2-digits, beginning at 1</p> <p><code>X</code></p> <p>1360013296</p> <p>Unix Timestamp in second</p> <p><code>x</code></p> <p>1360013296123</p> <p>Unix Timestamp in millisecond</p> <p><code>w</code></p> <p>1 2 … 52 53</p> <p>Week of year ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/week-of-year"><code>WeekOfYear</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>ww</code></p> <p>01 02 … 52 53</p> <p>Week of year, 2-digits ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/week-of-year"><code>WeekOfYear</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>W</code></p> <p>1 2 … 52 53</p> <p>ISO Week of year ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/iso-week"><code>IsoWeek</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>WW</code></p> <p>01 02 … 52 53</p> <p>ISO Week of year, 2-digits ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/iso-week"><code>IsoWeek</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>wo</code></p> <p>1st 2nd … 52nd 53rd</p> <p>Week of year with ordinal ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/week-of-year"><code>WeekOfYear</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>gggg</code></p> <p>2017</p> <p>Week Year ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/week-year"><code>WeekYear</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>GGGG</code></p> <p>2017</p> <p>ISO Week Year ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/iso-week"><code>IsoWeek</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>z</code></p> <p>EST</p> <p>Abbreviated named offset ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/timezone"><code>Timezone</code></a> plugin )</p> <p><code>zzz</code></p> <p>Eastern Standard Time</p> <p>Unabbreviated named offset ( dependent <a href="https://day.js.org/docs/en/plugin/timezone"><code>Timezone</code></a>plugin )</p> <p>To escape characters, wrap them in square brackets (e.g. <code>[MM]</code>).</p> <p>Example formats and outputs include:</p> <p>Format</p> <p>Output</p> <p><code>MMM D, YYYY</code></p> <p>Mar 7, 2005</p> <p><code>DD/MM/YYYY</code></p> <p>07/03/2005</p> <p><code>[YYYYescape] YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ[Z]</code></p> <p>YYYYescape 2005-03-07T00:00:00-05:00Z</p> <p><code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ</code></p> <p>2005-03-07T00:00:00-05:00</p> <p><code>dddd MMM D, YYYY</code></p> <p>Monday Mar 7, 2005</p> <h3 id="quarto-glob-syntax">Quarto Glob Syntax</h3> <h4 id="quarto-glob-syntax-1">Quarto Glob Syntax</h4> <h5 id="overview-122">Overview</h5> <p>Quarto sometimes allows you to provide a path or paths using glob syntax, providing wildcard expansion and other behavior that makes it simple to match a list of files without having to specify each file individually. Globs may be used:</p> <ul> <li>When specifying render targets in Quarto projects (see Render Targets).</li> <li>When defining resources for Quarto websites (see Site Resources).</li> <li>When defining documents to include in a listing (see Listing Contents).</li> <li>When automatically creating navigation for sidebars (see Auto Navigation).</li> </ul> <h5 id="glob-syntax">Glob Syntax</h5> <p>The below is a general reference of the syntax used for globs in Quarto. Note that globs match the filesystem recursively. If you prefer that they don’t, then prefix the pattern with a <code>/</code> (for example, use <code>/*.qmd</code> rather than <code>*.qmd</code>).</p> <ul> <li><code>*</code> - Matches everything.</li> <li><code>{foo,bar}</code> - Matches <code>foo</code> or <code>bar</code>.</li> <li><code>[abcd]</code> - Matches <code>a</code>, <code>b</code>, <code>c</code> or <code>d</code>.</li> <li><code>[a-d]</code> - Matches <code>a</code>, <code>b</code>, <code>c</code> or <code>d</code>.</li> <li><code>[!abcd]</code> - Matches any single character besides <code>a</code>, <code>b</code>, <code>c</code> or <code>d</code>.</li> <li><code>[[:<class>:]]</code> - Matches any character belonging to <code><class></code>. <ul> <li><code>[[:alnum:]]</code> - Matches any digit or letter.</li> <li><code>[[:digit:]abc]</code> - Matches any digit, <code>a</code>, <code>b</code> or <code>c</code>.</li> <li>See <a href="https://facelessuser.github.io/wcmatch/glob/#posix-character-classes">facelessuser.github.io</a> for a complete list of supported character classes.</li> </ul></li> <li><code>\</code> - Escapes the next character for an <code>os</code> other than <code>"windows"</code>.</li> <li><code>- Escapes the next character for</code>os<code>set to</code>“windows”`.</li> <li><code>/</code> - Path separator.</li> <li><code>\</code> - Additional path separator only for <code>os</code> set to <code>"windows"</code>.</li> <li><code>?(foo|bar)</code> - Matches 0 or 1 instance of <code>{foo,bar}</code>.</li> <li><code>@(foo|bar)</code> - Matches 1 instance of <code>{foo,bar}</code>. They behave the same.</li> <li><code>*(foo|bar)</code> - Matches n instances of <code>{foo,bar}</code>.</li> <li><code>+(foo|bar)</code> - Matches n > 0 instances of <code>{foo,bar}</code>.</li> <li><code>!(foo|bar)</code> - Matches anything other than <code>{foo,bar}</code>.</li> <li><code>**</code> - Matches any number of any path segments. <ul> <li>Must comprise its entire path segment in the provided glob.</li> <li>See <a href="https://www.linuxjournal.com/content/globstar-new-bash-globbing-option">linuxjournal.com</a>.</li> </ul></li> </ul> <h3 id="reference-1">Reference</h3> <h4 id="reference-2">Reference</h4> <p>Options reference for formats, code cells, and projects. See the user guide for more in-depth documentation on usage.</p> <h5 id="documents-3">Documents</h5> <ul> <li>HTML</li> <li>PDF</li> <li>MS Word</li> <li>Typst</li> <li>Open Office</li> <li>ePub</li> </ul> <h5 id="presentations-5">Presentations</h5> <ul> <li>Revealjs</li> <li>PowerPoint</li> <li>Beamer</li> </ul> <h5 id="markdown-3">Markdown</h5> <ul> <li>GitHub</li> <li>CommonMark</li> <li>Hugo</li> <li>Markua</li> </ul> <h5 id="wikis-2">Wikis</h5> <ul> <li>MediaWiki</li> <li>Jira Wiki</li> <li>DokuWiki</li> <li>ZimWiki</li> <li>XWiki</li> </ul> <h5 id="code-cells-4">Code Cells</h5> <ul> <li>Jupyter</li> <li>Knitr</li> <li>Observable JS</li> </ul> <h5 id="projects-10">Projects</h5> <ul> <li>Options</li> <li>Websites</li> <li>Books</li> <li>Manuscripts</li> </ul> <h5 id="metadata-12">Metadata</h5> <ul> <li>Dates</li> <li>Globs</li> <li>Citations</li> <li>Cross-References</li> <li>Brand</li> </ul> <h5 id="command-line-4">Command Line</h5> <ul> <li><code>quarto render</code></li> <li><code>quarto preview</code></li> <li><code>quarto create</code></li> <li><code>quarto publish</code></li> <li><code>quarto check</code> No matching items</li> </ul> <h3 id="restructuredtext-options">reStructuredText Options</h3> <h4 id="restructuredtext-options-1">reStructuredText Options</h4> <p>reStructuredText is an easy-to-read, what-you-see-is-what-you-get plaintext markup syntax and parser system. It is useful for in-line program documentation (such as Python docstrings), for quickly creating simple web pages, and for standalone documents. You can learn more about reStructuredText at <a href="https://docutils.sourceforge.io/rst.html">docutils.sourceforge.io</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: rst</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-28">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-30">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-31">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-29">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="formatting-4">Formatting</h5> <p><code>list-tables</code></p> <p>If true, tables are formatted as RST list tables.</p> <h5 id="code-28">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <h5 id="execution-28">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-36">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-40">Tables</h5> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-33">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. <p><code>max-width</code></p> <p>Adds a css <code>max-width</code> to the body Element.</p> <p><code>margin-left</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-left</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the left margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the left margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the left page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-right</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-right</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the right margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the right margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the right page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-top</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-top</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the top margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the top margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the top page margin.</p> <p><code>margin-bottom</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the <code>margin-bottom</code> property on the Body element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, sets the bottom margin if <code>geometry</code> is not used (otherwise <code>geometry</code> overrides this value)</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the bottom margin if <code>layout</code> is not used, otherwise <code>layout</code> overrides these.</p> <p>For <code>wkhtmltopdf</code> sets the bottom page margin.</p> <p><code>margin</code></p> <p>For <code>revealjs</code>, the factor of the display size that should remain empty around the content (e.g. 0.1).</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, a dictionary specifying page margins. Use <code>x</code> and <code>y</code> for symmetric horizontal/vertical margins, or <code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code> for individual sides. Values should include units (e.g. <code>1.5in</code>, <code>2cm</code>).</p> <h5 id="code-29">Code</h5> <p><code>code-fold</code></p> <p>Collapse code into an HTML <code><details></code> tag so the user can display it on-demand.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: collapse code</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): do not collapse code</li> <li><code>show</code>: use the <code><details></code> tag, but show the expanded code initially. <code>code-summary</code></li> </ul> <p>Summary text to use for code blocks collapsed using <code>code-fold</code></p> <p><code>code-overflow</code></p> <p>Choose how to handle code overflow, when code lines are too wide for their container. One of:</p> <ul> <li><code>scroll</code></li> <li><code>wrap</code> <code>code-line-numbers</code></li> </ul> <p>Include line numbers in code block output (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code>).</p> <p>For revealjs output only, you can also specify a string to highlight specific lines (and/or animate between sets of highlighted lines).</p> <ul> <li>Sets of lines are denoted with commas: <ul> <li><code>3,4,5</code></li> <li><code>1,10,12</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Ranges can be denoted with dashes and combined with commas: <ul> <li><code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>5-10,12,14</code></li> </ul></li> <li>Finally, animation steps are separated by <code>|</code>: <ul> <li><code>1-3|1-3,5</code> first shows <code>1-3</code>, then <code>1-3,5</code></li> <li><code>|5|5-10,12</code> first shows no numbering, then 5, then lines 5-10 and 12 <code>code-copy</code></li> </ul></li> </ul> <p>Enable a code copy icon for code blocks.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Always show the icon</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never show the icon</li> <li><code>hover</code> (default): Show the icon when the mouse hovers over the code block <code>code-link</code></li> </ul> <p>Enables hyper-linking of functions within code blocks to their online documentation.</p> <p>Code linking is currently implemented only for the knitr engine (via the <a href="https://downlit.r-lib.org/">downlit</a> package). For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-37">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-align</code></p> <p>Figure horizontal alignment (<code>default</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <p><code>fig-responsive</code></p> <p>Whether to make images in this document responsive.</p> <h5 id="tables-41">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-colwidths</code></p> <p>Apply explicit table column widths for markdown grid tables and pipe tables that are more than <code>columns</code> characters wide (72 by default).</p> <p>Some formats (e.g. HTML) do an excellent job automatically sizing table columns and so don’t benefit much from column width specifications. Other formats (e.g. LaTeX) require table column sizes in order to correctly flow longer cell content (this is a major reason why tables > 72 columns wide are assigned explicit widths by Pandoc).</p> <p>This can be specified as:</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code>: Apply markdown table column widths except when there is a hyperlink in the table (which tends to throw off automatic calculation of column widths based on the markdown text width of cells). (<code>auto</code> is the default for HTML output formats)</li> <li><code>true</code>: Always apply markdown table widths (<code>true</code> is the default for all non-HTML formats)</li> <li><code>false</code>: Never apply markdown table widths.</li> <li>An array of numbers (e.g. <code>[40, 30, 30]</code>): Array of explicit width percentages. <code>tbl-cap-location</code></li> </ul> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citations-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for citation that shows the reference information.</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <p><code>crossrefs-hover</code></p> <p>Enables a hover popup for cross references that shows the item being referenced.</p> <h5 id="citation-31">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-29">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="accessibility-2">Accessibility</h5> <p><code>axe</code></p> <p>When defined, run axe-core accessibility tests on the document.</p> <h5 id="includes-34">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>resources</code></p> <p>Path (or glob) to files to publish with this document.</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="metadata-13">Metadata</h5> <p><code>keywords</code></p> <p>List of keywords to be included in the document metadata.</p> <p><code>pagetitle</code></p> <p>Sets the title metadata for the document</p> <p><code>title-prefix</code></p> <p>Specify STRING as a prefix at the beginning of the title that appears in the HTML header (but not in the title as it appears at the beginning of the body)</p> <p><code>description-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the description metadata for the document</p> <p><code>author-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the author metadata for the document</p> <p><code>date-meta</code></p> <p>Sets the date metadata for the document</p> <h5 id="rendering-40">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>embed-resources</code></p> <p>Produce a standalone HTML file with no external dependencies, using <code>data:</code> URIs to incorporate the contents of linked scripts, stylesheets, images, and videos. The resulting file should be “self-contained,” in the sense that it needs no external files and no net access to be displayed properly by a browser. This option works only with HTML output formats, including <code>html4</code>, <code>html5</code>, <code>html+lhs</code>, <code>html5+lhs</code>, <code>s5</code>, <code>slidy</code>, <code>slideous</code>, <code>dzslides</code>, and <code>revealjs</code>. Scripts, images, and stylesheets at absolute URLs will be downloaded; those at relative URLs will be sought relative to the working directory (if the first source file is local) or relative to the base URL (if the first source file is remote). Elements with the attribute <code>data-external="1"</code> will be left alone; the documents they link to will not be incorporated in the document. Limitation: resources that are loaded dynamically through JavaScript cannot be incorporated; as a result, some advanced features (e.g. zoom or speaker notes) may not work in an offline “self-contained” <code>reveal.js</code> slide show.</p> <p><code>self-contained-math</code></p> <p>Embed math libraries (e.g. MathJax) within <code>self-contained</code> output. Note that math libraries are not embedded by default because they are quite large and often time consuming to download.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <h5 id="text-output-25">Text Output</h5> <p><code>strip-comments</code></p> <p>Strip out HTML comments in the Markdown source, rather than passing them on to Markdown, Textile or HTML output as raw HTML. This does not apply to HTML comments inside raw HTML blocks when the <code>markdown_in_html_blocks</code> extension is not set.</p> <p><code>ascii</code></p> <p>Use only ASCII characters in output. Currently supported for XML and HTML formats (which use entities instead of UTF-8 when this option is selected), CommonMark, gfm, and Markdown (which use entities), roff ms (which use hexadecimal escapes), and to a limited degree LaTeX (which uses standard commands for accented characters when possible). roff man output uses ASCII by default.</p> <h5 id="library">Library</h5> <p><code>revealjs-url</code></p> <p>Directory containing reveal.js files.</p> <h3 id="rtf-options">RTF Options</h3> <h4 id="rtf-options-1">RTF Options</h4> <p>The Rich Text Format (RTF) is a proprietary document file format with published specification developed by Microsoft Corporation from 1987 until 2008 for cross-platform document interchange with Microsoft products. Learn more about RTF at <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Text_Format">en.wikipedia.org</a>.</p> <pre><code>format: rtf</code></pre> <h5 id="title-author-30">Title & Author</h5> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Document title</p> <p><code>date</code></p> <p>Document date</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>Date format for the document</p> <p><code>author</code></p> <p>Author or authors of the document</p> <p><code>order</code></p> <p>Order for document when included in a website automatic sidebar menu.</p> <h5 id="format-options-32">Format Options</h5> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Branding information to use for this document. If a string, the path to a brand file. If false, don’t use branding on this document. If an object, an inline brand definition, or an object with light and dark brand paths or definitions.</p> <p><code>quarto-required</code></p> <p>A semver version range describing the supported quarto versions for this document or project.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <ul> <li><code>>= 1.1.0</code>: Require at least quarto version 1.1</li> <li><code>1.*</code>: Require any quarto versions whose major version number is 1</li> </ul> <h5 id="table-of-contents-33">Table of Contents</h5> <p><code>toc</code></p> <p>Include an automatically generated table of contents (or, in the case of <code>latex</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>docx</code>, <code>odt</code>, <code>opendocument</code>, <code>rst</code>, or <code>ms</code>, an instruction to create one) in the output document.</p> <p>Note that if you are producing a PDF via <code>ms</code>, the table of contents will appear at the beginning of the document, before the title. If you would prefer it to be at the end of the document, use the option <code>pdf-engine-opt: --no-toc-relocation</code>.</p> <p><code>toc-depth</code></p> <p>Specify the number of section levels to include in the table of contents. The default is 3</p> <h5 id="numbering-34">Numbering</h5> <p><code>number-sections</code></p> <p>Number section headings rendered output. By default, sections are not numbered. Sections with class <code>.unnumbered</code> will never be numbered, even if <code>number-sections</code> is specified.</p> <p><code>shift-heading-level-by</code></p> <p>Shift heading levels by a positive or negative integer. For example, with <code>shift-heading-level-by: -1</code>, level 2 headings become level 1 headings, and level 3 headings become level 2 headings. Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <h5 id="code-33">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-41">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; Headings cannot have a level less than 1, so a heading that would be shifted below level 1 becomes a regular paragraph. Exception: with a shift of -N, a level-N heading at the beginning of the document replaces the metadata title.</p> <p><code>page-numbering</code></p> <p>Schema to use for numbering pages, e.g. <code>1</code> or <code>i</code>, or <code>false</code> to omit page numbering.</p> <p>See <a href="https://typst.app/docs/reference/model/numbering/">Typst Numbering</a> for additional information.</p> <h5 id="fonts-9">Fonts</h5> <p><code>mainfont</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>font-family</code> on the HTML element.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, the main font family for use with <code>xelatex</code> or <code>lualatex</code>. property on the html element, which is preferred to be unitless.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, adjusts line spacing using the <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace">setspace</a> package, e.g. 1.25, 1.5.</p> <p>For Typst output, adjusts the spacing between lines of text.</p> <h5 id="colors-7">Colors</h5> <p><code>linkcolor</code></p> <p>For HTML output, sets the CSS <code>color</code> property on all links.</p> <p>For LaTeX output, The color used for internal links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For ConTeXt output, sets the color for both external links and links within the document.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of internal hyperlinks using Typst color syntax.</p> <p><code>filecolor</code></p> <p>For LaTeX output, the color used for external links using color options allowed by <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of href="https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor"><code>xcolor</code></a>, including the <code>dvipsnames</code>, <code>svgnames</code>, and <code>x11names</code> lists.</p> <p>For Typst output, sets the color of citation links using Typst color syntax.</p> <h5 id="layout-18">Layout</h5> <p><code>cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure and table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>papersize</code></p> <p>The paper size for the document.</p> <p><code>brand-mode</code></p> <p>The brand mode to use for rendering the document, <code>light</code> or <code>dark</code>.</p> <p><code>grid</code></p> <p>Properties of the grid system used to layout Quarto HTML and Typst pages.</p> <p><code>margin</code></p> <p>For <code>revealjs</code>, the factor of the display size that should remain empty around the content (e.g. 0.1).</p> <p>For
