Values should include units (e.g. <code>1.5in</code>, <code>2cm</code>).</p> <h5 id="code-34">Code</h5> <p><code>code-annotations</code></p> <p>The style to use when displaying code annotations. Set this value to false to hide code annotations.</p> <p><code>syntax-highlighting</code></p> <p>Specifies the coloring style to be used in highlighted source code.</p> <p>Valid values:</p> <ul> <li><code>none</code>: Disables syntax highlighting for code blocks.</li> <li><code>idiomatic</code>: Uses the format’s native syntax highlighter (e.g., Typst’s built-in highlighting, LaTeX <code>listings</code> package, or reveal.js highlight.js plugin).</li> <li>A style name (e.g., <code>pygments</code>, <code>tango</code>, <code>github</code>): Uses Pandoc’s skylighting with the specified theme.</li> <li>A path to a <code>.theme</code> file: Uses a custom KDE syntax highlighting theme. For adaptive light/dark themes, specify an object with <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> properties pointing to theme files.</li> </ul> <p><code>syntax-definitions</code></p> <p>KDE language syntax definition files (XML)</p> <h5 id="execution-34">Execution</h5> <p>Execution options should be specified within the <code>execute</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>execute: echo: false warning: false</code></pre> <p><code>eval</code></p> <p>Evaluate code cells (if <code>false</code> just echos the code into output).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default): evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>false</code>: don’t evaluate code cell</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative numbers to selectively include or exclude expressions (explicit inclusion/exclusion of expressions is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>echo</code></li> </ul> <p>Include cell source code in rendered output.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code> (default in most formats): include source code in output</li> <li><code>false</code> (default in presentation formats like <code>beamer</code>, <code>revealjs</code>, and <code>pptx</code>): do not include source code in output</li> <li><code>fenced</code>: in addition to echoing, include the cell delimiter as part of the output.</li> <li><code>[...]</code>: A list of positive or negative line numbers to selectively include or exclude lines (explicit inclusion/excusion of lines is available only when using the knitr engine) <code>output</code></li> </ul> <p>Include the results of executing the code in the output. Possible values:</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Include results.</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not include results.</li> <li><code>asis</code>: Treat output as raw markdown with no enclosing containers. <code>warning</code></li> </ul> <p>Include warnings in rendered output.</p> <p><code>error</code></p> <p>Include errors in the output (note that this implies that errors executing code will not halt processing of the document).</p> <p><code>include</code></p> <p>Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included in output.</p> <p><code>cache</code></p> <p>Cache results of computations (using the <a href="https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/cache/">knitr cache</a> for R documents, and <a href="https://jupyter-cache.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">Jupyter Cache</a> for Jupyter documents).</p> <p>Note that cache invalidation is triggered by changes in chunk source code (or other cache attributes you’ve defined).</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Cache results</li> <li><code>false</code>: Do not cache results</li> <li><code>refresh</code>: Force a refresh of the cache even if has not been otherwise invalidated. <code>freeze</code></li> </ul> <p>Control the re-use of previous computational output when rendering.</p> <ul> <li><code>true</code>: Never recompute previously generated computational output during a global project render</li> <li><code>false</code> (default): Recompute previously generated computational output</li> <li><code>auto</code>: Re-compute previously generated computational output only in case their source file changes</li> </ul> <h5 id="figures-42">Figures</h5> <p><code>fig-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place figure captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-width</code></p> <p>Default width for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-height</code></p> <p>Default height for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-format</code></p> <p>Default format for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics (<code>retina</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>jpeg</code>, <code>svg</code>, or <code>pdf</code>)</p> <p><code>fig-dpi</code></p> <p>Default DPI for figures generated by Matplotlib or R graphics.</p> <p>Note that with the Jupyter engine, this option has no effect when provided at the cell level; it can only be provided with document or project metadata.</p> <p><code>fig-asp</code></p> <p>The aspect ratio of the plot, i.e., the ratio of height/width. When <code>fig-asp</code> is specified, the height of a plot (the option <code>fig-height</code>) is calculated from <code>fig-width * fig-asp</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fig-asp</code> option is only available within the knitr engine.</p> <h5 id="tables-46">Tables</h5> <p><code>tbl-cap-location</code></p> <p>Where to place table captions (<code>top</code>, <code>bottom</code>, or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>df-print</code></p> <p>Method used to print tables in Knitr engine documents:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: Use the default S3 method for the data frame.</li> <li><code>kable</code>: Markdown table using the <code>knitr::kable()</code> function.</li> <li><code>tibble</code>: Plain text table using the <code>tibble</code> package.</li> <li><code>paged</code>: HTML table with paging for row and column overflow. The default printing method is <code>kable</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-39">References</h5> <p><code>bibliography</code></p> <p>Document bibliography (BibTeX or CSL). May be a single file or a list of files</p> <p><code>csl</code></p> <p>Citation Style Language file to use for formatting references.</p> <p><code>citation-location</code></p> <p>Where citation information should be displayed (<code>document</code> or <code>margin</code>)</p> <p><code>citeproc</code></p> <p>Turn on built-in citation processing. To use this feature, you will need to have a document containing citations and a source of bibliographic data: either an external bibliography file or a list of <code>references</code> in the document’s YAML metadata. You can optionally also include a <code>csl</code> citation style file.</p> <p><code>bibliographystyle</code></p> <p>The bibliography style to use (e.g. <code>#set bibliography(style: "apa")</code>) when using typst built-in citation system (e.g when not <code>citeproc: true</code>).</p> <p><code>citation-abbreviations</code></p> <p>JSON file containing abbreviations of journals that should be used in formatted bibliographies when <code>form="short"</code> is specified. The format of the file can be illustrated with an example:</p> <pre><code>{ "default": { "container-title": { "Lloyd's Law Reports": "Lloyd's Rep", "Estates Gazette": "EG", "Scots Law Times": "SLT" } } }</code></pre> <h5 id="footnotes-20">Footnotes</h5> <p><code>reference-location</code></p> <p>Specify location for footnotes. Also controls the location of references, if <code>reference-links</code> is set.</p> <ul> <li><code>block</code>: Place at end of current top-level block</li> <li><code>section</code>: Place at end of current section</li> <li><code>margin</code>: Place at the margin</li> <li><code>document</code>: Place at end of document</li> </ul> <h5 id="cross-references-43">Cross-References</h5> <p><code>crossref</code></p> <p>Configuration for cross-reference labels and prefixes. See <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/crossref.html">Cross-Reference Options</a> for more details.</p> <h5 id="citation-36">Citation</h5> <p><code>citation</code></p> <p>Citation information for the document itself specified as <a href="https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html">CSL</a> YAML in the document front matter.</p> <p>For more on supported options, see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/metadata/citation.html">Citation Metadata</a>.</p> <h5 id="language-34">Language</h5> <p><code>lang</code></p> <p>Identifies the main language of the document using IETF language tags (following the <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47">BCP 47</a> standard), such as <code>en</code> or <code>en-GB</code>. The <a href="https://r12a.github.io/app-subtags/">Language subtag lookup</a> tool can look up or verify these tags.</p> <p>This affects most formats, and controls hyphenation in PDF output when using LaTeX (through <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/babel"><code>babel</code></a> and <a href="https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia"><code>polyglossia</code></a>) or ConTeXt.</p> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>YAML file containing custom language translations</p> <p><code>dir</code></p> <p>The base script direction for the document (<code>rtl</code> or <code>ltr</code>).</p> <p>For bidirectional documents, native pandoc <code>span</code>s and <code>div</code>s with the <code>dir</code> attribute can be used to override the base direction in some output formats. This may not always be necessary if the final renderer (e.g. the browser, when generating HTML) supports the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm].</p> <p>When using LaTeX for bidirectional documents, only the <code>xelatex</code> engine is fully supported (use <code>--pdf-engine=xelatex</code>).</p> <h5 id="includes-39">Includes</h5> <p><code>include-before-body</code></p> <p>Include contents at the beginning of the document body (e.g. after the <code><body></code> tag in HTML, or the <code>\begin{document}</code> command in LaTeX).</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-after-body</code></p> <p>Include content at the end of the document body immediately after the markdown content. While it will be included before the closing <code></body></code> tag in HTML and the <code>\end{document}</code> command in LaTeX, this option refers to the end of the markdown content.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>include-in-header</code></p> <p>Include contents at the end of the header. This can be used, for example, to include special CSS or JavaScript in HTML documents.</p> <p>A string value or an object with key “file” indicates a filename whose contents are to be included</p> <p>An object with key “text” indicates textual content to be included</p> <p><code>metadata-files</code></p> <p>Read metadata from the supplied YAML (or JSON) files. This option can be used with every input format, but string scalars in the YAML file will always be parsed as Markdown. Generally, the input will be handled the same as in YAML metadata blocks. Values in files specified later in the list will be preferred over those specified earlier. Metadata values specified inside the document, or by using <code>-M</code>, overwrite values specified with this option.</p> <h5 id="rendering-45">Rendering</h5> <p><code>from</code></p> <p>Format to read from. Extensions can be individually enabled or disabled by appending +EXTENSION or -EXTENSION to the format name (e.g. markdown+emoji).</p> <p><code>output-file</code></p> <p>Output file to write to</p> <p><code>output-ext</code></p> <p>Extension to use for generated output file</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>Use the specified file as a custom template for the generated document.</p> <p><code>template-partials</code></p> <p>Include the specified files as partials accessible to the template for the generated content.</p> <p><code>filters</code></p> <p>Specify executables or Lua scripts to be used as a filter transforming the pandoc AST after the input is parsed and before the output is written.</p> <p><code>shortcodes</code></p> <p>Specify Lua scripts that implement shortcode handlers</p> <p><code>keep-md</code></p> <p>Keep the markdown file generated by executing code</p> <p><code>keep-ipynb</code></p> <p>Keep the notebook file generated from executing code.</p> <p><code>ipynb-filters</code></p> <p>Filters to pre-process ipynb files before rendering to markdown</p> <p><code>ipynb-shell-interactivity</code></p> <p>Specify which nodes should be run interactively (displaying output from expressions)</p> <p><code>plotly-connected</code></p> <p>If true, use the “notebook_connected” plotly renderer, which downloads its dependencies from a CDN and requires an internet connection to view.</p> <p><code>keep-typ</code></p> <p>Keep the intermediate typst file used during render.</p> <p><code>extract-media</code></p> <p>Extract images and other media contained in or linked from the source document to the path DIR, creating it if necessary, and adjust the images references in the document so they point to the extracted files. Media are downloaded, read from the file system, or extracted from a binary container (e.g. docx), as needed. The original file paths are used if they are relative paths not containing … Otherwise filenames are constructed from the SHA1 hash of the contents.</p> <p><code>resource-path</code></p> <p>List of paths to search for images and other resources.</p> <p><code>default-image-extension</code></p> <p>Specify a default extension to use when image paths/URLs have no extension. This allows you to use the same source for formats that require different kinds of images. Currently this option only affects the Markdown and LaTeX readers.</p> <p><code>abbreviations</code></p> <p>Specifies a custom abbreviations file, with abbreviations one to a line. This list is used when reading Markdown input: strings found in this list will be followed by a nonbreaking space, and the period will not produce sentence-ending space in formats like LaTeX. The strings may not contain spaces.</p> <p><code>dpi</code></p> <p>Specify the default dpi (dots per inch) value for conversion from pixels to inch/ centimeters and vice versa. (Technically, the correct term would be ppi: pixels per inch.) The default is <code>96</code>. When images contain information about dpi internally, the encoded value is used instead of the default specified by this option.</p> <p><code>html-table-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, do not process tables in HTML input.</p> <p><code>html-pre-tag-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>none</code>, ignore any divs with <code>html-pre-tag-processing=parse</code> enabled.</p> <p><code>css-property-processing</code></p> <p>If <code>translate</code>, translate CSS properties into output format properties. If <code>none</code>, do not process css properties.</p> <h5 id="pdfa-3">PDF/A</h5> <p><code>pdf-standard</code></p> <p>Specifies PDF conformance standards and/or version for the output.</p> <p>Accepts a single value or array of values:</p> <p>PDF versions (both Typst and LaTeX): <code>1.4</code>, <code>1.5</code>, <code>1.6</code>, <code>1.7</code>, <code>2.0</code></p> <p>PDF/A standards (both engines): <code>a-1b</code>, <code>a-2a</code>, <code>a-2b</code>, <code>a-2u</code>, <code>a-3a</code>, <code>a-3b</code>, <code>a-3u</code>, <code>a-4</code>, <code>a-4f</code></p> <p>PDF/A standards (Typst only): <code>a-1a</code>, <code>a-4e</code></p> <p>PDF/UA standards: <code>ua-1</code> (Typst), <code>ua-2</code> (LaTeX)</p> <p>PDF/X standards (LaTeX only): <code>x-4</code>, <code>x-4p</code>, <code>x-5g</code>, <code>x-5n</code>, <code>x-5pg</code>, <code>x-6</code>, <code>x-6n</code>, <code>x-6p</code></p> <p>Example: <code>pdf-standard: [a-2b, ua-2]</code> for accessible archival PDF.</p> <h5 id="text-output-30">Text Output</h5> <p><code>wrap</code></p> <p>Determine how text is wrapped in the output (the source code, not the rendered version).</p> <ul> <li><code>auto</code> (default): Pandoc will attempt to wrap lines to the column width specified by <code>columns</code> (default 72).</li> <li><code>none</code>: Pandoc will not wrap lines at all.</li> <li><code>preserve</code>: Pandoc will attempt to preserve the wrapping from the source document. Where there are nonsemantic newlines in the source, there will be nonsemantic newlines in the output as well. <code>columns</code></li> </ul> <p>Specify length of lines in characters. This affects text wrapping in generated source code (see <code>wrap</code>). It also affects calculation of column widths for plain text tables.</p> <p>For <code>typst</code>, number of columns for body text.</p> <p><code>tab-stop</code></p> <p>Specify the number of spaces per tab (default is 4). Note that tabs within normal textual input are always converted to spaces. Tabs within code are also converted, however this can be disabled with <code>preserve-tabs: false</code>.</p> <p><code>preserve-tabs</code></p> <p>Preserve tabs within code instead of converting them to spaces. (By default, pandoc converts tabs to spaces before parsing its input.) Note that this will only affect tabs in literal code spans and code blocks. Tabs in regular text are always treated as spaces.</p> <p><code>eol</code></p> <p>Manually specify line endings:</p> <ul> <li><code>crlf</code>: Use Windows line endings</li> <li><code>lf</code>: Use macOS/Linux/UNIX line endings</li> <li><code>native</code> (default): Use line endings appropriate to the OS on which pandoc is being run).</li> </ul> <h3 id="website-options">Website Options</h3> <h4 id="website-options-1">Website Options</h4> <p>All available options for <code>website</code> projects are documented below. See Creating a Website for an in-depth guide to creating websites with Quarto.</p> <h5 id="project-2">Project</h5> <p>Options that define the type, render targets, and output of a project. Project options are specified under the <code>project</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: website output-dir: _site</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Project type (<code>default</code>, <code>website</code>, <code>book</code>, or <code>manuscript</code>)</p> <p><code>render</code></p> <p>Files to render (defaults to all files)</p> <p><code>execute-dir</code></p> <p>Control the working directory for computations.</p> <ul> <li><code>file</code>: Use the directory of the file that is currently executing.</li> <li><code>project</code>: Use the root directory of the project. <code>output-dir</code></li> </ul> <p>Output directory</p> <p><code>lib-dir</code></p> <p>HTML library (JS/CSS/etc.) directory</p> <p><code>resources</code></p> <p>Additional file resources to be copied to output directory</p> <p><code>brand</code></p> <p>Path to brand.yml or object with light and dark paths to brand.yml</p> <p><code>preview</code></p> <p>Options for <code>quarto preview</code> (see Preview)</p> <p><code>pre-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a pre-render step</p> <p><code>post-render</code></p> <p>Scripts to run as a post-render step</p> <h6 id="preview-9">Preview</h6> <p>Specify options that control the behavior of <code>quarto preview</code> within the <code>preview</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: website output-dir: _site preview: port: 4200 browser: false</code></pre> <p>Available <code>preview</code> options include:</p> <p><code>port</code></p> <p>Port to listen on (defaults to random value between 3000 and 8000)</p> <p><code>host</code></p> <p>Hostname to bind to (defaults to 127.0.0.1)</p> <p><code>serve</code></p> <p>Options for external preview server (see Serve)</p> <p><code>browser</code></p> <p>Open a web browser to view the preview (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>watch-inputs</code></p> <p>Re-render input files when they change (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>navigate</code></p> <p>Navigate the browser automatically when outputs are updated (defaults to true)</p> <p><code>timeout</code></p> <p>Time (in seconds) after which to exit if there are no active clients</p> <h6 id="serve-4">Serve</h6> <p>If you are creating a project extension for another publishing system that includes its own preview server (for example, Hugo or Docusaurus) then use the <code>preview: serve</code> options to customize the behavior of the preview server.</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml project: type: website preview: serve: cmd: "hugo serve --port {port} --bind {host} --navigateToChanged" env: HUGO_RELATIVEURLS: "true" ready: "Web Server is available at"</code></pre> <p><code>cmd</code></p> <p>Serve project preview using the specified command. Interpolate the <code>--port</code> into the command using <code>{port}</code>.</p> <p><code>args</code></p> <p>Additional command line arguments for preview command.</p> <p><code>env</code></p> <p>Environment variables to set for preview command.</p> <p><code>ready</code></p> <p>Regular expression for detecting when the server is ready.</p> <p>See the <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/hugo/_extension.yml">Hugo</a> and <a href="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/extensions/quarto/docusaurus/_extension.yml">Docusaurus</a> extension source code for example usages of <code>preview: serve</code>.</p> <h5 id="website-5">Website</h5> <p>Options that affect website output. Website options are specified under the <code>website</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: title: "My Website" image: opengraph.png page-navigation: true</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Website title</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>Website description</p> <p><code>favicon</code></p> <p>The path to the favicon for this website</p> <p><code>site-url</code></p> <p>Base URL for published website</p> <p><code>site-path</code></p> <p>Path to site (defaults to <code>/</code>). Not required if you specify <code>site-url</code>.</p> <p><code>repo-url</code></p> <p>Base URL for website source code repository</p> <p><code>repo-link-target</code></p> <p>The value of the target attribute for repo links</p> <p><code>repo-link-rel</code></p> <p>The value of the rel attribute for repo links</p> <p><code>repo-subdir</code></p> <p>Subdirectory of repository containing website</p> <p><code>repo-branch</code></p> <p>Branch of website source code (defaults to <code>main</code>)</p> <p><code>issue-url</code></p> <p>URL to use for the ‘report an issue’ repository action.</p> <p><code>repo-actions</code></p> <p>Links to source repository actions (<code>none</code> or one or more of <code>edit</code>, <code>source</code>, <code>issue</code>)</p> <p><code>reader-mode</code></p> <p>Displays a ‘reader-mode’ tool which allows users to hide the sidebar and table of contents when viewing a page.</p> <p><code>llms-txt</code></p> <p>Generate llms.txt and .llms.md files for LLM-friendly content consumption.</p> <p><code>google-analytics</code></p> <p>Enable Google Analytics for this website</p> <p><code>plausible-analytics</code></p> <p>Enable Plausible Analytics for this website by pasting the script snippet from your Plausible dashboard, or by providing a path to a file containing the snippet.</p> <p>Plausible is a privacy-friendly, GDPR-compliant web analytics service that does not use cookies and does not require cookie consent.</p> <p>Option 1: Inline snippet</p> <pre><code>website: plausible-analytics: | <script async src="[plausible.io](https://plausible.io/js/script.js)"></script></code></pre> <p>Option 2: File path</p> <pre><code>website: plausible-analytics: path: _plausible_snippet.html</code></pre> <p>To get your script snippet:</p> <ul> <li>Log into your Plausible account at <a href="https://plausible.io">plausible.io</a></li> <li>Go to your site settings</li> <li>Copy the JavaScript snippet provided</li> <li>Either paste it directly in your configuration or save it to a file For more information, see <a href="https://plausible.io/docs/plausible-script">plausible.io</a></li> </ul> <p><code>announcement</code></p> <p>An announcement displayed at the top of the page. (see Announcement)</p> <p><code>cookie-consent</code></p> <p>Quarto includes the ability to request cookie consent before enabling scripts that set cookies, using <a href="https://www.cookieconsent.com/">Cookie Consent</a>.</p> <p>The user’s cookie preferences will automatically control Google Analytics (if enabled) and can be used to control custom scripts you add as well. For more information see <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html#custom-scripts-and-cookie-consent">Custom Scripts and Cookie Consent</a>.</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Site search (<code>true</code> or <code>false</code> to enable/disable, or provide custom Search Options</p> <p><code>navbar</code></p> <p>Navbar options (see Navbar)</p> <p><code>sidebar</code></p> <p>Sidebar options (see Sidebar)</p> <p><code>body-header</code></p> <p>Markdown to insert at the beginning of each page’s body (below the title and author block).</p> <p><code>body-footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to insert below each page’s body.</p> <p><code>margin-header</code></p> <p>Markdown to place above margin content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>margin-footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to place below margin content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>page-navigation</code></p> <p>Provide next and previous article links in footer</p> <p><code>back-to-top-navigation</code></p> <p>Provide a ‘back to top’ navigation button</p> <p><code>bread-crumbs</code></p> <p>Whether to show navigation breadcrumbs for pages more than 1 level deep</p> <p><code>page-footer</code></p> <p>Page footer. Text content or page footer definition.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>Default site thumbnail image for <code>twitter</code> /<code>open-graph</code></p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>Default site thumbnail image alt text for <code>twitter</code> /<code>open-graph</code></p> <p><code>comments</code></p> <p><code>open-graph</code></p> <p>Generate Open Graph metadata (see Open Graph options)</p> <p><code>twitter-card</code></p> <p>Generate Twitter Card metadata (see Twitter Card options)</p> <p><code>other-links</code></p> <p>A list of other links to appear below the TOC.</p> <p><code>code-links</code></p> <p>A list of code links to appear with this document.</p> <p><code>drafts</code></p> <p>A list of input documents that should be treated as drafts. Read more at Website Drafts.</p> <p><code>draft-mode</code></p> <p>How to handle drafts that are encountered.</p> <p><code>visible</code> - the draft will visible and fully available <code>unlinked</code> - the draft will be rendered, but will not appear in navigation, search, or listings. <code>gone</code> - the draft will have no content and will not be linked to (default).</p> <h5 id="navbar-1">Navbar</h5> <p>Options that define the top navigation bar for a website For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: navbar: search: true</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The navbar title. Uses the project title if none is specified. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Specification of image that will be displayed to the left of the title.</p> <p><code>logo-alt</code></p> <p>Alternate text for the logo image.</p> <p><code>logo-href</code></p> <p>Target href from navbar logo / title. By default, the logo and title link to the root page of the site (/index.html).</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>The navbar’s background color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>The navbar’s foreground color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Include a search box in the navbar.</p> <p><code>pinned</code></p> <p>Always show the navbar (keeping it pinned).</p> <p><code>collapse</code></p> <p>Collapse the navbar into a menu when the display becomes narrow.</p> <p><code>collapse-below</code></p> <p>The responsive breakpoint below which the navbar will collapse into a menu (<code>sm</code>, <code>md</code>, <code>lg</code> (default), <code>xl</code>, <code>xxl</code>).</p> <p><code>left</code></p> <p>List of items for the left side of the navbar (see Nav Items)</p> <p><code>right</code></p> <p>List of items for the right side of the navbar (see Nav Items)</p> <p><code>toggle-position</code></p> <p>The position of the collapsed navbar toggle when in responsive mode</p> <p><code>tools-collapse</code></p> <p>Collapse tools into the navbar menu when the display becomes narrow.</p> <h5 id="nav-items-1">Nav Items</h5> <p>Nav items appear in the <code>left</code> or <code>right</code> key of <code>navbar</code> definitions, or <code>contents</code> key of <code>sidebar</code> definitions. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: navbar: right: - icon: github href: [github.com](https://github.com/) aria-label: GitHub</code></pre> <p><code>aria-label</code></p> <p>Accessible label for the item.</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Link to file contained with the project or external URL</p> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Name of bootstrap icon (e.g. <code>github</code>, <code>bluesky</code>, <code>share</code>) See <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com/">icons.getbootstrap.com</a> for a list of available icons</p> <p><code>menu</code></p> <p>Submenu of navigation items</p> <p><code>text</code></p> <p>Text to display for item (defaults to the document title if not provided). Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>rel</code></p> <p>Value for rel attribute. Multiple space-separated values are permitted. See <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel">developer.mozilla.org</a> for a details.</p> <p><code>target</code></p> <p>Value for target attribute. See <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#attr-target">developer.mozilla.org</a> for details.</p> <p>Note that the <code>icon</code> option is available for items in the Navbar, however items in the Sidebar do not support the <code>icon</code> option.</p> <h5 id="sidebar-1">Sidebar</h5> <p>Options that define the side navigation area for a website. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: sidebar: search: true</code></pre> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>The identifier for this sidebar.</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The sidebar title. Uses the project title if none is specified. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>logo</code></p> <p>Specification of image that will be displayed in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>logo-alt</code></p> <p>Alternate text for the logo image.</p> <p><code>logo-href</code></p> <p>Target href from navbar logo / title. By default, the logo and title link to the root page of the site (/index.html).</p> <p><code>search</code></p> <p>Include a search control in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>tools</code></p> <p>List of sidebar tools (see Sidebar Tools)</p> <p><code>contents</code></p> <p>List of navigation items to appear in the sidebar. Can also include <code>section</code> entries which in turn contain sub-lists of navigation items.</p> <p><code>style</code></p> <p>The style of sidebar (<code>docked</code> or <code>floating</code>).</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>The sidebar’s background color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>The sidebar’s foreground color (named or hex color).</p> <p><code>border</code></p> <p>Whether to show a border on the sidebar (defaults to true for ‘docked’ sidebars)</p> <p><code>alignment</code></p> <p>Alignment of the items within the sidebar (<code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>)</p> <p><code>collapse-level</code></p> <p>The depth at which the sidebar contents should be collapsed by default.</p> <p><code>pinned</code></p> <p>When collapsed, pin the collapsed sidebar to the top of the page.</p> <p><code>header</code></p> <p>Markdown to place above sidebar content (text or file path)</p> <p><code>footer</code></p> <p>Markdown to place below sidebar content (text or file path)</p> <h6 id="sidebar-tools-2">Sidebar Tools</h6> <p>Action buttons that appear on the sidebar. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: sidebar: tools: - icon: github href: [github.com](https://github.com/)</code></pre> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Name of bootstrap icon (e.g. <code>github</code>, <code>twitter</code>, <code>share</code>) See <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com/">icons.getbootstrap.com</a> for a list of available icons</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Link to file contained with the project or external URL</p> <p><code>menu</code></p> <p>Submenu of navigation items</p> <h5 id="announcement">Announcement</h5> <p>An announcement that appears at the top of the site. For example:</p> <pre><code>--- website: announcement: content: "**New** - this is an announcement" position: below-navbar ---</code></pre> <p><code>content</code></p> <p>The content of the announcement. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>dismissable</code></p> <p>Whether this announcement may be dismissed by the user.</p> <p><code>icon</code></p> <p>Name of bootstrap icon (e.g. <code>github</code>, <code>twitter</code>, <code>share</code>) for the announcement. See <a href="https://icons.getbootstrap.com/">icons.getbootstrap.com</a> for a list of available icons</p> <p><code>position</code></p> <p>The position of the announcement. One of <code>above-navbar</code> (default) or <code>below-navbar</code>.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>The type of announcement. One of <code>primary</code>, <code>secondary</code>, <code>success</code>, <code>danger</code>, <code>warning</code>, <code>info</code>, <code>light</code> or <code>dark</code>. Affects the appearance of the announcement.</p> <h5 id="footer-1">Footer</h5> <p>Website page footer definition. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: page-footer: center: - text: "About" href: about.qmd - text: "License" href: license.qmd - text: "Trademark" href: trademark.qmd</code></pre> <p><code>left</code></p> <p>Footer left content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>right</code></p> <p>Footer right content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>center</code></p> <p>Footer center content. Supports markdown formatting.</p> <p><code>border</code></p> <p>Footer border (<code>true</code>, <code>false</code>, or a border color)</p> <p><code>background</code></p> <p>Footer background color</p> <p><code>foreground</code></p> <p>Footer foreground color</p> <h5 id="search-1">Search</h5> <p>Search options are specified under the <code>search</code> key of <code>website</code>. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: search: location: navbar type: overlay</code></pre> <p><code>location</code></p> <p>Location for search widget (<code>navbar</code> or <code>sidebar</code>)</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Type of search UI (<code>overlay</code> or <code>textbox</code>)</p> <p><code>limit</code></p> <p>Number of matches to display (defaults to 20)</p> <p><code>collapse-after</code></p> <p>Matches after which to collapse additional results</p> <p><code>copy-button</code></p> <p>Provide button for copying search link</p> <p><code>merge-navbar-crumbs</code></p> <p>When false, do not merge navbar crumbs into the crumbs in <code>search.json</code>.</p> <p><code>keyboard-shortcut</code></p> <p>One or more keys that will act as a shortcut to launch search (single characters)</p> <p><code>show-item-context</code></p> <p>Whether to include search result parents when displaying items in search results (when possible).</p> <p><code>algolia</code></p> <p>Use an Algolia index for site search (see Algolia Options)</p> <h6 id="algolia-options-1">Algolia Options</h6> <p>You can use an Algolia index as the back end of website search. Specify Algolia options using the <code>algolia</code> sub-key of <code>search</code>, for example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: search: algolia: index-name: <my-index-name> application-id: <my-application-id> search-only-api-key: <my-search-only-api-key></code></pre> <p><code>index-name</code></p> <p>The name of the index to use when performing a search</p> <p><code>application-id</code></p> <p>The unique ID used by Algolia to identify your application</p> <p><code>search-only-api-key</code></p> <p>The Search-Only API key to use to connect to Algolia</p> <p><code>analytics-events</code></p> <p>Enable tracking of Algolia analytics events</p> <p><code>show-logo</code></p> <p>Enable the display of the Algolia logo in the search results footer.</p> <p><code>index-fields</code></p> <p>Fields to target for searches (see below for details)</p> <p><code>params</code></p> <p>Additional parameters to pass when executing a search</p> <p>The <code>index-fields</code> option provides sub-fields within the Algolia index to target for searches:</p> <p><code>href</code></p> <p>Field that contains the URL of index entries</p> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>Field that contains the title of index entries</p> <p><code>text</code></p> <p>Field that contains the text of index entries</p> <p><code>section</code></p> <p>Field that contains the section of index entries</p> <h5 id="social-1">Social</h5> <p>Social metadata is provided as a subkey of <code>website</code> options. You can specify <code>true</code> to generate social metadata using a set of default option, or specify one or more Twitter or Open Graph specific options as enumerated below. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: open-graph: true twitter-card: site: "@sitehandle"</code></pre> <h6 id="twitter-card-1">Twitter Card</h6> <p>Set Twitter options under the <code>twitter-card</code> key:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: twitter-card: site: "@sitehandle"</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The title of the page. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the title metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the title for this provider.</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>A short description of the content. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the description metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the description for this provider.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to a preview image for the content. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for the preview image. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image-alt</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>Image width (pixels)</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>Image height (pixels)</p> <p><code>card-style</code></p> <p>Card style (<code>summary</code> or <code>summary_large_image</code>).</p> <p>If this is not provided, the best style will automatically selected based upon other metadata. You can learn more about Twitter Card styles <a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/abouts-cards">here</a>.</p> <p><code>creator</code></p> <p><code>@username</code> of the content creator (must be a quoted string)</p> <p><code>site</code></p> <p><code>@username</code> of the website (must be a quoted string)</p> <h6 id="open-graph-1">Open Graph</h6> <p>Set Open Graph options under the <code>open-graph</code> key:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: open-graph: title: "Title for Open Graph"</code></pre> <p><code>title</code></p> <p>The title of the page. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the title metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the title for this provider.</p> <p><code>description</code></p> <p>A short description of the content. Note that by default Quarto will automatically use the description metadata from the page. Specify this field if you’d like to override the description for this provider.</p> <p><code>image</code></p> <p>The path to a preview image for the content. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-alt</code></p> <p>The alt text for the preview image. By default, Quarto will use the <code>image-alt</code> value from the format metadata. If you provide an image, you may also optionally provide an <code>image-width</code> and <code>image-height</code>.</p> <p><code>image-width</code></p> <p>Image width (pixels)</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>Image height (pixels)</p> <p><code>locale</code></p> <p>Locale of open graph metadata</p> <p><code>site-name</code></p> <p>Name that should be displayed for the overall site. If not explicitly provided in the <code>open-graph</code> metadata, Quarto will use the website or book <code>title</code> by default.</p> <h5 id="comments-1">Comments</h5> <p>You can add commenting to your website using either <a href="https://web.hypothes.is/">Hypothesis</a>, <a href="https://utteranc.es/">Utterances</a>, or <a href="https://giscus.app/">Giscus</a>.</p> <h6 id="hypothesis-1">Hypothesis</h6> <p>Enable and configure Hypothesis commenting via <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: hypothesis: theme: clean openSidebar: false</code></pre> <p><code>client-url</code></p> <p>Override the default hypothesis client url with a custom client url.</p> <p><code>openSidebar</code></p> <p>Controls whether the sidebar opens automatically on startup.</p> <p><code>showHighlights</code></p> <p>Controls whether the in-document highlights are shown by default (<code>always</code>, <code>whenSidebarOpen</code> or <code>never</code>)</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>Controls the overall look of the sidebar (<code>classic</code> or <code>clean</code>)</p> <p><code>enableExperimentalNewNoteButton</code></p> <p>Controls whether the experimental New Note button should be shown in the notes tab in the sidebar.</p> <p><code>usernameUrl</code></p> <p>Specify a URL to direct a user to, in a new tab. when they click on the annotation author link in the header of an annotation.</p> <p><code>services</code></p> <p>Array of service definitions</p> <p><code>branding</code></p> <p>Custom branding/colors to apply to UI</p> <p><code>externalContainerSelector</code></p> <p>A CSS selector specifying the containing element into which the sidebar iframe will be placed.</p> <p><code>focus</code></p> <p>User focused filter set for the available annotations on a page</p> <p><code>requestConfigFromFrame</code></p> <p>Specify a host iframe to request configuration from</p> <p><code>assetRoot</code></p> <p>The root URL from which assets are loaded.</p> <p><code>sidebarAppUrl</code></p> <p>The URL for the sidebar application which displays annotations.</p> <p>For additional documentation on the Hypothesis options enumerated above, see the <a href="https://h.readthedocs.io/projects/client/en/latest/publishers/config.html">Hypothesis Publisher Config</a> documentation.</p> <h6 id="utterances-1">Utterances</h6> <p>Enable and configure Utterances commenting via the <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: utterances: repo: quarto-dev/quarto-web</code></pre> <p><code>repo</code></p> <p>The Github repo that will be used to store comments.</p> <p><code>label</code></p> <p>The label that will be assigned to issues created by Utterances.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>The Github theme that should be used for Utterances (<code>github-light</code>, <code>github-dark</code>, <code>github-dark-orange</code>, <code>icy-dark</code>, <code>dark-blue</code>, <code>photon-dark</code>, <code>body-light</code>, or <code>gruvbox-dark</code>)</p> <p><code>issue-term</code></p> <p>How posts should be mapped to Github issues (<code>pathname</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>title</code> or <code>og:title</code>)</p> <h6 id="giscus-1">Giscus</h6> <p>Enable and configure usage of the <a href="https://giscus.app">Giscus app</a> via the <code>comments</code> key. For example:</p> <pre><code>_quarto.yml website: comments: giscus: repo: quarto-dev/quarto-web</code></pre> <p><code>repo</code></p> <p>The Github repo that will be used to store comments.</p> <p>In order to work correctly, the repo must be public, with the giscus app installed, and the discussions feature must be enabled.</p> <p><code>repo-id</code></p> <p>The Github repository identifier.</p> <p>You can quickly find this by using the configuration tool at <a href="https://giscus.app">giscus.app</a>. If this is not provided, Quarto will attempt to discover it at render time.</p> <p><code>category</code></p> <p>The discussion category where new discussions will be created. It is recommended to use a category with the Announcements type so that new discussions can only be created by maintainers and giscus.</p> <p><code>category-id</code></p> <p>The Github category identifier.</p> <p>You can quickly find this by using the configuration tool at <a href="https://giscus.app">giscus.app</a>. If this is not provided, Quarto will attempt to discover it at render time.</p> <p><code>mapping</code></p> <p>The mapping between the page and the embedded discussion.</p> <ul> <li><code>pathname</code>: The discussion title contains the page path</li> <li><code>url</code>: The discussion title contains the page url</li> <li><code>title</code>: The discussion title contains the page title</li> <li><code>og:title</code>: The discussion title contains the <code>og:title</code> metadata value</li> <li>any other string or number: Any other strings will be passed through verbatim and a discussion title containing that value will be used. Numbers will be treated as a discussion number and automatic discussion creation is not supported. <code>reactions-enabled</code></li> </ul> <p>Display reactions for the discussion’s main post before the comments.</p> <p><code>loading</code></p> <p>Specify <code>loading: lazy</code> to defer loading comments until the user scrolls near the comments container.</p> <p><code>input-position</code></p> <p>Place the comment input box above or below the comments.</p> <p><code>theme</code></p> <p>The giscus theme to use when displaying comments. Light and dark themes are supported. If a single theme is provided by name, it will be used as light and dark theme. To use different themes, use <code>light</code> and <code>dark</code> key:</p> <pre><code>website: comments: giscus: theme: light: light # giscus theme used for light website theme dark: dark_dimmed # giscus theme used for dark website theme</code></pre> <p><code>language</code></p> <p>The language that should be used when displaying the commenting interface.</p> <h5 id="listings-3">Listings</h5> <p>Listings enable you to automatically generate the contents of a page (or region of a page) from a list of Quarto documents or other custom data. You can enable listings on a page using the <code>listing</code> option in the document front matter. For example, setting <code>listing: default</code> will generate a listing of all documents in the directory (with the exception of the current document):</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Listing Example" listing: default ---</code></pre> <p>To customize the listing, specify additional options under the <code>listing</code> key:</p> <pre><code>--- title: "Listing Example" listing: contents: posts type: grid grid-columns: 2 ---</code></pre> <p><code>id</code></p> <p>The id of this listing. When the listing is rendered, it will place the contents into a <code>div</code> with this id. If no such <code>div</code> is defined on the page, a <code>div</code> with this id will be created and appended to the end of the page.</p> <p>If no <code>id</code> is provided for a listing, Quarto will synthesize one when rendering the page.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>The type of listing to create. Choose one of:</p> <ul> <li><code>default</code>: A blog style list of items</li> <li><code>table</code>: A table of items</li> <li><code>grid</code>: A grid of item cards</li> <li><code>custom</code>: A custom template, provided by the <code>template</code> field <code>contents</code></li> </ul> <p>The files or path globs of Quarto documents or YAML files that should be included in the listing.</p> <p><code>sort</code></p> <p>Sort items in the listing by these fields. The sort key is made up of a field name followed by a direction <code>asc</code> or <code>desc</code>.</p> <p>For example: <code>date asc</code></p> <p>Use <code>sort:false</code> to use the unsorted original order of items.</p> <p><code>max-items</code></p> <p>The maximum number of items to include in this listing.</p> <p><code>page-size</code></p> <p>The number of items to display on a page.</p> <p><code>sort-ui</code></p> <p>Shows or hides the sorting control for the listing. To control the fields that will be displayed in the sorting control, provide a list of field names.</p> <p><code>filter-ui</code></p> <p>Shows or hides the filtering control for the listing. To control the fields that will be used to filter the listing, provide a list of field names. By default all fields of the listing will be used when filtering.</p> <p><code>categories</code></p> <p>Display item categories from this listing in the margin of the page.</p> <ul> <li><code>numbered</code>: Category list with number of items</li> <li><code>unnumbered</code>: Category list</li> <li><code>cloud</code>: Word cloud style categories <code>feed</code></li> </ul> <p>Create an RSS feed for this page using the items in this listing (see Feed).</p> <p><code>date-format</code></p> <p>The date format to use when displaying dates (e.g. d-M-yyy). Learn more about supported date formatting values <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/reference/dates.html">here</a>.</p> <p><code>max-description-length</code></p> <p>The maximum length (in characters) of the description displayed in the listing. Defaults to 175.</p> <p><code>image-placeholder</code></p> <p>The default image to use if an item in the listing doesn’t have an image.</p> <p><code>image-lazy-loading</code></p> <p>If false, images in the listing will be loaded immediately. If true, images will be loaded as they come into view.</p> <p><code>image-align</code></p> <p>In <code>default</code> type listings, whether to place the image on the right or left side of the post content (<code>left</code> or <code>right</code>).</p> <p><code>image-height</code></p> <p>The height of the image being displayed (a CSS height string).</p> <p>The width is automatically determined and the image will fill the rectangle without scaling (cropped to fill).</p> <p><code>grid-columns</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, the number of columns in the grid display. Defaults to 3.</p> <p><code>grid-item-border</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, whether to display a border around the item card. Defaults to <code>true</code>.</p> <p><code>grid-item-align</code></p> <p>In grid type listings, the alignment of the content within the card (<code>left</code> (default), <code>right</code>, or <code>center</code>).</p> <p><code>table-striped</code></p> <p>In table type listings, display the table rows with alternating background colors. Defaults to <code>false</code>.</p> <p><code>table-hover</code></p> <p>In table type listings, highlight rows of the table when the user hovers the mouse over them. Defaults to false.</p> <p><code>template</code></p> <p>The path to a custom listing template.</p> <p><code>template-params</code></p> <p>Parameters that are passed to the custom template.</p> <p><code>fields</code></p> <p>The list of fields to include in this listing.</p> <p><code>field-display-names</code></p> <p>A mapping that provides display names for specific fields. For example, to display the title column as ‘Report’ in a table listing you would write:</p> <pre><code>listing: field-display-names: title: "Report"</code></pre> <p><code>field-types</code></p> <p>Provides the date type for the field of a listing item. Unknown fields are treated as strings unless a type is provided. Valid types are <code>date</code>, <code>number</code>.</p> <p><code>field-links</code></p> <p>The list of fields to display as hyperlinks to the source document when the listing type is a table. Defaults to 20.</p> <p><code>type</code></p> <p>Whether to include full or partial content in the feed.</p> <ul> <li><code>full</code> (default): Include the complete content of the document in the feed.</li> <li><code>partial</code>: Include only the first paragraph of the document in the feed.</li> <li><code>metadata</code>: Use only the title, description, and other document metadata in the feed. <code>title</code></li> </ul> <p>The title for this feed.
